rules.what_you_get: Three layers of cover. Years 1-2: everything on the fridge, parts and labour, free. Years 1-5: the compressor, condenser, evaporator, drier and connecting pipes, parts and labour, free. Years 6-12: those same cooling parts still free, but you pay the repair person's time.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Sub-Zero and ask for the Factory Certified Service company nearest you. Use their approved service company, because if you use an outside repairer Sub-Zero will only send you the part and will not pay you back for parts you bought elsewhere. Note that fan motors are not part of the cooling system and are not covered by the 12-year rule.
rules.script_hint: My Sub-Zero was installed less than 12 years ago and the sealed system has failed. That's covered for 12 years on parts. Please send Factory Certified Service and supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Bosch dishwasher: control board and racks covered to year 5
rules.window_note: Years 2 through 5 after you bought it. Year 1 is full cover including labour, so this rule matters most once that first year has run out.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement circuit board or dish rack. Bosch covers the electronics (the microprocessor or printed circuit board) and the racks for parts right through to the end of year 5. You pay the repair person's time.
rules.how_to_claim: A dead control panel, buttons that do nothing, or a machine that will not start is usually the circuit board. Rusted or collapsing racks count too, though the small clips and tines on the racks are not included. Call Bosch with your model and serial number.
rules.script_hint: My Bosch dishwasher's control board has failed and the machine is under 5 years old. Bosch covers the electronics for parts from year 2 through year 5, so I'd like the part supplied under warranty.

rules.title: Bosch vacuum: register it and the motor is covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase, but only if you registered the vacuum with Bosch. The vacuum itself is covered for 2 years or 300 hours of use, whichever comes first.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement motor for 10 years. This is the single most valuable part in a vacuum, and it only applies if you registered the machine, so it is worth registering today even if nothing is wrong yet.
rules.how_to_claim: First check whether you ever registered it. If not, register it now so future you is covered. If the motor has already died and you did register, call Bosch's vacuum and espresso line rather than the main appliance line.
rules.script_hint: My registered Bosch vacuum's motor has failed. Registered Bosch vacuums have a 10-year parts warranty on the motor, so I'd like a replacement motor supplied under that warranty.

rules.title: Bosch built-in fridge: extra cover most owners never hear about
rules.window_note: Year 1 is everything, parts and labour. Year 2 is every part, free. Years 3 to 5 cover the electronics. Rust-through on the stainless door has no time limit at all.
rules.what_you_get: Free parts for the whole fridge right through year 2, free circuit boards through year 5, and a free stainless steel door for life if it rusts through. This only applies to built-in models, not freestanding ones.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether yours is a built-in model (it slots into the cabinetry and takes a cabinet front panel). Call Bosch's large appliance line with your model and serial number and name which of these tiers you are claiming under.
rules.script_hint: I have a Bosch built-in refrigerator that's under 2 years old. Built-in models get parts cover for the entire appliance through the second year, so please supply this part under warranty.

rules.title: Speed Queen TC5 washer: the gearbox is covered for 15 years
rules.window_note: Fifteen years from installation on the transmission of TC5 washers. On TC5s with serial numbers from 2102000001 on, the whole washer gets 5 years of parts and labour, then years 6 to 15 are parts only. Older TC5s get 3 years of parts and labour, then years 4 to 15 are parts only. In the parts-only years you pay the repair person's time but not the part.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement transmission (the gearbox that turns the drum) for fifteen years. This is one of the longest single-part warranties on any home appliance and it is almost never mentioned at the point of sale.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether your model number starts TC5. If the drum will not spin or agitate, or the machine makes a grinding noise under load, ask for the transmission to be checked specifically.
rules.script_hint: My Speed Queen TC5 washer's transmission has failed. The transmission assembly carries a 15-year warranty on that model, so please supply the part under warranty.
rules.source_quote: Fifteen (15) year limited warranty on the transmission assembly. Year 6 through 15 parts only limited warranty.

rules.title: Speed Queen: the drum and tub are covered for life against rust
rules.window_note: No time limit. This one runs for as long as you own the machine. Many models also get a separate 5-year cover on the cabinet against rusting from the inside out.
rules.what_you_get: A free stainless steel wash tub, or a free steel dryer drum, if it rusts or corrodes, with no deadline. Speed Queen covers the stainless tub and outer tub on washers, and the steel drum on dryers, for life.
rules.how_to_claim: Look for rust streaks on your laundry, rough or flaking metal inside the drum, or brown water. Photograph it. Note that surface rust from something you left in the machine, and rust caused by chemicals, are excluded, so describe it as rust coming from the metal itself.
rules.script_hint: The stainless steel tub in my Speed Queen washer is corroding. Speed Queen gives a lifetime warranty on the stainless tub against rust or corrosion, so I'd like the part replaced under that warranty.
rules.source_quote: Lifetime limited warranty on the stainless steel tub and outer tub against rust or corrosion.

rules.title: Maytag: 10 years of free parts on almost everything they make
rules.window_note: Ten years from purchase, on any major Maytag kitchen or laundry appliance made after 2017. Year 1 includes labour; years 2 to 10 are the part only.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement for the expensive core part of your appliance. On washers and dryers that's the drive motor, wash basket and dryer drum. On dishwashers it's the stainless tub, nylon racks and chopper. On fridges it's the compressor. On microwaves it's the magnetron and cavity. On ranges and ovens it's the burners, elements, ceramic top, grates and cavity.
rules.how_to_claim: Check the appliance was made after 2017 (the serial number sticker gives the build date). Work out which of the listed parts has failed, then call Maytag or book service and name that part. Two specific laundry pairs also get labour covered for the first 5 years, so ask whether yours is one of them.
rules.script_hint: My Maytag was made after 2017 and the drive motor has failed. That part is covered by Maytag's 10-year limited parts warranty, so I'd like the part supplied free.

rules.title: Dyson corded vacuum: 5 years, parts and labour
rules.window_note: Five years from purchase or delivery, whichever is later. If you have lost your receipt, Dyson starts the clock 90 days after the machine was made, so you may still have time.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair covering both parts and labour for five years on corded vacuums (and Dyson lights and hand dryers). It only covers machines bought from Dyson or a Dyson authorized seller in the US, so keep your receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Dyson helpline with your model name, serial number and where and when you bought it. Note that blockages, worn filters, worn brush bars and a battery simply getting older are not covered, so describe an actual fault rather than a maintenance issue.
rules.script_hint: My Dyson corded vacuum has developed a fault. Corded Dyson vacuums carry a 5-year parts and labour warranty and mine is inside that window, so I'd like it repaired at no cost.
rules.source_quote: This warranty provides, at no cost to you, all labor and parts necessary to ensure your machine is in proper operating condition during the warranty period.

rules.title: Roomba: the battery is inside the 1-year warranty
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, or from delivery if that was later. If the delivery date can't be checked, the clock starts two weeks after purchase.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement robot. The robot's battery counts as part of the robot, so a battery that has actually failed is covered, not just the robot body.
rules.how_to_claim: Have your serial number and your receipt from an approved seller ready before you contact iRobot. You do not need to have registered the robot: iRobot states in writing that not registering does not reduce your rights. Note that a battery just getting weaker with age counts as wear and is not covered, and robots bought from unapproved sellers are not covered at all.
rules.script_hint: My Roomba is under a year old and has failed. iRobot's warranty covers the robot including the battery for one year, so I'd like it repaired or replaced.
rules.source_quote: this Product (including the robot battery, if applicable, and collectively referred to as the “Product”) for the period of one (1) year from the date of purchase

rules.title: Older Miele vacuum: the motor and body may be covered for 7 years
rules.window_note: Seven years from purchase, but only if your vacuum came with Miele's older US warranty. The 2014 version covers the motor and body on models starting S2, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S160 or S190 (10 years on the S8990), while everything else on those vacuums is only covered for 1 year. Miele's US vacuum warranty dated 1 August 2023 has no separate motor or body cover: newer vacuums get a flat 1 to 3 years, or 5 years on most HomeCare models. Check the warranty page in your own manual to see which one you have.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, parts and labour, if the suction motor or the power head motor dies, or if the plastic body cracks or breaks. On the S8990 model these go to 10 years instead of 7.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your model number on the underside or back of the vacuum. If it starts with one of those S codes and the motor has gone, contact Miele or an approved Miele dealer. This is a US-only warranty and does not apply to vacuums used for work.
rules.script_hint: My Miele vacuum's motor has failed. The warranty that came with my vacuum covers the vacuum and power head motors for 7 years from purchase, separately from the 1-year warranty on the rest of the machine, and I am still inside that time.
rules.source_quote: Vacuum cleaner and power head motors will be covered for seven (7) years from the date of purchase on the S2xxx, S4xxx, S5xxx, S6xxx, S7xxx, S8xxx, S160 and S190 product series.

rules.title: Cuisinart: 3 years, and no receipt needed to try
rules.window_note: Three years from purchase on Cuisinart kitchen appliances, which is three times the usual one year. If you cannot find your receipt, Cuisinart uses the date the item was made instead, so a missing receipt does not end the conversation.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or, if it can't be fixed, a free replacement. Cuisinart calls this its hassle-free replacement warranty and will send you a return shipping label so you are not out of pocket for postage. Coffee grinders are 18 months instead of 3 years, and outdoor grills vary.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the product inquiry form on Cuisinart's site or call their consumer service line to get a free return shipping label. You must have bought it from Cuisinart or an approved seller.
rules.script_hint: My Cuisinart has failed and it's under three years old. Cuisinart's standard warranty is three years with hassle-free replacement, so please send me a return shipping label.

rules.title: Cuisinart pots and pans: covered for your lifetime
rules.window_note: For as long as the person who bought it is alive. There is genuinely no expiry date on this one.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, a free identical or equivalent replacement, or, if they cannot do either, your money back minus an amount for the use you've had. This covers Cuisinart cookware, but not the electrical appliances, which get 3 years instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Email through the product inquiry form or call to get a free return shipping label. Normal wear and tear is not covered, so describe an actual defect, like a handle that snapped off or a pan base that warped or separated. Without a receipt they use the date it was made.
rules.script_hint: My Cuisinart cookware has a manufacturing defect. Cuisinart cookware carries a lifetime warranty for the original purchaser, so I'd like it repaired or replaced and a return shipping label sent.
rules.source_quote: if Cuisinart is unable to repair or replace the Product, refund the purchase price, less the amount directly attributable to the consumer’s prior usage of the Product.

rules.title: KitchenAid tools and gadgets: free for a year, covered for life after
rules.window_note: Year 1 is a straight swap for a new one. Year 2 onwards runs for the life of the product with no end date.
rules.what_you_get: In the first year, a free replacement, no questions about repairing it. From year two onwards, for the life of the product, anything found to be defective gets repaired free or replaced with the same item or something of equal or better value. This covers the KitchenAid hand tools and gadgets range, not the stand mixers or the big appliances.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the KitchenAid customer satisfaction line to start the claim, or post the item to their consumer service department in Trenton, New Jersey. You pay the postage to send it in. Normal use and care is the test, so describe a real defect rather than damage from dropping it.
rules.script_hint: My KitchenAid tool has a defect in materials or workmanship. KitchenAid tools and gadgets carry a lifetime limited warranty from year two onward, so I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: Frigidaire dishwasher: tub covered for life, racks to year 5
rules.window_note: The stainless tub and door liner have no expiry date. The racks and the electronic control module are covered in years 2 through 5. The machine as a whole is 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free stainless tub or door liner for as long as you own the dishwasher, and a free set of racks or a free control board up to the end of year 5. The control board is the part that usually kills a dishwasher, so that 5-year cover is worth checking before you replace the machine.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Frigidaire with your model and serial number, on a sticker on the edge of the door. Say which part has failed and which tier of the warranty you are claiming under. These extra tiers are parts only, so budget for the repair person's time.
rules.script_hint: My Frigidaire dishwasher's electronic control module has failed and the machine is under five years old. Frigidaire covers the control module for parts in years two through five, so please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Frigidaire stacked laundry: tub for life, motor for 10 years
rules.window_note: The inner wash tub has no time limit. The motor runs to 10 years. The unit as a whole is covered for 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: A free inner wash tub with no deadline, and a free motor for ten years, on Frigidaire laundry centers (the stacked washer-and-dryer-in-one units). Standalone Frigidaire washers and dryers only get the 1 year, so this extra cover is specific to the stacked units and easy to miss.
rules.how_to_claim: Confirm you have a laundry center rather than a separate washer and dryer. Call Frigidaire with the model and serial number and name the motor or the inner wash tub specifically. These are parts-only tiers, so you cover the labour.
rules.script_hint: I have a Frigidaire laundry center and the motor has failed. Laundry centers carry a 10-year parts warranty on the motor, so please supply the part under warranty.

rules.title: Frigidaire garbage disposal: up to 12 years, plus rust cover for life
rules.window_note: How long depends on the motor size: 12 years for a 1.25 horsepower unit, 10 years for 0.75 horsepower, and 5 or 6 years for a 0.5 horsepower unit. Rusting through has no time limit at all.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement disposal unit for anything from 5 to 12 years depending on which one you bought, plus lifetime cover if it corrodes. People replace jammed or leaking disposals without ever checking, because nobody expects a warranty this long on a part hidden under the sink.
rules.how_to_claim: Look under the sink for the label on the disposal body giving the model and horsepower rating, then match that to the length above. Call Frigidaire and quote the horsepower, since that is what sets your window.
rules.script_hint: My Frigidaire garbage disposal has failed. It's a three-quarter horsepower unit, which carries a 10-year warranty, and mine is inside that window. I'd like a replacement under warranty.

rules.title: "Warranty void if this sticker is broken" is generally not allowed
rules.window_note: Works any time your written warranty is still running.
rules.what_you_get: Opening the case or breaking a seal to do normal maintenance or a repair does not kill your warranty. You still get the repair or replacement you were promised. In July 2024 the FTC sent warning letters to PC and parts makers over exactly these stickers.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask for the warranty repair as normal. If they refuse because a seal was broken, tell them the sticker doesn't cancel your rights and ask them to show what damage you actually caused. If they still refuse, report them to the FTC.
rules.script_hint: The FTC has warned companies that "warranty void if removed" stickers break the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act. Breaking that seal doesn't cancel my warranty. Please book the repair.

rules.title: If it came with any written warranty, the built-in "it should work" promise can't be taken away
rules.window_note: Runs alongside the written warranty. In most states you have about 4 years from the purchase date to make the claim. If the written one is a 'limited' warranty the company may cap this second one to the same length; if it is a 'full' warranty they cannot cap it at all. Then escalate to your state attorney general's consumer protection office.
rules.what_you_get: On top of whatever the paper warranty says, you also have the law's built-in promise that the product actually does what it's supposed to do. If a company gives you a written warranty, it is not allowed to cancel that built-in promise. Same if it sold you a service contract.
rules.how_to_claim: If the written warranty just ran out, or doesn't cover your particular problem, write to the seller and the maker and say you are also claiming the implied warranty of merchantability, which they were never allowed to cancel.
rules.script_hint: You gave a written warranty on this product, so under federal law you can't disclaim the implied warranty that it works. It failed far too soon for a product like this. I'd like it repaired or my money back.

rules.title: A limited warranty can only shorten the built-in promise to its own length, never shorter
rules.window_note: Lasts at least as long as the written warranty. Some states ignore these cut-offs entirely and give you longer.
rules.what_you_get: If your limited warranty runs 2 years, the built-in "it works" promise runs at least 2 years too. A company with a 1-year warranty cannot shrink your built-in promise down to 90 days. And a warranty labelled "Full" can't shorten it at all.
rules.how_to_claim: If they tell you the implied warranty expired earlier than the written warranty, point out that the law only lets them match it to their own warranty length, not cut it shorter.
rules.script_hint: Your written warranty runs [X] years, so the implied warranty runs at least that long as well. Federal law doesn't let you cut it shorter than your own warranty period.

rules.title: You usually have about 4 years from the purchase date to make a warranty claim stick
rules.window_note: About 4 years from the purchase date in most states. This is your deadline to act. It does NOT mean the product has to last 4 years.
rules.what_you_get: Time. Even after the printed warranty has run out, the law's built-in promise can usually still be enforced for roughly 4 years from when you bought it, as long as the fault was already there when it was sold to you.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your receipt and check the date. If it's under about 4 years, write to the seller and the maker and say the fault was built in from the start, so you're still inside the time limit.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on [date], which is inside the time limit for a warranty claim in this state. The fault was there from the start, so please repair, replace or refund it.

rules.title: Massachusetts: "sold as is" doesn't work, and you can ask a court for up to triple your money
rules.window_note: Send the demand letter as soon as you can. You have to wait 30 days after sending it before you can file in court.
rules.what_you_get: In Massachusetts, any wording a seller or maker uses to cancel the built-in promise that a product works is simply void. "As is" and "no warranty" don't count, and they can't be waived by agreement. On top of that, if you send a proper 30-day demand letter and they ignore it or lowball you on purpose, a court can award you two to three times your loss plus your lawyer's fees.
rules.how_to_claim: Write a letter (keep a copy) saying who you are, exactly what went wrong, what it cost you, and what you want them to do. Mail it to the company. Wait 30 days. If they don't make a fair offer, you can file in court and ask for multiplied damages and your legal costs.
rules.script_hint: This is a 30-day demand letter under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 93A. Any "as is" or disclaimer wording is void here under Chapter 106 Section 2-316A. Please repair or refund within 30 days.

rules.title: Maryland: "as is" doesn't hold up, and the maker has to fix things quickly
rules.window_note: Applies to consumer goods and services. Older cars over 6 model years old with more than 60,000 miles are treated differently.
rules.what_you_get: In Maryland, wording a seller uses to cancel or cut back the built-in promise that a product works is unenforceable. And a maker can only limit what you get under its own written warranty if it actually gives you a reasonable and quick way to get the warranty work done. If it doesn't, those limits don't hold either.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller that Maryland law makes "as is" and disclaimer wording unenforceable on consumer goods, and ask for a repair, replacement or refund. If the maker is dragging its feet, point out that its warranty limits only count if it gives you a fast, reasonable way to get the repair.
rules.script_hint: Maryland Commercial Law 2-316.1 makes "as is" and warranty disclaimers unenforceable on consumer goods. And if your warranty limits don't come with a reasonable and expeditious way to get this fixed, those limits don't hold either.

rules.title: California: makers must keep parts and repair manuals available for up to 7 years
rules.window_note: Counted from when the maker last built your model, not from when you bought it. If your model is still being made, the clock has not even started, but an old model may already be past it. The rules started 1 July 2024 and cover products first made and first sold or used in California on or after 1 July 2021. Game consoles and alarm and fire systems are left out. If the maker refuses, get the refusal in writing, because the refusal itself is what you complain about.
rules.what_you_get: Spare parts, tools and the service manuals needed to fix your electronics or appliance, available to you and to independent repair shops on fair terms and at the same cost the maker charges its own approved shops. Documents must be free apart from real printing and postage costs. 7 years for anything with a wholesale price of $100 or more, 3 years for $50 to $99.99.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker's support line for the part and the service manual, or ask a local independent repair shop to order them for you. If the maker refuses, say California's Right to Repair Act requires it and that a city attorney, district attorney or the Attorney General can enforce it.
rules.script_hint: California's Right to Repair Act requires you to supply parts, tools and repair documents on fair and reasonable terms for 7 years after this model was last made. Please send me the part and the service manual.
rules.source_quote: for at least seven years after the last date a product model or type was manufactured, regardless of whether the seven-year period exceeds the warranty period for the product.

rules.title: New York: makers must hand over parts, tools and repair manuals
rules.window_note: In force since 28 December 2023. Covers gear first made, and first sold or used in New York, on or after 1 July 2023. Home appliances are left out, including fridges, ovens, microwaves, heating and cooling units and home alarm systems, and so are cars, medical devices, farm and off-road gear, power tools, yard and garden equipment, e-bikes and industrial electrical gear. No deadline tied to when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: The parts, tools and repair information you or a local shop need to fix your device. The manual and the tools have to be free, apart from the real cost of posting a physical copy, and parts have to be offered at a reasonable cost and on reasonable terms. A maker cannot use its contracts with its own approved shops to get out of this.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker's support for the part and the repair manual, in writing. If they refuse, file a complaint with the New York Attorney General, who enforces this section.
rules.script_hint: New York's Digital Fair Repair Act, General Business Law 399-nn, says you have to make the parts, tools and documentation available to owners and independent shops on fair and reasonable terms. Please send them.

rules.title: Oregon: makers can't use software to block a working replacement part
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2025. Covers phones first made and sold from 1 July 2021, and other consumer electronics from 1 July 2015. Important catch: the Attorney General can only take companies to court over violations happening on or after 1 July 2027, so before then this is a strong argument rather than an instant penalty. Cars, medical gear, heating and cooling, solar, game consoles, power tools and electric toothbrushes are excluded. The one pairing use still allowed is limiting a battery after it overheats. Check the date your device was made or first sold, then say that to the maker in writing.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, tools and manuals on fair terms, at the best price the maker gives its own approved shops. Plus, for gear first made and sold after 1 January 2025, the maker cannot use software "parts pairing" to stop a good replacement part working, to slow your device down, or to nag you with warnings about unidentified parts that you can't dismiss.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker, or get your repair shop to ask, for the part and for the software or tool needed to make that part work. If a fitted part is being blocked, throttled or flagged, say so in writing and complain to the Oregon Department of Justice.
rules.script_hint: Oregon's right to repair law bans using parts pairing to block or throttle a working replacement part, or to show warnings I can't dismiss. Please give me the tool to pair this part.
rules.source_quote: Prohibit parts pairing for the purpose of reducing the functionality of a battery if a thermal event occurs.

rules.title: Colorado: parts, tools and manuals for your electronics, and no software lock-outs
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2026, covering digital electronics first made and sold or used in Colorado on or after 1 July 2021. The parts-pairing ban covers gear first made and sold in Colorado after 1 January 2026. Cars, boats, aviation, most medical devices, power tools, game consoles and some monitored alarm and fire systems are excluded.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, tools and repair documentation from the maker, on request. For newer gear the maker also can't use software parts pairing to block a replacement part, reduce how well the device works, or show misleading warnings about unidentified parts. Refusing is a deceptive trade practice under Colorado law.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker in writing for the part, tool or manual. If they refuse, tell them that failing to comply is a deceptive trade practice under Colorado's right-to-repair statutes, and report it to the Colorado Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Colorado's Consumer Right to Repair law requires you to give me the parts, tools and documentation to fix this, and failing to do so is a deceptive trade practice. Please supply them.
rules.source_quote: WITH RESPECT TO DIGITAL ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT, THIS PART 15 DOES NOT APPLY TO: ... (h) PORTABLE GENERATORS, ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS, FUEL CELL POWER SYSTEMS, OR POWER TOOLS;

rules.title: Colorado: powered wheelchair makers must let you or a local shop repair it
rules.window_note: In force since 1 January 2023. No time limit tied to when you got the chair.
rules.what_you_get: Parts, embedded software, firmware, tools and repair manuals for your powered wheelchair, given to you or to an independent repair shop so you don't have to wait on the manufacturer. Any contract wording signed from 2023 onwards that tries to take this away is void and unenforceable.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the manufacturer in writing for the specific part, software, tool or manual you or your repair shop needs. If they refuse, tell them it's a deceptive trade practice under Colorado law and report it to the Colorado Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Colorado law requires powered wheelchair makers to give owners and independent repairers the parts, software, tools and manuals needed for repairs, and refusing is a deceptive trade practice. Please send them.

rules.title: Paid by credit card? You can refuse to pay for a faulty item
rules.window_note: Only works while you still owe money on that purchase, so act before you've paid the card off. You must genuinely try to sort it out with the shop first. Usually the item must have cost more than $50 and been bought in your state or within 100 miles of your home, but those two limits drop away if the card is the shop's own card, the shop and card company are connected, or the card company mailed you the offer.
rules.what_you_get: You can stop paying your card company for a faulty item, up to the amount still owed on that purchase plus the interest charged on it. This works even when the shop refuses to help, because you're raising the same complaint against the card company that you have against the shop.
rules.how_to_claim: First genuinely try to get the shop to repair, replace or refund it, and keep a record of what you asked and what they said. Then write to your card company, explain the item is faulty, say you are asserting your claims and defences, and ask them to hold that amount off your bill.
rules.script_hint: I'm asserting my claims and defences under the Fair Credit Billing Act. The item is faulty, I made a good faith attempt to resolve it with the merchant, and I'm withholding payment on that amount.
rules.source_quote: The cardholder may withhold payment up to the amount of credit outstanding for the property or services that gave rise to the dispute and any finance or other charges imposed on that amount.

rules.title: Quebec: your stuff has to last a reasonable time
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. How long is long enough depends on the price you paid, the contract and how you used it. Quebec's consumer office says an $850 TV can't be expected to last as long as a similar $1,500 one. It covers used items bought from a business too, taking their age and wear into account. It still applies if the seller says the item comes with no warranty.
rules.what_you_get: The item must work for what it is normally used for, and keep working in normal use for a reasonable time. If it doesn't, you can ask for a free repair, a swap or your money back. This legal warranty is automatic and free.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the store in writing that the item stopped working too soon and that you are using the legal warranty. You can deal with the store, the manufacturer or both, and the store can't make you deal with the manufacturer. Ask for a free repair, a swap or a refund. Quebec's consumer office says the store or maker can choose which of these to offer. Keep your receipt. If they refuse, send a formal notice. As a last step you can go to small claims court (for $15,000 or less). There you can ask the court to make them fix it, to let you have it fixed at their cost, to lower what you pay or to cancel the sale, and to pay damages. Quebec's consumer office (OPC) can explain your rights and options, but you have to deal with the store yourself.
rules.script_hint: Sections 37 and 38 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act say goods must be fit for their normal use and last a reasonable time in normal use. This stopped working too soon, so I'm asking you to repair, replace or refund it at no cost to me.
rules.source_quote: Thus, a TV set worth $850 cannot be expected to last as long as another TV set with similar characteristics, but that is worth $1,500.

rules.title: Quebec: repairs on phones, computers, TVs, fridges and washers are guaranteed for 3 months
rules.window_note: This clock does not start when you bought the item. The 3 months start on the day the repaired item is given back to you. So a repair done years after you bought it still gets its own 3 months.
rules.what_you_get: In Quebec, a repair is guaranteed for 3 months, parts and labour included. If the problem comes back in that time, the person who did the repair has to fix it again for free. The law gives the list of items this covers: a stove, a fridge, a freezer, a dishwasher, a microwave oven, a washer, a dryer, an audio device, an audio-video device such as a TV, a computer or tablet and the equipment you plug into it like a monitor or printer, a cell phone, an air conditioner, a dehumidifier and a heat pump. The law does not name headphones, speakers or game consoles one by one, so ask the repair shop whether your item counts as an audio device or an audio-video device. Other small appliances, like a kettle, a toaster or a coffee maker, are not on the list, and neither is a vacuum, a furnace or a water heater. The repair must have cost more than $50 in total, counting parts, labour and shipping. The guarantee does not cover damage from misusing the item after the repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the person or shop that did the repair, with your repair bill. Say the problem came back within the 3-month repair guarantee in Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. You should not be charged for parts or labour. If they refuse, you can call Quebec's consumer protection office, the Office de la protection du consommateur.
rules.script_hint: You repaired this less than three months ago and the problem is back. Under section 186 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act, the repair is guaranteed for three months, parts and labour included, so please fix it again at no charge.
rules.source_quote: Every repair is guaranteed for three months.

rules.title: New Brunswick: you can go after the maker, not just the shop
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. How long a product should last is judged from what it is, whether it was new or used, and how you actually used and looked after it.
rules.what_you_get: New Brunswick law says products must be decent quality and last a reasonable time, sellers cannot sign those promises away, and you can claim against a company you never bought from directly — including the manufacturer.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the shop and to the manufacturer at the same time. Say New Brunswick's Consumer Product Warranty and Liability Act gives you a durability warranty that cannot be excluded, and that section 23 lets you claim even without a contract with them. Ask the shop to fix it or give you your money back, and ask the maker to pay for your loss, like the cost of the repair.
rules.script_hint: Under New Brunswick's Consumer Product Warranty and Liability Act this had to be durable for a reasonable time, and I don't need a contract with you to make that claim.
rules.source_quote: any person who is not a party to the contract but who suffers a consumer loss because of the breach may recover damages against the seller for the loss

rules.title: Ontario: small print can't cancel the law's quality promises
rules.window_note: The Sale of Goods Act does not give these promises a set number of months. Section 9 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2002 applies if you or the business was in Ontario when the deal took place. In Ontario you generally have two years from the day you found the problem, or should have found it, to start a court case.
rules.what_you_get: Ontario's Sale of Goods Act builds promises into a sale. If you bought the goods by description, so by what they were said to be, they have to match that description. If you bought them by description from a business that deals in that kind of goods, they also have to be of merchantable (sellable) quality. But if you examined the goods first, faults that check should have shown don't count. When you deal with a business for personal, family or household use, section 9 of Ontario's Consumer Protection Act, 2002 applies these promises to things you lease or trade for as well. It also makes any term or statement, in your contract or not, that tries to cancel or change them void, so it has no effect. If such a term is in your contract, it is cut out and can't be used as proof that the promises were not meant to apply.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the seller and say what is wrong with the item. Say you bought it by description from a business that sells that kind of thing, so the Sale of Goods Act's implied conditions apply, and that section 9 of Ontario's Consumer Protection Act, 2002 makes any term that cancels or changes them void. Ask them to put it right. If they refuse, you can sue the business in Small Claims Court for $50,000 or less, and you don't need a lawyer to do it.
rules.script_hint: I bought this by description from a business that sells that kind of thing, so Ontario's Sale of Goods Act says it had to be of merchantable quality. I bought it for personal use, so section 9 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2002 makes any term that cancels or changes that promise void, and I'm asking you to put it right.
rules.source_quote: Any term or acknowledgement, whether part of the consumer agreement or not, that purports to negate or vary any implied condition or warranty under the Sale of Goods Act or any deemed condition or warranty under this Act is void.

rules.title: UK: 30 days to reject a faulty item for a full refund
rules.window_note: 30 days, counted from the day after you owned it, got it, and had it installed (if it needed installing). Shorter for things that go off quickly, like food.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back in full — not a credit note, not a repair — if the item is faulty, doesn't match how it was described, or isn't fit for the job you told the seller about.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the shop that sold it (not the manufacturer) within 30 days and say clearly, in writing if you can, that you are rejecting the goods. Ask for a full refund. Don't let them push you into a repair — that's your choice, not theirs, inside 30 days.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: I'm exercising my short-term right to reject under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. The goods are faulty and I'd like a full refund, please.

rules.title: UK: one failed repair and you can demand your money back
rules.window_note: Use this once the first 30 days have passed. Within the first 6 months the shop cannot knock anything off your refund for the use you've had (cars are the one exception); after 6 months they can deduct something. Starts the moment the shop has had one go at fixing it or swapping it and the item is still faulty. You do not have to accept a second attempt.
rules.what_you_get: The shop gets ONE go at repairing or replacing it — free, reasonably quickly, and without a lot of hassle for you. If that one attempt fails, you can either keep the item and get money back off the price, or hand it back for a refund.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the shop in writing for a repair or replacement. Keep the date. If the same fault comes back, or they drag it out, write again saying the repair has failed and you are now using your final right to reject and want a refund.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: The repair has failed, so under section 24 of the Consumer Rights Act I'm using my final right to reject and asking for a refund.

rules.title: UK: 14 days to send back anything bought online
rules.window_note: 14 days from the day the goods land in your hands. If you ordered several things in one go, the clock starts when the last one arrives. If it comes in separate lots, it starts with the last lot.
rules.what_you_get: You can cancel an online, phone or doorstep purchase and get your money back, even if there's nothing wrong with the item. Useful when something arrives dead and you'd rather have the cash than argue about a repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller you are cancelling within 14 days of delivery — email is fine, and get it in writing. Then send the goods back and ask for your refund.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: I'm cancelling under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013. The goods arrived on [date], so I'm inside the 14-day cancellation period.
rules.source_quote: the cancellation period ends at the end of 14 days after the day on which the goods come into the physical possession of— (a) the consumer

rules.title: EU: choosing repair adds a year to your guarantee
rules.window_note: For things bought on or after 31 July 2026. It is an EU directive, so it works through your own country's law. Every country had to bring it in by 31 July 2026, but not all had done so: in September 2026 France's law still gave six months after a repair, not twelve. Check your own country's rules. The extra year is added once only, even if the item is repaired more than once, and it covers the whole item, not just the part that was fixed. During the extra year the seller can ask you to show the fault was there when you got the item. Your country can give you more, such as a longer extension or a new one after each repair.
rules.what_you_get: If you choose repair instead of replacement under the legal guarantee, your guarantee gets 12 more months. Where it is two years, it becomes three. Countries without a fixed guarantee period must still give you at least three years when the item is repaired. Before fixing anything, the seller has to tell you that you can choose repair or replacement, and about the extra year. The seller can refuse a repair that would cost far more than a replacement, and then there is no extra year.
rules.how_to_claim: When the seller offers you repair or replacement, say you want it repaired, and ask them to confirm in writing that your legal guarantee now runs 12 months longer and to give you the new end date.
rules.script_hint: I am choosing repair rather than replacement. Under Directive (EU) 2019/771 as amended by Directive (EU) 2024/1799, as it applies in our national law, that extends my legal guarantee by 12 months, so please confirm my new end date in writing.
rules.source_quote: The Directive amends the Directive on Sale of Goods giving consumers a new right to an extra year of the legal guarantee if they choose to repair a defective product instead of replacing it.

rules.title: EU: makers must repair some products, even after the guarantee ends
rules.window_note: There is no set number of years from the day you bought it. The maker only has to repair your product for as long as, and as far as, EU repair rules still apply to it. Those rules are not only about spare parts. They can also be about how easily the product comes apart, and about getting repair information and tools. The European Commission says that in practice this means faults in parts the maker has to keep as spare parts, and that it runs 5 to 10 years depending on the product and the part, counted from when the last one of your model was put on the market, not from the day you bought it. That is the Commission's view, not a court ruling. For vacuum cleaners and for servers and data storage there is no spare-parts rule at all, so how far the duty goes for those two is not settled. Things bought before 31 July 2026 are covered too, but only items that had to follow these rules when they were put on the market: for example washing machines, dishwashers, fridges, TVs and monitors from 1 March 2021, phones and tablets from 20 June 2025, and tumble dryers and room heaters from 1 July 2025. Every EU country had to apply this in its own law from 31 July 2026, but many had not yet told the EU they had done it, so it may not apply in your country yet.
rules.what_you_get: For washing machines and washer-dryers, dishwashers, fridges and freezers, tumble dryers, TVs and monitors, phones, cordless phones and tablets, room heaters, welding equipment, vacuum cleaners, and servers and data storage: when you ask, the maker must repair it, even after your guarantee has ended, as far as the EU repair rules for your product go. The repair can be free or cost a reasonable price, and it must be done in a reasonable time. The maker can refuse only if repair is impossible. It cannot refuse just because parts cost a lot, or because someone else repaired it before. It may lend you a replacement while it repairs yours, or offer you a refurbished one if repair is impossible. It also cannot use contract terms, hardware or software to block repairs, unless it has a legitimate and objective reason. Vacuum cleaners and servers are a weaker case than the rest. For them the EU rules set no time for keeping spare parts. They only cover taking the product apart, handing out repair information, and, for servers, firmware updates. So you can still ask for a repair, but the maker may say it cannot get the part, and how far it has to go for those two is not settled.
rules.how_to_claim: If the seller's legal guarantee still covers the fault, go to the seller instead, because that repair is free. Otherwise ask the maker to repair it. The maker has to give you free information about its repair service and show its typical repair prices on a free website, so check its site first. If the maker is based outside the EU, ask its authorised representative in the EU. If it has none, ask the importer, and if there is no importer, the distributor, such as the shop. You can ask for a European Repair Information Form. They do not have to give you one, but if they do, it is free and its price and terms stay fixed for 30 days. They may charge for a check that is needed to find the fault, but they must tell you the cost first.
rules.script_hint: I am asking you to repair this under your obligation to repair in Directive (EU) 2024/1799, because it is one of the products listed in its Annex II. Please tell me the price and how long the repair will take.
rules.source_quote: Member States shall ensure that upon the consumer’s request, the manufacturer shall repair goods for which, and to the extent that, repairability requirements are provided for by Union legal acts listed in Annex II.

rules.title: Apple free-repair programs (check your serial number first)
rules.window_note: Most Apple programs last 3 years from the day the device was first sold, even if your normal warranty ran out years ago. A few (safety recalls) have no end date at all. Apple's list changes, so check it again whenever something breaks.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or free replacement part for a fault Apple has admitted is its own. No AppleCare needed, no receipt needed - they go by the serial number.
rules.how_to_claim: Open Apple's service programs page and see if your product is on the list. If it is, put your serial number into the checker on that program's page (Settings > General > About on an iPhone or iPad, or the Apple menu > About This Mac). If it says you're eligible, book a Genius Bar appointment or an Apple Authorised Service Provider and bring the device in.
rules.script_hint: My serial number comes up as eligible for your service program for this exact fault, so this repair should be free of charge.

rules.title: Mac mini (2023, M2) that won't turn on: free repair
rules.window_note: Covered for 3 years after the Mac mini was first sold. Only M2 Mac minis built between 16 June 2024 and 23 November 2024 count. Apple may make you get it fixed in the country you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: Apple repairs a Mac mini that has stopped powering on, free of charge, out of warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Type the serial number (it's on the bottom of the Mac mini) into the checker on Apple's program page. If it's eligible, book a repair at an Apple Store or Apple Authorised Service Provider.
rules.script_hint: My Mac mini won't power on and its serial number is eligible for your no-power service program - this repair should be free.
rules.source_quote: If so, Apple or an Apple Authorized Service Provider will provide service, free of charge.

rules.title: Pixel 7a swollen battery: free new battery (or cash outside the US)
rules.window_note: Google says coverage lasts 3 years from the day you bought it. Not every Pixel 7a is affected - you have to be checked.
rules.what_you_get: One free battery replacement. Outside the US you can take cash instead: 200 USD if your phone is out of warranty, or 456 USD if it's still in warranty. Or, out of warranty, you can take a 300 USD discount code toward a new Pixel on the Google Store. Amounts are paid in your local currency. Signs to look for: the phone looks fatter, the back is bulging or lifting away, or the battery drains very fast.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to g.co/pixel/7abattery and register your phone. Google runs an eligibility check and a physical inspection. Free battery swaps are done at walk-in repair centres in the US, Canada, UK, Germany, Japan, Singapore, Australia, France and India, or by post in the US and India.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 7a battery is swelling and I want to register for your extended repair programme for the 7a battery.
rules.source_quote: Out of warranty appeasement options (not available in India, Japan, and the United States where both mail-in and walk-in services are available)

rules.title: Sony CEA-G CFexpress Type A cards: free repair until 2029
rules.window_note: Sony started this free repair programme on 26 June 2024 and says it runs until 29 June 2029. It doesn't matter how old the card is, only whether its serial number is on the list.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair for CEA-G80T, CEA-G160T, CEA-G320T and CEA-G640T memory cards that stop being recognised, or fail to finish saving a photo, when it's very cold (around -10C).
rules.how_to_claim: Read the 8 or 9 digit lot number on the back of the card and check it against the affected ranges on Sony's notice page (numbers that start with 3 are not affected). If yours is on the list, back up and then erase everything on the card, because the repair wipes it, and contact Sony support to send it in.
rules.script_hint: My CEA-G CFexpress card's serial number is on your free repair list - please repair it under that programme.
rules.source_quote: we will repair affected memory cards free of charge until June 29, 2029, subject to the terms and conditions of the memory card's original Limited Warranty.

rules.title: EU: search Safety Gate for dangerous product alerts
rules.window_note: No deadline. New alerts from EU countries are added almost every day.
rules.what_you_get: Confirmation that your product was flagged as dangerous somewhere in the EU, with the brand, model and the risk - useful proof when you ask the seller or maker for a free fix or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the European Commission's Safety Gate alerts site for your brand and model. If it appears, take the alert to whoever sold it to you and ask what they are doing for owners.
rules.script_hint: My model appears in the EU Safety Gate alerts - what are you offering owners of this product?
rules.source_quote: Informe- | 17/09/2026 Número de aviso SR/02570/26 Producto Coche de pasajeros Marca Land Rover

rules.title: AppleCare+: free battery service once yours drops under 80%
rules.window_note: Any time your AppleCare+ plan is still running. A one-off plan is usually 2 years (Mac plans are usually 3); a monthly or yearly plan keeps going until you cancel it. Only the battery in your covered device counts.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery repair, or a replacement device, with no service fee and no parts charge.
rules.how_to_claim: Check the battery first. On an iPhone open Settings, tap Battery, then Battery Health, and read Maximum Capacity. On a Mac hold Option, click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power. If it says under 80%, book a free appointment at an Apple Store or an Apple Authorised Service Provider, bring the device, and ask for battery service under AppleCare+.
rules.script_hint: My AppleCare+ is still active and Battery Health shows maximum capacity below 80%, so the battery replacement is covered at no extra charge.
rules.source_quote: the capacity of the Covered Device's battery to hold an electrical charge is less than eighty percent (80%) of its original specifications

rules.title: Apple's free 1-year warranty covers a broken battery, not a tired one
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. This is the free warranty everyone gets, separate from AppleCare+. In the EU and UK your legal rights run longer than Apple's own year.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery replacement, but only if the battery is genuinely faulty: it swells, leaks, shuts the device off suddenly, or will not charge at all. Slowly holding less charge is called normal ageing and is not covered here.
rules.how_to_claim: Book a free Genius Bar or Apple Authorised Service Provider appointment inside the first year. Describe the actual failure (sudden shutdowns, swelling, refuses to charge) rather than saying the battery runs down faster than it used to.
rules.script_hint: This isn't normal ageing. It shuts down at 40% / the back has swollen / it won't take a charge at all. That's a defect in materials or workmanship, which the one-year warranty covers.

rules.title: Samsung: battery is covered if it falls under 80% or leaks
rules.window_note: Usually one year from purchase for recent Galaxy phones, tablets and watches, though the exact length depends on the model. Accessories in the box get a shorter period.
rules.what_you_get: A free battery replacement if the battery drops below 80% of the capacity it is rated for, or if it leaks, while still inside the warranty period.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the phone with your receipt to a Samsung walk-in service centre, or start a mail-in repair on Samsung's support site, and ask them to test the battery capacity.
rules.script_hint: Samsung's own warranty says batteries are covered if capacity falls below 80% of rated capacity. Please test mine and replace it under warranty.

rules.title: Your 3-year laptop probably only has a 1-year battery
rules.window_note: One year from purchase, even if the laptop itself has a 3-year or 5-year plan. The battery clock runs on its own. Some people bought a longer battery option at checkout, so check your order.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery if it fails inside that first year. After that you pay, unless you bought extended battery coverage at the same time as the laptop.
rules.how_to_claim: Run the maker's built-in battery test (Dell SupportAssist, or the battery health screen on your machine), save the result, then contact support with your service tag or serial number.
rules.script_hint: I know my system warranty is longer. I'm claiming on the separate one-year battery warranty and my machine is still inside it. Here is the failed battery test result.

rules.title: DEWALT replaces worn-out parts free for the first year
rules.window_note: The first 12 months after you buy the tool. The separate 3-year warranty covers faults, but only this first year covers parts that simply wore out. After that, worn parts are on you. The limited warranty rejects wear. The free service contract is the one that covers it.
rules.what_you_get: DEWALT services the tool and replaces parts worn out by normal use, for free. This is unusual: most brands never cover worn parts at all. There is also a 90-day money-back guarantee if you are not happy with how the tool performs.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the tool and your receipt to a DEWALT factory or authorised service centre and ask for the one-year free service contract, not a warranty repair.
rules.script_hint: I'm not claiming a defect. I'm asking for the one-year free service contract, which covers maintaining the tool and replacing parts worn by normal use.

rules.title: Makita: 3 years on lithium tools and batteries, 1 year on most other gear
rules.window_note: Three years from purchase for lithium-ion tools, batteries and chargers, and also for air (pneumatic) nailers and MAKTRAK storage. Most other Makita products get one year. Repairs needed because of normal wear and tear are never covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the tool, battery or charger has a fault in its parts or in how it was made.
rules.how_to_claim: Send or take the complete tool, battery or charger with proof of purchase to a Makita factory or authorised service centre.
rules.script_hint: This is a lithium-ion battery, so it has the three-year warranty, and it's a defect, not wear. Please repair or replace it.
rules.source_quote: Every Makita® Lithium-Ion Tool, Battery, Charger, MAKTRAK™ Modular Storage System, and Pneumatic Nailer is warranted to be free of defects from workmanship and materials for the period of THREE YEARS

rules.title: RYOBI ONE+ batteries carry a 3-year warranty of their own
rules.window_note: Three years from the date you bought the battery. If the battery came inside a tool kit, the kit receipt covers it. Only the person who first bought it new is covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery if it fails from a fault in its parts or workmanship inside three years.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring the battery with proof of purchase to a RYOBI authorised service centre, or contact RYOBI support through their website.
rules.script_hint: This 18V ONE+ battery has its own three-year limited warranty and it's still inside it. It won't take a charge any more.
rules.source_quote: With the exception of batteries, power tool accessories are warranted for ninety (90) days. Batteries are warranted for three years.

rules.title: EU: smartphone and tablet batteries must pass an 800-charge test
rules.window_note: Covers smartphones and slate tablets put on the EU market from 20 June 2025, so a phone sold to you after that date can still be older stock. Home cordless phones have no charge test at all. The claim below goes to the shop that sold it, under the EU legal guarantee, which runs at least 2 years from delivery. Some countries give longer, so it is worth asking even after 2 years.
rules.what_you_get: This is not a promise about your own battery. It is a test the model has to pass: a smartphone or slate tablet battery must last at least 800 full charges and still hold 80% of its rated capacity. A basic mobile phone has to reach 500. The tested number is on the model's EU energy label. Your smartphone or tablet must also record how many full charges the battery has done and its health in %, in the settings or somewhere else you can get to. If your battery is far below 80% after far fewer charges than the label says, those numbers help you argue to the seller that it is not as durable as you could expect. The seller can disagree. Heat and fast charging wear a battery out too, and the maker's manual has to say so.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the full charge count and battery health on your device, in the settings or wherever your maker put them, and take a screenshot. For a smartphone or slate tablet the model's charge number is on its EU energy label, and the label's QR code opens the EU product database. A basic mobile phone has neither, so name the 500-charge rule instead. Then write to the shop that sold it to you, not the maker, while you are inside the legal guarantee, and ask for a free repair or replacement. You can report a model you think fails the test to your country's market surveillance authority.
rules.script_hint: My [phone] is still inside its legal guarantee. Its battery shows [X]% health after only [Y] full charges, while the EU energy label for this model says [Z] charges. Under Directive (EU) 2019/771 that is not the durability I could reasonably expect, so please repair or replace it free of charge.
rules.source_quote: Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall ensure that the devices achieve at least 800 cycles at 80 % remaining capacity, to be tested under charging conditions where the charging rate is limited by the battery management system and not by the power delivery capabilities of the power supply.

rules.title: The parts meant to wear out usually aren't covered
rules.window_note: This exclusion lasts for the whole life of the product, so check it before you spend time claiming. Milwaukee, for example, says chucks, brushes, cords, o-rings, seals, bumpers and driver blades wear out with normal use and are not covered. An exception: in the US and Canada, DEWALT replaces worn parts free in the first year. Otherwise, buy the replacement part and fit it.
rules.what_you_get: An honest 'probably nothing' — and a way to reframe it. Makers name these parts and refuse them outright: motor brushes, chucks, cords, saw shoes, blade clamps, o-rings, seals, bumpers, driver blades, pistons, air filters and drive belts. But if the part broke or failed early rather than gradually wearing down, that is a defect, and defects ARE covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Before claiming, ask yourself: did it wear away smoothly over time, or did it fail? If it failed, say so plainly and describe how — cracked, snapped, leaked, seized — and how little use it had.
rules.script_hint: This part didn't wear out. It failed after very light use, and that's a defect in materials or workmanship, not normal wear.
rules.source_quote: This warranty does not cover repair when normal use has exhausted the life of a part including, but not limited to, chucks, brushes, cords, saw shoes, blade clamps, o-rings, seals, bumpers, driver blades

rules.title: Trek covers your bike frame for as long as you own it
rules.window_note: No time limit if you are the first owner. If you bought the bike second-hand, you still get 3 years from the day the first owner bought it. Paint, Bontrager parts and wheels with metal rims run out after 2 years.
rules.what_you_get: A new frame, rigid fork or full-suspension swing arm if yours cracks or fails because it was badly made. Bontrager wheels with carbon rims are covered for life too. The shop may charge you for the labour to swap the parts over.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike and your receipt into any Trek shop and ask them to open a warranty claim with Trek. Only a Trek shop can start one.
rules.script_hint: My Trek frame has cracked. Trek covers frames for the lifetime of the original owner - can you open a warranty claim for me?
rules.source_quote: Framesets (frame and rigid fork), main frame, and full suspension swing arms for the lifetime of the original owner

rules.title: Specialized frames are covered for life if you registered the bike
rules.window_note: Lifetime only if you registered the bike, frameset or Roval wheels on Specialized's site within 90 days of buying it. If you did not register it, you get 2 years. Second owners get 2 years from the first sale.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame or rigid fork if it fails because it was badly made. Suspension forks are not part of the lifetime cover. Paint, Specialized-branded parts and e-bike motors get 2 years. Turbo e-bike batteries get 2 years or 300 charges, whichever comes first.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring the part and the original receipt to a Specialized shop. If you bought it on specialized.com, message Rider Care instead.
rules.script_hint: My Specialized frame has failed and I registered it within 90 days of buying it, so it has the lifetime frame warranty. Please start a claim.
rules.source_quote: *Register your bike, frameset, or Roval wheels within the first 90 days of purchase for a lifetime warranty to the original owner.

rules.title: Crashed your Specialized? They sell you a new frame at a discount
rules.window_note: Frames and framesets have no time limit. Helmets, shoes, carbon bars, stems, seatposts, cranks, saddles and Turbo batteries and motors are covered for 5 years. Second-hand owners qualify too, as long as you have a receipt.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement or repair at a discount when you broke it yourself riding, so a warranty will not help. You get 35% off if the item is under 3 years old, 25% off at 3-4 years, and 20% off after that. Turbo motor and battery parts get 50% off under 3 years, then 35%, then 20% up to 5 years. Prices can vary by country, and the shop may charge for labour.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the damaged part and any proof of purchase (receipt, bank or card statement) to a Specialized shop and ask for Assisted Replacement. It only covers damage that happened while riding, not scratches.
rules.script_hint: I crashed and damaged this - I know it is not a warranty claim. Can you put it through Specialized's Assisted Replacement programme?
rules.source_quote: The discount structure is tiered and based on the original retail purchase date of the product being replaced. Pricing may vary depending on your location.

rules.title: Giant and Liv bike frames have no time limit
rules.window_note: No time limit on the frame for the first owner. Downhill frames get 3 years, rigid forks 10 years, Giant-branded parts 2 years, paint 1 year. It does not pass on to whoever you sell the bike to.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame if it fails because it was badly made, plus free parts and some labour money for the shop. E-bike batteries and electric parts are covered for 2 years, or 600 charges for the battery.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike and your receipt to a Giant shop. They have to see the bike in person - photos by email will not do.
rules.script_hint: My Giant frame has failed. Giant gives the original owner a lifetime frame warranty - here is my receipt, can you file it?

rules.title: Cannondale frames are covered for life if the bike is registered
rules.window_note: No time limit on frames, swing arms, stays and shock links of models Cannondale brought out in 2026 or later, but only if the bike was registered on cannondale.com or by the shop. Older models have their own rules: most frames are still covered for life, but swing arms and stays get 5 years and gravity and downhill frames get 3, so ask the shop which set applies. Paint and Cannondale-branded parts get 1 year. It does not pass to a new owner.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement frame, swing arm, chainstay, seatstay or shock link if it fails because it was badly made. Lefty and Headshok fork bodies are covered for life too. You pay the shop for the labour to swap parts over.
rules.how_to_claim: Clean the bike, then take it with the original dated receipt to a Cannondale shop on the same continent where you bought it.
rules.script_hint: My Cannondale frame has failed. The bike is registered with Cannondale, so the frame has lifetime cover - please open a claim.
rules.source_quote: Frames, Swing Arms, Chainstays, Seatstays (including FlexPivot™) on models introduced in 2026 and after: Lifetime of product.

rules.title: Brompton frames get 7 years if you registered the bike
rules.window_note: 7 years from the day it was sold if you registered it in the My Brompton area of their site. Only 2 years if you never registered it. There is no mileage limit either way.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of the main frame parts if they fail because they were badly made. Other non-wearing parts like crank arms, brake calipers and mudguards get 2 years. Electric Brompton parts get 2 years, or 3 if registered.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the shop that sold you the bike, or contact Brompton, with your frame number and receipt.
rules.script_hint: My Brompton main frame has failed and the bike is registered on My Brompton, so it has 7-year cover. Can you start a warranty claim?

rules.title: Britax: 1 year on car seats, 2 years on strollers
rules.window_note: Car seats are covered for 1 year from the day you bought them. Strollers get 2 years. Both start from the original purchase date, and you need the receipt. Items bought second-hand, on auction sites or from shops Britax has not approved are not covered. Damage from misuse or from not following the manual isn't covered.
rules.what_you_get: Britax repairs the item or sends you free replacement parts if something was badly made.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Britax Consumer Services with your receipt and the model and date-of-manufacture label on the seat or stroller. Lines are open weekdays 10am-4pm Eastern.
rules.script_hint: My Britax stroller has a fault and it is less than 2 years old. I have the receipt - can you send replacement parts under warranty?
rules.source_quote: Britax® products purchased from unauthorized retailers, online auction sites, or as second hand items, are not covered under warranty.

rules.title: Graco replaces a faulty car seat or stroller free for 1 year
rules.window_note: 1 year from the day you bought it or the day it was delivered, whichever is later. Second-hand items are not covered. For most Graco gear you must have bought it from Graco or a shop they approve of, but that limit does not apply to car seats and carriers.
rules.what_you_get: A brand-new product or a brand-new part, free, if yours was badly made. If your model is gone they send something similar of the same or higher value.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Graco or fill in their warranty claim form. Have the item number, serial number, date stamp, receipt and photos ready.
rules.script_hint: My Graco is under a year old and this part broke on its own. I have the receipt and photos - I would like a free replacement under the limited warranty.

rules.title: A recalled car seat must be fixed, swapped or refunded free
rules.window_note: No purchase window, and it does not matter whether you ever registered the seat or kept the receipt. The free-fix duty only stops for things bought more than 15 years before the recall notice, and car seats expire long before that. Free, including posting you the fix kit. Free recall fixes don't expire and don't depend on you having the receipt.
rules.what_you_get: By US law the maker has to put it right for free - repair it, swap it for the same or an equal seat, or refund what you paid. The maker picks which one.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the model number and date of manufacture on the sticker on the seat, look it up on the government recall list, then call the maker and say your seat is on it. Registering your seat also gets you told automatically next time.
rules.script_hint: My car seat, model number [X] made on [date], is on the recall list. The law says the remedy is free - please send me the fix or a replacement.

rules.title: Big Agnes fixes faults for life and other damage for a small fee
rules.window_note: No time limit on manufacturing faults, for the life of the product. Electronics are the exception at 2 years with a receipt. You must have bought it from Big Agnes or a shop they approve of.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if it has a fault in how it was made or in the materials. If they can't replace it, you get credit for what you paid, with a receipt. Normal wear - sun damage, broken poles, peeling seam tape, torn fabric, worn-out zippers - is not covered, but they will repair it as cheaply as they can.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a case on the Big Agnes support site or call them, then send the item in clean and dry.
rules.script_hint: The zipper slider on my Big Agnes tent has split. If that is not a warranty fault, can you quote me for a repair instead?
rules.source_quote: Normal wear and tear includes things like UV damage, pole breakage, seam tape failure, fabric tears, and worn out zippers.

rules.title: MSR tents and stoves: 3 years on faults
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase, for the first owner only, and only if you looked after the gear. Normal wear, punctures, scrapes and misuse do not count.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the tent, stove or filter was faulty. They try to fix it first and will often just post you the replacement part with instructions.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact MSR through Cascade Designs and attach your receipt, a clear description of the problem, and photos - photos speed it up a lot.
rules.script_hint: My MSR tent has a fault and it is under 3 years old. Photos and receipt attached - can you repair or replace it under warranty?
rules.source_quote: we warrant your product to be free from defects in materials and workmanship for three years.

rules.title: NEMO covers its gear for as long as it lasts
rules.window_note: No time limit, but you must be the first owner and have a receipt from a shop NEMO approves of. Gear bought second-hand or at a garage sale is not covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if it has a fault in how it was made or in the materials. If they no longer make it, you get NEMO credit instead. Return postage back to you inside the US and Canada is free. Wear and tear or accident damage is not covered, but they can usually fix it for a fair price.
rules.how_to_claim: File a claim on NEMO's site and wait for a return number. Wash and dry the item first - they will not inspect dirty gear - then post it to them with the number in the box. Expect 2 to 6 weeks.
rules.script_hint: The seams on my NEMO sleeping bag have come apart. NEMO's guarantee has no time limit for the original owner - here is my receipt.
rules.source_quote: All NEMO products carry a lifetime warranty against defects in workmanship and materials to the original owner, with proof of purchase from an authorized NEMO dealer.

rules.title: Therm-a-Rest pads are covered for life against faults
rules.window_note: No time limit on faults for the first owner, buying from an approved shop. Electronics are the exception at 2 years. Punctures, scrapes and general wear are not faults.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the pad, bag or pillow was badly made. They repair first where they can. A mattress over two years old may come back as a similar-looking one instead. If your damage is not a fault, they will often still repair it for a fair fee.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Therm-a-Rest through Cascade Designs with your receipt, a description, and photos so they can identify the model.
rules.script_hint: My Therm-a-Rest is leaking along a seam, not from a puncture. Photos and receipt attached - can you repair or replace it?
rules.source_quote: We offer a Limited Lifetime Warranty on all products, except electronic devices, which have a 2-year Limited Warranty. Warranty coverage is extended only to original purchasers and purchases from authorized dealers.

rules.title: Casper mattress sagging more than an inch: 10-year cover
rules.window_note: 10 years from purchase. Only the first buyer is covered - it does not pass on. If you bought it somewhere other than casper.com, you must register it on Casper's site to switch the warranty on. Clearance and final-sale mattresses can have a shorter warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the mattress has a visible dip deeper than 1 inch, the foam splits or cracks, or the cover zip is faulty. If it has to be shipped back, Casper covers that cost.
rules.how_to_claim: Email Casper at support@casper.com with your proof of purchase and photos. A tape measure or ruler laid across the dip in the photo makes the claim much easier to approve.
rules.script_hint: My Casper mattress has a dip deeper than one inch, measured with a ruler in these photos. That is a covered defect under the 10-year warranty.
rules.source_quote: If purchased from another retailer, please click here to register your product to activate your warranty

rules.title: Purple mattress dipping more than an inch: 10-year cover
rules.window_note: 10 years from purchase, first buyer only. The cover is separate and only gets 2 years. After the first 100 days you pay the shipping. Do not take the cover off to inspect it - that can cancel the warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement if the mattress has a dip deeper than 1 inch that stays after you get off it, or if the material cracks or splits during normal use.
rules.how_to_claim: If you bought it from another shop, ask that shop first. If you bought it from Purple, or the shop can't be reached, start a claim on Purple's site or call 1-888-848-8456. Have your order number or receipt, photos of the dip measured against the flat area around it, photos of the whole mattress, and proof of your bed frame. The law tag must still be sewn on. Leave the cover on.
rules.script_hint: My Purple mattress has a body impression deeper than one inch after full recovery. That is listed as a defect in the 10-year warranty - please open a claim.
rules.source_quote: Mattress law tags, usually sewn into the head or foot of bed, must be intact for Purple or its third-party providers to process a warranty claim

rules.title: Tempur-Pedic: 10 years, no deductible
rules.window_note: 10 years from the purchase date on your receipt, first buyer only - it does not pass to anyone you sell it to. Keep the receipt for the full 10 years. If they replace it, the new one keeps the original date, it does not restart.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of a faulty mattress or flat foundation, covering every part, with nothing to pay towards it. You pay only the transport cost.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Tempur-Pedic on 1-800-821-6621 (in Canada, call 1-800-887-4321) and send a copy of the receipt, a written description of what is wrong, and photos (or a recording if the problem is a noise). They may ask for proof that the base or frame under the mattress was a proper one.
rules.script_hint: My Tempur-Pedic mattress has a defect and it is inside the 10-year limited warranty. Receipt and photos attached - please arrange a repair or replacement.
