rules.source_quote: If you believe your product is defective and want to file a warranty claim, please email/call our Customer Service staff at inquiries@tempurpedic.com or 800-887-4321.

rules.title: IKEA mattresses have a 10-year warranty most people forget
rules.window_note: 10 years from the day you bought it, first buyer only. It does not cover kids' mattresses, mattress pads or toppers, mattress protectors, or sofa-bed mattresses.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or the same or a comparable mattress, if the seams split, springs are damaged, the handles or base break, or it sags badly. IKEA pays for parts, labour and the repair staff's travel.
rules.how_to_claim: Take or send your original receipt to your local IKEA store - the receipt is the proof of purchase and the claim will not work without it. IKEA inspects it and decides between repair and replacement.
rules.script_hint: My IKEA mattress is sagging badly and it is under 10 years old. IKEA gives mattresses a 10-year limited warranty - here is my receipt.

rules.title: Chase Sapphire Reserve buys it back when the store won't take a return
rules.window_note: You must call within 90 days of buying it, and only after the store has already said no to your return. Then you have 60 days to send the paperwork. The item has to still work and look new. Be ready to show the shop's return policy or that they turned you down.
rules.what_you_get: Chase refunds what you paid, up to $500 for one item and $1,000 per 12 months. You may have to mail the item in at your own cost.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the store for a return first and get their no. Then go to chasecardbenefits.com or call 1-800-350-1697 within 90 days of the purchase date.
rules.script_hint: The store refused to take this back and I bought it under 90 days ago on my Chase Sapphire Reserve. I'd like to use return protection.

rules.title: Chase Freedom Flex pays for a cracked or stolen phone
rules.window_note: This has nothing to do with when you bought the phone. You just have to have paid your whole phone bill with the card the month before the damage. Report it within 60 days of the damage and send papers within 90 days. If it was stolen, file a police report within 48 hours.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $800 per claim after a $50 deductible, with 2 paid claims and $1,000 max per 12 months. Lost phones and battery problems are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to chasecardbenefits.com or call 1-800-349-2691. Have your phone bill showing you paid it with the card, your card statement, and a repair estimate.
rules.script_hint: I pay my phone bill with my Chase Freedom Flex and my screen cracked. I want to file a cell phone protection claim.
rules.source_quote: Coverage is limited to a maximum of two (2) paid claims per twelve (12) month period and $1,000 per twelve (12) month period.

rules.title: Chase Freedom Flex: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Not tied to when you bought the phone. You must have paid your whole phone bill with the card the month before it broke or was stolen. Report it within 60 days and send the papers within 90 days. For theft, file a police report within 48 hours.
rules.what_you_get: Pay your phone bill with a Freedom Flex and a broken or stolen phone gets fixed or replaced - up to $800 a claim and $1,000 a year, minus a $50 deductible, maximum 2 claims in 12 months. Lost phones and battery problems are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to chasecardbenefits.com or call 1-800-349-2691 within 60 days. Have the phone bill and card statement showing you paid last month's bill with the card, a repair estimate, and a police report if it was stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a cell phone protection claim on my Chase Freedom Flex. I pay my monthly wireless bill with this card and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date.
rules.source_quote: This benefit may allow cardmembers to get up to $800 per claim and $1,000 per 12-month period in cell phone protection against covered theft or damage

rules.title: Amex Green, Blue Cash and Delta cards cover broken or stolen buys, with a smaller cap
rules.window_note: Same 90-day cover and same tight 30-day reporting window as the premium Amex cards, but the payout cap is ten times smaller. Send proof within 60 days.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $1,000 for one item and $50,000 per card per calendar year. Covers Green, Blue Cash Everyday, Blue Cash Preferred, Amex EveryDay, Delta Gold and Blue, Hilton and Marriott Bonvoy cards.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to americanexpress.com/onlineclaim or call 1-800-228-6855 within 30 days of the damage.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on my Amex Blue Cash card in the last 90 days and it got damaged. I want to open a purchase protection claim.

rules.title: Amex Platinum and Blue Cash Preferred buy it back when the store won't take a return
rules.window_note: Call within 90 days of buying it, and only after the store has already refused your return. You then have 30 days to send the paperwork, and 30 days to mail the item in if they ask. The item must be unused and in working order.
rules.what_you_get: Amex refunds what you paid, up to $300 for one item and $1,000 per card per calendar year. Only some Amex cards have this, like the Platinum Card and Blue Cash Preferred - the Gold Card and Blue Cash Everyday don't. If they ask you to mail the item in, they pay the postage.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the store for a return first and get their no. Then call 1-800-228-6855 within 90 days of the purchase date.
rules.script_hint: The store won't take this back and I bought it under 90 days ago on my Amex. I'd like to use return protection.
rules.source_quote: American Express may refund the full purchase price excluding shipping and handling, up to $300 per item, up to a maximum of $1,000 per calendar year per Card account

rules.title: Amex Platinum and other premium cards pay for a cracked or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the phone. You must have paid last month's whole phone bill with the card. Report within 90 days of the damage and send written proof within 120 days. For theft, file a police report within 48 hours.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $800 per claim after a $50 deductible, 2 claims per card per 12 months. Cracked screens count. Lost phones and scratches do not. Only some cards have it, like the Platinum Card, Business Platinum, Centurion, Delta SkyMiles Reserve and Platinum, Hilton Honors Aspire, Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant and Business Gold. The Gold Card and Blue Cash cards don't.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-833-784-1467 or file at aig.claimnotify.com/americanexpress. Have the phone bill showing you paid with the card and your card statement.
rules.script_hint: I pay my phone bill with my Amex Platinum and my phone got damaged. I want to file a cell phone protection claim.
rules.source_quote: U.S. issued American Express account as defined: Centurion, Platinum, Delta Reserve, Delta Platinum, Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant, Business Gold and Hilton Aspire Consumer

rules.title: Citi Strata Elite doubles your warranty, up to 2 extra years
rules.window_note: Works on maker or store warranties of 24 months or less, and it doubles them, so a 2-year warranty becomes 4 years. Tell them within 60 days of the item breaking and send written proof within 180 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim. Citi took these shopping benefits off most of its cards in 2019 and brought them back on this newer card.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call the Mastercard Assistance Center at 1-833-251-6404. Have the receipt, warranty paper, and card statement.
rules.script_hint: My item's warranty just ran out and it failed. I bought it on my Citi Strata Elite card and want to open an extended warranty claim.

rules.title: Citi Strata Elite covers new stuff that gets broken or stolen
rules.window_note: The damage or theft has to happen within 120 days of buying it (90 days in New York). You then have 60 days to report it.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account over 12 months.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-833-251-6404. Have the receipt, card statement, and a police report if it was stolen.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on my Citi Strata Elite in the last few months and it got damaged. I want to file a purchase assurance claim.

rules.title: Capital One Venture X pays for a cracked or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the phone. Pay your monthly phone bill with the card. Report within 60 days of the damage. For theft, file a police report within 48 hours.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $800 per claim after a $50 deductible, 2 claims and $1,600 per 12 months. That yearly cap is higher than most other cards.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140 within 60 days. Have the phone bill paid with the card and your card statement.
rules.script_hint: I pay my phone bill with my Capital One Venture X and my phone got damaged. I want to file a cellular telephone protection claim.

rules.title: Capital One Venture X buys it back when the store won't take a return
rules.window_note: Call within 90 days of buying it, and only after the store has already said no to your return.
rules.what_you_get: You get back what you paid, up to $300 per item and $1,000 per account per year.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the store for a return first and get their no. Then call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140 within 90 days of the purchase date.
rules.script_hint: The store refused my return and I bought it under 90 days ago on my Capital One Venture X. I'd like to use return protection.

rules.title: Capital One Venture X covers new stuff that gets broken or stolen
rules.window_note: The damage or theft has to happen within 90 days of buying it. Then call within 60 days and send documents within 90 days of the damage.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $10,000 per claim and $50,000 per cardholder to repair, replace or refund the item.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140 within 60 days. Have the receipt, card statement, and photos of the damage.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on my Capital One Venture X within the last 90 days and it got damaged. I want to file a purchase security claim.

rules.title: Capital One World Elite Mastercard refunds the difference if the price drops
rules.window_note: You have 120 days from buying it to spot a printed or online ad with a lower price for the exact same make and model. Then open a claim within 120 days of that ad, and send the proof within 180 days of the ad's date. Price protection is rare now, so this one is easy to miss.
rules.what_you_get: They pay you the difference between what you paid and the lower advertised price, up to $250 per claim and 4 claims per 12 months.
rules.how_to_claim: Save the ad showing the lower price, then go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-877-288-6784.
rules.script_hint: I bought this on my Capital One World Elite Mastercard and found it advertised cheaper within 120 days. I want to file a price protection claim.
rules.source_quote: Visit www.mycardbenefits.com or call 1-877-288-6784 to open a claim. You must report the claim within one hundred twenty (120) days of the incident or the claim may not be honored.

rules.title: UK Section 75: your credit card company owes you exactly what the shop owes you
rules.window_note: The law itself sets no cut-off. In practice people claim up to about six years after the thing went wrong, because six years is the normal court deadline for a broken deal in England and Wales. Don't wait — ask as soon as you spot the problem. If they turn you down, take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Debit cards do not count - for those, ask about chargeback instead.
rules.what_you_get: This is the biggest unused right in Britain. If you put a purchase on a credit card, your card company is on the hook for exactly the same things the shop is. Faulty, never turned up, or not what you were promised? Ask the card company for a repair, a replacement or your money back. It still works if the shop has gone bust, moved on, or is simply ignoring you. It covers anything with a ticket price over £100 and up to £30,000. It does NOT work with debit cards, charge cards, overdrafts, bank transfers or cash — and note that some American Express cards are charge cards rather than credit cards, so check yours. Pay even a tiny slice — a £20 deposit on a £3,000 kitchen — and the card company is still on the hook for the whole thing.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone or message your credit card company (not the shop) and say you are making a Section 75 claim. Send them the receipt, whatever you were promised in the advert or listing, and photos of what is wrong. They have to investigate it themselves — they are not allowed to just tell you to go back to the shop.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a Section 75 claim under the Consumer Credit Act 1974. The cash price was over £100 and I paid at least part of it on this credit card, so you are jointly and severally liable with the seller. I want a repair, a replacement, or my money back.

rules.title: UK Section 75A: the backup rule for things costing more than £30,000
rules.window_note: No fixed legal deadline, but treat six years from the problem as your practical limit. You also need to have tried the seller first, so start that straight away.
rules.what_you_get: If something cost more than £30,000, Section 75 is too small for it, but Section 75A can still catch it — as long as the loan itself is no more than £60,260. It applies when you paid with a loan taken out just for that purchase — one the seller set up, or one that names the item — and it lets you make the lender put things right. It is one step weaker than Section 75: you have to have genuinely tried the seller first and got nowhere (including because they have gone bust, vanished, or won't reply).
rules.how_to_claim: First chase the seller and keep every email and letter as proof you tried. If they go bust, save the news or the Companies House page. Then write to the lender saying you are making a Section 75A claim and attach that proof.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a claim under Section 75A of the Consumer Credit Act 1974. I've taken reasonable steps to pursue the supplier and have not obtained satisfaction, so I'm asking you as the lender under the linked credit agreement to put this right.
rules.source_quote: This section does not apply where— (a) the cash value of the goods or service is £30,000 or less, (b) the linked credit agreement is for credit which exceeds £60,260

rules.title: Chargeback: your bank claws the money back — and it works on debit cards too
rules.window_note: Usually about 120 days — roughly four months — counted from the day you should have received the thing, or the day you got something broken or not as described. Some cases get longer, some shorter, so ring the bank the same week you notice.
rules.what_you_get: Your bank asks the seller's bank to hand the money back. Unlike Section 75, it works on debit cards and there is no £100 minimum, so it covers all the cheap stuff Section 75 misses. Good reasons to use it: the thing never arrived, it arrived broken, it wasn't what was described, or a refund you were promised never showed up. Your bank does not have to raise a chargeback, but if you have a good reason, it can be good practice for them to do it.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the seller first and save the messages — banks usually want to see you tried. Then ring your bank, say you want to raise a chargeback, and give them the receipt, the messages and photos of the problem. If the first attempt is knocked back, ask them to push it again with extra evidence.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to raise a chargeback on this transaction. The goods were [never delivered / faulty / not as described], I've already contacted the seller and got nowhere, and I'm within the card scheme's time limit.
rules.source_quote: This might be from the date you expected to receive them but they weren't provided, or from the date you got something that was defective or not as described.

rules.title: If your UK bank says no, the Ombudsman is free — and often says yes
rules.window_note: Complain to the bank first. If eight weeks go by with no final answer, or you don't like the answer they give, take it to the Ombudsman. Don't sit on it — go soon after the bank replies, because the Ombudsman has its own deadline for taking cases on. You get 6 months from the date on the bank's final response letter to go to the ombudsman. You also normally need to have complained to the bank within 6 years of the problem, or 3 years of realising you had one. They get 8 weeks for most complaints and 15 days for payment complaints.
rules.what_you_get: A free referee. If your bank turns down your Section 75 claim, or refuses to try a chargeback, the Financial Ombudsman Service will look at it for nothing. They can order the bank to refund you in full or in part, arrange a repair or replacement, collect the goods at no cost to you, refund interest and charges, and pay you extra for the trouble and upset. Banks know this, which is why simply saying the words often gets the claim reopened.
rules.how_to_claim: Send the bank a formal complaint in writing and ask for a final response letter. Wait for their answer or for eight weeks, whichever comes first. Then fill in the free complaint form on the Ombudsman's website and attach everything you sent the bank.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to raise this as a formal complaint and receive a final response letter. If I'm not happy with it I'll be taking the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

rules.title: EU: a fault in the first year counts as there from the start
rules.window_note: Runs for one year from the day you got the item. Some EU countries make it two years. France does for new goods, and keeps one year for second-hand goods. After that you can still claim under the two-year guarantee, but the seller can ask you to show the fault was there when you got the item.
rules.what_you_get: If a fault shows up within a year of getting the item, the law assumes it was already there on the day you got it, so you don't have to prove that part. The seller can still try to prove the item was fine. The rule also does not apply when it cannot fit the kind of item or the kind of fault. When it applies, you get the free repair or replacement the legal guarantee gives you.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller in writing that the fault showed up within a year of delivery, so the law presumes it was there from the start and it is up to them to prove otherwise. Then ask for a free repair or replacement. Writing it down gives you a record of the date.
rules.script_hint: The fault appeared within one year of delivery, so under Article 11 of Directive (EU) 2019/771, as it applies in our national law, it is presumed to have existed at delivery unless you prove otherwise. Please repair or replace it free of charge.
rules.source_quote: Any lack of conformity which becomes apparent within one year of the time when the goods were delivered shall be presumed to have existed at the time when the goods were delivered, unless proved otherwise or unless this presumption is incompatible with the nature of the goods or with the nature of the lack of conformity.

rules.title: Canada: 90 days of free theft-and-damage cover on most big-bank credit cards
rules.window_note: The item itself is covered for 90 days from the day you bought it. But once something happens you have to report it fast, and each card is different: American Express wants a call within 48 hours, RBC and BMO within 30 days, CIBC within 45, TD and Scotiabank within 90. Ring the same day if you can.
rules.what_you_get: Most credit cards from Canada's big banks quietly insure whatever you buy with them against theft and accidental damage for the first 90 days — free, automatic, no sign-up. Drop the new laptop down the stairs, have the new bike stolen off the porch, and the card's insurer repairs it, replaces it, or pays you back. Two catches worth knowing: it usually pays only after your home or tenant insurance does, so often you get the deductible back rather than the whole item, and used items are usually excluded.
rules.how_to_claim: Search your card's exact name plus 'certificate of insurance' to find the claims number, then phone it before you pay for any repair or replacement. If it was stolen, report it to the police first and get the report number — the insurer will ask for it. Keep the store receipt and the card statement showing the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open a purchase security claim. I bought this on my card on [date], it was [stolen / accidentally damaged] on [date], and I'm still inside the 90 days.
rules.source_quote: All claims must be reported within 48 hours of the theft and damage occurring

rules.title: RBC credit cards double the maker's warranty for free
rules.window_note: The free extra cover starts the moment the maker's warranty ends and lasts as long as that warranty did, up to one extra year. The maker's warranty and RBC's extra can't add up to more than five years total. Once something breaks, tell RBC within 30 days and get your paperwork in within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Buy something on an RBC credit card and RBC automatically doubles the manufacturer's warranty for you, up to one extra year, at no cost and with nothing to sign up for. A one-year warranty becomes two. If the thing fails during that bonus year, RBC's insurer pays to repair or replace it. Exactly what's covered mirrors the original warranty, so if the maker only repaired rather than replaced, so will RBC.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone the claims line and open a claim BEFORE you pay for any repair — paying first can void it. Have three things ready: the store receipt, the RBC statement showing the purchase, and the manufacturer's original warranty paperwork. Terms vary slightly between RBC cards, so pull up your own card's certificate of insurance too.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open an extended warranty claim on my RBC card. The manufacturer's warranty has expired but I'm still inside the extra year that RBC's Extended Warranty Insurance gives me.

rules.title: TD credit cards double the maker's warranty by up to 12 extra months
rules.window_note: TD's cover begins the day the maker's warranty runs out and lasts as long as that warranty did, capped at 12 extra months. Report a problem to TD's claims administrator within 90 days of it happening. One trap: if the maker's warranty is longer than five years, TD only covers it if you registered the item within the first year after buying it.
rules.what_you_get: TD doubles the manufacturer's warranty on things you buy with a TD credit card, up to 12 extra months, free and automatic. The warranty has to be valid in Canada. Used, refurbished and demo items are out, and so are vehicles. There's a $60,000 lifetime cap across all your TD cards combined, which almost nobody ever reaches.
rules.how_to_claim: Call TD's claims administrator before you spend anything on the repair. Bring the store receipt, the TD statement showing the purchase, the manufacturer's Canadian warranty, and a repair estimate from an authorised repair shop. Check your own card's product summary too — the Aeroplan Visa Infinite Privilege and some other TD cards differ slightly.
rules.script_hint: I'm opening an Extended Warranty Protection claim on my TD credit card. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm within the additional period TD's coverage provides.
rules.source_quote: Coverage for eligible new items You purchase with your TD Credit Card. If the item comes with a Manufacturer's Warranty valid in Canada, you may be entitled to double the warranty period for up to 12 additional months.

rules.title: Scotiabank cards double the maker's warranty, up to one extra year
rules.window_note: Cover starts when the maker's warranty ends and runs for the same length again, capped at one extra year. Once something goes wrong, call within 90 days and before you get anything repaired. If the maker's warranty is five years or more, you must register the item with Scotiabank's insurer within one year of buying it or it isn't covered at all.
rules.what_you_get: Scotiabank doubles the repair cover the manufacturer gave you, up to one extra year, free, on things where you charged the full price to your Scotiabank card (Scene+ points count too). It works on items bought anywhere in the world as long as the maker's warranty is honoured in Canada or the US. You can file the claim online rather than sitting on the phone.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the claims administrator, or file online at manulife.ca/scotia, before paying for any repair. Have the store receipt, the card statement, and the manufacturer's warranty ready. Wording varies a little between Scotiabank cards, so also look up your own card's certificate of insurance.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an Extended Warranty claim on my Scotiabank card. The original manufacturer's warranty has run out and I'm within the additional year of repair coverage.
rules.source_quote: Insured Items with a Manufacturer's Warranty of 5 years or more are ONLY covered if registered within the first year of purchase.

rules.title: BMO Mastercards add up to a free extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: The extension runs on from the day the maker's warranty ends, up to a maximum of one extra year. Give BMO's operations centre written notice within 30 days of the problem and send proof within 90 days. If it truly wasn't possible to do that in time, you still have up to one year to get it in. If the maker's warranty is over five years, register the item with BMO within one year of purchase.
rules.what_you_get: BMO stretches the manufacturer's warranty on things bought with a BMO Mastercard by up to one extra year, free and automatic, and it covers parts and labour for mechanical breakdown just as the original warranty did. Items bought with reward points count as long as you charged the taxes to the card. Two things to know: cover stops dead if the manufacturer goes out of business, and items sold with a lifetime warranty are excluded.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring the operations centre as soon as it breaks to get a claim form, and don't pay for the repair first. You'll need the claim form, the store receipt, the BMO statement showing the purchase, the maker's Canadian warranty, and a repair bill or estimate from an authorised repair shop.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open an Extended Warranty claim on my BMO Mastercard. The original manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm within BMO's one-year extension.

rules.title: CIBC Visa cards double the maker's warranty, up to one extra full year
rules.window_note: The extra cover starts the moment the maker's warranty expires and doubles it, capped at one extra full year. Tell CIBC's insurer as soon as you know there's a problem, and no later than 45 days after it happens — miss that and they can turn the claim down. Then send the signed loss report within 90 days. If the maker's warranty is over five years, register the item within the first year.
rules.what_you_get: CIBC's Extended Protection automatically doubles the manufacturer's warranty on anything you pay for with a CIBC Visa, even if only part of the price went on the card, up to one extra full year, with nothing to sign up for. If only part went on the card, they pay no more than that part. It works on items bought in Canada, the US or anywhere in the world, as long as the maker's warranty is honoured in Canada or the US. Gifts you buy for other people are covered too. Used and demo items are not, and refurbished items only count if the maker refurbished them.
rules.how_to_claim: Phone the claims line straight away — the 45-day clock is strict. Then send the signed loss report with ORIGINAL receipts (not photocopies): the store receipt, the Visa slip or statement, and the manufacturer's warranty.
rules.script_hint: I'm reporting an Extended Protection claim on my CIBC Visa. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and I'm inside the additional year of coverage. Please send me the loss report form.
rules.source_quote: when at least a portion of the purchase price is charged to the card and the original manufacturer's warranty is honoured in Canada or the United States

rules.title: Costco adds a free second year of warranty on TVs, computers and big appliances
rules.window_note: Covers you for 2 years from the day you bought it in the warehouse, or the day it was delivered if you ordered online. Most makers only give you 1 year, so year two is free cover you probably did not know you had. Touchscreen tablets are not included.
rules.what_you_get: Costco fixes it, replaces it, or refunds up to what you paid - their choice. Covers TVs, projectors, computers, and big appliances like fridges over 10 cubic feet, freezers, ranges, cooktops, over-the-range microwaves, dishwashers, water heaters, washers and dryers.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Costco Technical and Warranty Services. Have ready: your membership number, the item number from your receipt, the model and serial number, and the date you bought it.
rules.script_hint: I bought this at Costco and it's broken. Costco extends the maker's warranty to 2 years, and I'm still inside that - I'd like it repaired or replaced.

rules.title: REI takes back anything badly made, no matter how old
rules.window_note: No deadline at all, as long as the problem is a fault in how the thing was made - a seam that came apart, a zip that failed, a buckle that snapped. Normal wear and tear does not count, and neither does damage from an accident or from using it wrong.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Wash or clean the item first - REI turns away dirty gear. Then take it to any REI store, or start a return on rei.com and say the reason is a manufacturing defect.
rules.script_hint: This has a manufacturing defect in materials or workmanship. REI's policy says those can come back at any time, whatever the purchase date.

rules.title: REI members get a full year to change their mind
rules.window_note: 365 days if you are an REI Co-op member. 90 days if you are not. Outdoor electronics - watches, GPS units, bike trainers, emergency beacons, cameras - are 90 days for everyone. Used gear bought in store is final sale.
rules.what_you_get: A swap for something else or your money back, even if you have used it, as long as you genuinely are not satisfied.
rules.how_to_claim: Clean the item, then take it to any REI store - free, and no paper receipt needed if you used your member number when you bought it. By post they take $7.99 off your refund.
rules.script_hint: I'm an REI member and this is inside my one-year satisfaction guarantee. I'd like to return it.

rules.title: Nordstrom has no time limit on returns at all
rules.window_note: Nordstrom says plainly: there are no time limits for returns or exchanges. They decide each one case by case, and now and then they may turn a return down. There are no restocking fees. This is only the main Nordstrom stores and nordstrom.com - Nordstrom Rack has its own, separate return policy.
rules.what_you_get: A refund back to how you paid. If they cannot find any record of the sale, you get the current price on a Nordstrom gift card instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any register at a Nordstrom store, or start a return online. Bring the receipt or order number if you have it - if you do not, they can often still find the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I know this is old, but Nordstrom's policy says there's no time limit on returns. Could you take a look at it for me?
rules.source_quote: From time to time we may not accept a return. There are no time limits for returns or exchanges.

rules.title: Target's own brands come back for a whole year
rules.window_note: A full year, but only for Target's own labels - the brands you can only buy at Target. Anything else in the shop gets 90 days. One catch: designer collaborations that are only in shops for a short time get just two weeks.
rules.what_you_get: A swap for a new one, or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the guest service desk at any Target with your receipt. If you paid through the Target app, the purchase in your Target Wallet counts as the receipt.
rules.script_hint: This is a Target owned brand, and those have a one-year return window - here's my receipt.

rules.title: Paying with the Target Circle card buys you 30 extra days
rules.window_note: Most things get 90 days at Target. Pay with the Target Circle credit or debit card, or be a Circle 360 member, and you get 30 days on top - so 120 days. It does not stack on Target's own brands, which already get a year.
rules.what_you_get: An extra 30 days to return nearly anything you bought with that card.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to guest service at any Target with the Circle card you paid with, so they can pull up the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I paid with my Target Circle card, so I get an extra 30 days on this return.

rules.title: IKEA gives you a year to return anything you never opened
rules.window_note: 365 days if the box is still sealed. 180 days if you opened it. You need the receipt and a government photo ID. They will not take plants, cut fabric, custom worktops, as-is items, or anything that is dirty, stained or altered.
rules.what_you_get: A full refund back to the way you paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the returns desk at any IKEA store with the receipt and your photo ID.
rules.script_hint: This is unopened and still inside IKEA's 365-day return window - here's my receipt.

rules.title: IKEA lets you swap a mattress you don't find comfy
rules.window_note: One swap, within 90 days of buying it. Sleep on it first - that is what the window is for. It must not be dirty, marked or damaged, and bed bases, slats and toppers don't count.
rules.what_you_get: You can swap it once for a different IKEA mattress. If the new one costs more you pay the difference; if it costs less you get the difference back on an IKEA refund card.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the returns desk at any IKEA with your receipt and ask to use the Love It or Exchange It mattress swap.
rules.script_hint: This mattress isn't comfortable for me. I'd like to use IKEA's one-time mattress exchange.
rules.source_quote: If you would like to upgrade your mattress, all we ask is that you pay the difference between the original purchase price and the price of the replacement chosen.

rules.title: IKEA quietly covers kitchens for 25 years and mattresses for 10
rules.window_note: Kitchen cabinet frames, doors, hinges and drawers (SEKTION): 25 years. Mattresses, sofa frames and cushions, wardrobes, storage and taps: 10 years. Kitchen knives and pots and pans: 15 years. Appliances: 5 years. The clock starts the day you bought it, and you need the original receipt.
rules.what_you_get: IKEA repairs it or replaces the faulty part or product at no cost, if the problem is a fault in the materials or the way it was made. Sagging mattresses, split seams, broken springs and broken mattress bases are all covered. Normal wear, scratches, knocks and bad assembly are not.
rules.how_to_claim: Take photos of the fault, find your original receipt, and take both to the returns desk at any IKEA or call IKEA customer service. Say you are making a warranty claim, not a return.
rules.script_hint: I'm making a claim under the IKEA limited warranty on this - it's a fault in materials or workmanship, and the warranty runs for years, not months.

rules.title: Home Depot's own card turns 90 days of returns into 365
rules.window_note: A full year instead of 90 days, if you paid with a Home Depot Consumer Credit Card, a Pro Xtra Credit Card, or a Home Depot Commercial Account. It does not rescue the short-window stuff: big appliances are 48 hours; dehumidifiers, air conditioners, gas generators, gas pressure washers, pumps and portable heaters are 7 days; and furniture, TVs, computers, gas-powered garden kit and holiday decor are 30 days.
rules.what_you_get: A full refund, up to a year after you bought it.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any Home Depot store with your receipt, the Home Depot card you paid with, and photo ID. Any store will take it, even if you bought it online.
rules.script_hint: I paid with my Home Depot card, which gives me 365 days to return this instead of 90.
rules.source_quote: Return in 30 Days Furniture, Tractors, Framing & Roofing Compressors, Consumer Electronics (televisions and computers), Paint Sprayers and Gas Powered Items

rules.title: Home Depot guarantees trees and shrubs for a year
rules.window_note: Perennials, trees, roses and shrubs are guaranteed for a full year. Most other plants get 90 days. Cut flowers and floral arrangements can't be returned at all.
rules.what_you_get: Store credit if a perennial, tree, rose or shrub dies after the first 90 days. Inside 90 days it is a normal return.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the dead plant and your receipt to any Home Depot.
rules.script_hint: This shrub died. Home Depot's everyday guarantee covers perennials, trees, roses and shrubs for a year - I'd like the store credit.
rules.source_quote: Most plants are returnable within 90 days. Perennials, trees, roses, and shrubs have a 1-year guarantee and can be returned after 90 days for Store Credit.

rules.title: Best Buy's paid membership stretches 15 days of returns to 60
rules.window_note: 60 days if you pay for My Best Buy Plus or My Best Buy Total. Everyone else gets 15 days. The clock starts the day you receive it. Anything you activate - phones, cellular tablets, hotspots, cellular watches - is 14 days no matter what, except Verizon devices which get 30. The membership window does not apply to things sold by other sellers on the Best Buy site. Opened cameras, drones and projectors can cost you a 15% restocking fee, and activatable devices $45. These terms took effect on 23 February 2026, so check anything you read that is older.
rules.what_you_get: A refund the same way you paid, or a straight swap for the same item.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any Best Buy store with the packaging, accessories and your receipt or packing slip, or start a return in your Best Buy account for a free FedEx label. Wipe your data and unlink the device first, or they can refuse it.
rules.script_hint: I'm a My Best Buy Plus member, so my return window on this is 60 days, not 15.
rules.source_quote: If you want to return or exchange your purchase, please know that the time period begins the day you receive your product

rules.title: John Lewis includes 2 years of cover on electricals and 5 on TVs
rules.window_note: At least 2 years on every electrical item, and 5 years on TVs. You do not pay extra for it - it comes with the purchase. Most makers only give you 1 year, so John Lewis is covering you long after the maker has stopped.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, done by a repairer that John Lewis and the maker both approve. If it cannot be fixed, John Lewis gives you the same or a similar model, or its price on a John Lewis e-gift card.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact John Lewis - in a shop, or through the guarantees page on their site - with your order number, and tell them the item is faulty and still inside the John Lewis guarantee.
rules.script_hint: This is faulty and it's still covered by the John Lewis guarantee that came with it - I'd like it repaired.
rules.source_quote: Minimum 2 year guarantee now included on all electricals, 5 years on TVs. All at no extra cost.

rules.title: Decathlon covers everything it makes for 2 years, and some gear for life
rules.window_note: 2 years on every Decathlon-brand product, counted from the day you bought it. In the UK this cover is for Decathlon members. Longer on some things: Quechua and Forclaz backpacks are covered 10 years (Simond too in the US), metal bike frames and forks for life, and carbon bike frames for 5 years. In the UK, fitness machines and inflatable tents also get 5 years.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or a swap for the same item. If it cannot be fixed or swapped, you get store credit or your money back.
rules.how_to_claim: Find your order confirmation or receipt. In the US, contact Decathlon customer service online (customer.service@decathlon.com) with the date you bought it and photos or a video of the fault. In the UK, take it to a Decathlon store or contact customer service. Say it has a manufacturing fault.
rules.script_hint: This is a Decathlon product with a manufacturing defect, and Decathlon gives a 2-year warranty on all its products.
rules.source_quote: Two year warranty on all Brands by Decathlon products for members

rules.title: MEC has no deadline for returning gear
rules.window_note: MEC says straight out that there is no time limit on returns of qualifying products. Electronics are the one exception - those are capped at 90 days. What they will not take: gear that is simply worn out or at the end of its life, final sale items unless they are faulty, hygiene items that have been worn, and food, fuel or bear spray.
rules.what_you_get: A refund to how you paid, or an MEC gift card.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any MEC store (free), or use the online return form on mec.ca to get a shipping label and post it to MEC's warehouse (this costs $11 plus tax). For a warranty problem, contact MEC Customer Care with photos and details before you send anything.
rules.script_hint: MEC's return policy has no time limit on qualifying products, and this is not worn out or a final-sale item - I'd like to return it for a refund.
rules.source_quote: There is no time limit to make a return on qualifying product (except for electronics which are limited to 90-days).

rules.title: Pixel 9 Pro / 9 Pro XL line or flicker on screen - Google replaces the screen free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new.
rules.what_you_get: A free screen replacement if a vertical line runs from the bottom of the screen to the top. Screen flicker also counts on the Pixel 9 Pro.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to store.google.com/repair, check your device, then book a walk-in repair centre or start a mail-in repair. A cracked screen or water damage can stop you qualifying.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 9 Pro has the vertical line on the display, which is covered by your Extended Repair Program, so the screen replacement should be at no charge.

rules.title: Pixel 8 line or flicker on screen - Google replaces the screen free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new.
rules.what_you_get: One free screen replacement if your Pixel 8 shows a vertical line running up the display, or the display flickers.
rules.how_to_claim: Enter your IMEI number on Google's repair page to check you qualify, then book a walk-in or mail-in repair. Cracked glass or water damage can mean you have to pay.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 8 has the vertical line fault covered by your Extended Repair Program, so I should get a free display replacement.

rules.title: Pixel 9 Pro Fold acting up - Google may swap the whole phone free
rules.window_note: Coverage runs for 3 years from the day you bought the phone new. Replacements started going out on 8 December 2025.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement phone if your Pixel 9 Pro Fold is one of the units Google flagged as having a fault that stops it working properly.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to store.google.com/repair and check your Pixel 9 Pro Fold. If it is affected, Google arranges a replacement online, at a Google Store, or at a walk-in centre.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel 9 Pro Fold is covered by your extended warranty program, so I should be eligible for a replacement at no charge.

rules.title: LG fridge stopped getting cold - the compressor is covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: Years 1-5: LG pays for the compressor part AND the labour. Years 6-10: LG still pays for the Linear or Inverter compressor part, but you pay the fitting. The clock starts on the day you bought it, so keep your receipt. Ask them to confirm in writing that the part is covered before the technician arrives. Terms vary by model, so check your own model number on LG's site. Book a repair through LG rather than a random local engineer - an outside repair can cost you the free part.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement compressor - the expensive part that makes the fridge cold. In the first 5 years the fitting is free too. The sealed system (condenser, dryer, connecting tube, evaporator) is also parts-and-labour free for 5 years.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring LG on 1-800-243-0000 and tell them the fridge is not cooling. Have your model number, serial number and proof of purchase ready. Ask them to book a warranty repair, not a paid one.
rules.script_hint: My LG fridge has stopped cooling and my Linear Inverter compressor is still inside the 10-year parts warranty, so I want this booked as a warranty repair.

rules.title: LG washing machine motor covered for 10 years
rules.window_note: The whole washer is parts-and-labour free for 1 year. After that, the Direct Drive Motor (the stator or rotor) is a free part for 10 years from the day you bought it, but you pay the fitting. The stainless steel drum is a free part for 3 years. Find the model and serial number, usually inside the door frame or on the back panel.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement motor if the motor in your LG washer dies. You pay only the labour after year one.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring LG on 1-800-243-0000 with your model number, serial number and receipt. Say you think the Direct Drive Motor has failed and ask for it to be booked under the 10-year motor warranty.
rules.script_hint: The Direct Drive Motor on my LG washer has failed and it is still inside the 10-year parts warranty, so the motor itself should come at no cost to me.

rules.title: HP laptop battery or power cord recall - free replacement, no time limit
rules.window_note: HP gives no end date for these programs and still lists them today. The battery recalls cover batteries sold from March 2013 to December 2018. The power cord recall covers cords sold with laptops from September 2010 to June 2012. HP says to check your battery again even if you checked before. HP's power cord recall page no longer loads, so for a cord, contact HP support.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery (or a free replacement AC power cord) for HP and Compaq laptops on the recall list, because the originals can overheat and catch fire.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to HP's recalls page, open the battery program, and run HP's free checker (the HP Battery Program Validation Utility). It tells you in about 30 seconds if your battery is affected. If it is, HP replaces it free - built-in batteries are swapped by an HP-approved technician. Stop using the battery in the meantime.
rules.script_hint: HP's checker says my battery is affected by your safety recall, so I need the free replacement battery sent out.
rules.source_quote: The affected batteries were shipped with specific HP, Compaq, HP ProBook, HP ENVY, Compaq Presario, and HP Pavilion Notebook Computers sold worldwide from March 2013 through October 2016

rules.title: Whirlpool, Maytag, KitchenAid, Jenn-Air or Amana appliance recalls - free fix
rules.window_note: Recalls have no cut-off date. If your appliance was recalled and never fixed, the free fix is still owed to you years later. You need the model number and the serial number - they are on a sticker inside the door frame or behind a drawer.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, free replacement part, or a replacement appliance, depending on what the recall notice says. Whirlpool Corporation owns all these brands and lists their recalls on its own site.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the model and serial number sticker on your appliance, then check it against Whirlpool Corporation's recall pages - the current list, and the past recalls list linked from it. Each recall notice tells you the exact phone line or web form for that product.
rules.script_hint: My model and serial number match one of your recalls, and the fix was never done on my unit, so I would like the free remedy arranged.
rules.source_quote: Quality Campaigns and Product Recall

rules.title: Car, tyre, car seat or trailer recall - get the free fix
rules.window_note: Once a safety recall is announced, the free fix for a vehicle or car seat has no end date. The law only lets the maker charge if the vehicle or part was first sold new more than 15 years before the recall was announced (5 years for tyres). For a tyre, bring it in within 180 days of getting the recall notice, or of being told a replacement is ready if that comes later. You do not need to have bought it new yourself.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair at a dealer for any open safety recall on your vehicle. Sometimes the maker replaces the part, refunds you, or buys the vehicle back instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Type your 17-character VIN into the recall checker at nhtsa.gov/recalls. For a car seat or tyre, search the same page by brand and model instead. If an open recall shows up, ring any franchised dealer for that brand and book the recall work. Say the word 'recall' - it is not a normal service booking.
rules.script_hint: My VIN shows an open safety recall, and I would like it booked in for the free recall repair.
rules.source_quote: The requirement that a remedy be provided without charge does not apply if the motor vehicle or replacement equipment was bought by the first purchaser more than 15 calendar years

rules.title: Canada: check if your product has been recalled
rules.window_note: Make sure your product is the exact one in the notice, for example by the model, UPC or code it lists. Older recalls are archived, so tick "Include archived" when you search. The site's data is updated daily, so it is worth checking again later. You can also sign up for emails about new and updated recalls.
rules.what_you_get: If your product is on a recall notice, the notice says what to do. Some notices offer a refund or a free repair kit. Others tell you to stop using the product, or to throw it out or return it to where you bought it.
rules.how_to_claim: Search recalls-rappels.canada.ca by brand or product type. It has recalls from Health Canada, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency and Transport Canada. If your product matches, follow the instructions in the notice. If there are none, or you have questions, call the company or visit its website. Don't give the product to someone else, and don't throw it out without following the instructions.
rules.script_hint: My product matches a recall notice on the Government of Canada's Recalls and Safety Alerts site. Please tell me what that notice says I should do next.
rules.source_quote: Find recalls, advisories and safety alerts

rules.title: Check any UK product for a recall - free replacement, repair or refund
rules.window_note: There is no time limit on a recall. Old recalls stay claimable, and the government keeps a searchable list you can check any time. New alerts are added regularly, so search again whenever something goes wrong. You can filter by product type and by whether it's an alert, a report or a recall.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement, a free repair, or a refund from the maker or the shop - whichever the recall notice says.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the Product Safety Alerts, Reports and Recalls list on gov.uk for your brand and model. You can also sign up for email alerts. Then contact whoever the notice names.
rules.script_hint: My product is on the OPSS recall list and I have never had it dealt with, so I would like the free repair or replacement.
rules.source_quote: You can search the list to check products you own are safe and subscribe to email updates for new products added.

rules.title: Before you pay for any repair, search the maker's own 'service program' list
rules.window_note: These lists change all the time - programs get added and quietly retired. Check on the day your thing breaks, and check again if you get told no.
rules.what_you_get: Big makers quietly fix known faults for free long after the warranty ends, but they rarely tell you. Apple, Google (for Pixel phones) and HP publish these programs on their own support sites.
rules.how_to_claim: Search the web for your brand plus the words 'service program' or 'extended repair program' plus your exact model and the fault, for example 'Pixel 8 extended repair program display line'. Only trust pages on the maker's own website. Then put in your serial number or IMEI on that page.
rules.script_hint: You publish a service program covering exactly this fault on this model, and my serial number qualifies, so I am asking for the free repair rather than a paid one.
rules.source_quote: iPhone 14 Plus Service Program for Rear Camera Issue

rules.title: Bosch e-bike battery that lost most of its range
rules.window_note: For personal use, Bosch's North American battery cover ends at whichever comes first: 2 years from the day you bought it, 4 years from the day the battery was made (this limit does not apply to batteries bought in California), or 500 full charges. Only the North American version of the battery is covered - check the label on the back of the battery.
rules.what_you_get: If a Bosch e-bike battery has fallen below the capacity Bosch promises, Bosch replaces it free. In North America Bosch promises most sizes (400–800Wh) keep at least 60% of their capacity, and 300Wh batteries at least 70%, within 500 full charges.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the bike to the shop you bought it from with your dated receipt and ask them to plug it into the Bosch diagnostic tool and check the battery's real capacity against the guaranteed figure.
rules.script_hint: My range has collapsed. Can you run the Bosch diagnostic and check the battery's remaining capacity against Bosch's guaranteed capacity? I think it qualifies for a warranty replacement.
rules.source_quote: With respect to batteries utilized for non-commercial purposes by the original consumer purchaser (i.e. personal use), the Battery Warranty Period is defined as any one of the following three cases, whichever occurs first

rules.title: Rad Power e-bike bought after 15 May 2026 — 2 years on frame and battery
rules.window_note: 2 years from the day you got the bike (or bought it, if later) for the frame, forks, stem, bars, headset, seat post, brakes, lights, bottom bracket, rims, hubs and reflectors. The battery ends at 2 years OR 300 charge cycles, whichever comes first. Pedals, freewheel, cranks, cassette, derailleur, shifter and saddle: 1 year. Tyres, tubes, brake pads, cables, chain, chainring, bearings and spokes: never covered. This cover comes from Rad Life Mobility, which took over the Rad brand after Rad Power Bikes went bankrupt, and it only covers bikes bought in the US or Canada after 15 May 2026. For a Rad bike bought before 15 December 2025, the new owner does not have to help: your route is a Proof of Claim in the Rad Power Bikes bankruptcy case, number 25-02183. For a bike bought between those two dates, Rad's page does not say what cover you have.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or a free replacement part - including a whole new battery or frame - when something fails from a build fault inside the window. You pay the shipping.
rules.how_to_claim: Open a case with Rad's customer service team through the Help Center on radpowerbikes.com. Send clear photos or a video of the fault first - they will not replace anything without them.
rules.script_hint: I bought my Rad bike on [date], after 15 May 2026, and the [part] has failed within 2 years. Here are photos and my order number - please send a warranty replacement.
rules.source_quote: Claims or issues relating to any Rad-branded products purchased prior to December 15, 2025, must be submitted as part of the bankruptcy process by filing a Proof of Claim.

rules.title: Segway scooter — battery only covered 180 days, so move fast
rules.window_note: Body of the scooter (deck, forks, stem, front hub motor, control board, dashboard, bars, charge port): 1 year. Battery pack and charger: only 180 days. Grips, fenders, lights, kickstand, grip tape: 90 days. Check the warranty sheet in your box — Segway varies this by model.
rules.what_you_get: Segway repairs or replaces the faulty part free, with new or refurbished parts, and pays the shipping back to you. The battery and charger window is short, so a battery that won't charge is worth reporting the same week it happens.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Segway on 1-866-473-4929 or email technicalsupport@segway.com with your serial number (on the underside of the deck, or in the Segway-Ninebot app) and your receipt. They give you an RMA number and you post the scooter in within 30 days.
rules.script_hint: My Segway scooter's battery won't charge. Here's the serial number and my receipt — please issue an RMA under the limited warranty.
rules.source_quote: This is the manufacturer's limited warranty ("Limited Warranty") for the Ninebot KickScooter ("Product") for consumers in North and South America.

rules.title: Car seat that was in a crash — get the letter, claim on insurance
rules.window_note: Ask while the crash claim is still open. In the US, NHTSA says a seat can be kept after a 'minor' crash only if ALL of these are true: the car could be driven away, the door nearest the seat was not damaged, nobody in the car was hurt, no airbags went off, and the seat has no visible damage. Anything worse and the seat should be replaced. In Canada, Transport Canada says not to use a car seat that has been in any collision, even if it was empty.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement car seat paid for by the car insurance claim, not by you. The seat's maker will send you a letter on their own letterhead saying the seat must be replaced after a crash — that letter is what the insurer wants before they pay.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the car seat's maker, give them the model and serial number off the sticker, and ask for their accident replacement policy letter. Send that letter and the receipt for the new seat to whoever is handling the crash claim.
rules.script_hint: My car seat was in a crash. Please email me your accident replacement policy letter with my model and serial number on it, so I can give it to my insurance company.
rules.source_quote: Do not use a child car seat that has been in a collision

rules.title: UPPAbaby car seat covered for its whole life, stroller for 3 years
rules.window_note: Car seats: the whole usable life of the seat, up to 10 years from the date it was made (that date is printed on a sticker on the seat). Strollers: 3 years from the day you bought it. Neither passes on if you sell it, and it only counts in the country you bought it in.
rules.what_you_get: UPPAbaby repairs the fault or sends you the replacement part free when a car seat or stroller has a manufacturing defect.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring UPPAbaby on (844) 823-3132, or email them through uppababy.com/support. Have your receipt from an authorised UPPAbaby shop ready, plus the serial number and date of manufacture from the sticker on the frame or seat shell.
rules.script_hint: My UPPAbaby [seat/stroller] has this fault. Here's my receipt and the serial number — please repair it or send the replacement part under warranty.
rules.source_quote: contact UPPAbaby customer experience by phone at (844) 823-3132 and visit uppababy.com/support/ to send an email.

rules.title: Bugaboo pram — 4 years if you registered it
rules.window_note: 2 years as standard. Register within 3 months of buying and you get 2 extra years — 4 in total. Bought straight from bugaboo.com? You were registered automatically. Refurbished and outlet items don't get the extension, and outlet items only get 1 year.
rules.what_you_get: Bugaboo repairs or replaces a faulty chassis, seat frame, plastic seat part, wheel, adapter, zip, harness part or seam - free, and pays to ship it to and from the shop.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the shop you bought it from, or Bugaboo customer service if you bought it on bugaboo.com. You need a copy of your dated receipt, a clear description of what's wrong, and photos of the broken part.
rules.script_hint: My Bugaboo [part] has broken. It's registered so I'm on the extended 4-year warranty — here are photos and my receipt, please repair or replace it.
rules.source_quote: Bugaboo will bear the expense and risk of transport from and to the retailer

rules.title: UK: the shop must repair or replace it for free, and pay the postage
rules.window_note: There is no fixed cut-off. It lasts as long as you could still take the shop to court - six years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, five in Scotland. But the older the item, the more you have to show the fault was there from the start.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a free replacement. The shop has to cover parts, labour and postage, and get it done in a reasonable time without messing you around.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the shop that sold it - not the manufacturer. Your contract is with the shop, so 'it's out of warranty, call the maker' is not an answer they are allowed to give. Say whether you want a repair or a replacement.
rules.script_hint: Under section 23 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 I am asking you to repair or replace this at no cost to me, including labour and postage. My contract is with you, not the manufacturer.

rules.title: UK: in the first 6 months the shop has to prove it, not you
rules.window_note: Six months from the day it was delivered. This one does not apply to the 30-day full-refund right - only to repair, replacement, price reduction and the final right to hand it back. After six months you can still claim, but then it's on you to show the fault was there from the start. If they refuse and you paid by credit card for an item priced over £100 (and up to £30,000), forward the very same email to your card company as a Section 75 claim.
rules.what_you_get: You do not have to prove anything. If it breaks in the first six months the law assumes the fault was already there when you got it, and the shop has to prove otherwise if it wants to refuse.
rules.how_to_claim: If the shop says 'you must have damaged it' or asks you to pay for an inspection report, point at this rule. The burden is on them, and paying for a report is not something you have to do.
rules.contact: 0808 223 1133 (Citizens Advice consumer helpline, England and Wales)
rules.script_hint: It failed within six months, so under section 19(14) of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 it is taken to have been faulty on the day it was delivered. If you disagree, it is for you to prove that, not me.
rules.source_quote: so far as the claim relates to any single item to which the supplier has attached a cash price not exceeding £100 or more than £30,000

rules.title: EU: if the maker gave a durability guarantee, go straight to the maker
rules.window_note: Lasts for the whole period of the maker's durability guarantee, for whatever that guarantee covers. This EU rule covers things bought from 1 January 2022. Your legal guarantee from the seller still applies alongside it. If the advertising for the guarantee promised better terms than the guarantee statement, the advertising's terms count, unless the advert was corrected before you bought.
rules.what_you_get: If the maker offered you a guarantee that the product will keep working normally for a set time, it has to repair or replace it for you directly for that whole time. What you can ask for is what the guarantee says. It binds the maker on the terms written in the guarantee statement and in the advertising for it, so read those terms and check what they cover. A 10 year guarantee on the motor covers the motor, not the whole machine, and a guarantee can set conditions, such as registering the product. Here "the maker" also means the company that brought it into the EU, or a company that put its own brand name on it. The repair or replacement must be free, done in a reasonable time, and without major hassle for you.
rules.how_to_claim: Find where the maker gave the guarantee: the box, the guarantee leaflet, the product page or an advert. Take a photo or screenshot of it, and read what it covers and what it asks you to do. Then contact the maker, not the shop, with that and your proof of purchase, and ask for a repair or replacement under its durability guarantee.
rules.script_hint: You gave a durability guarantee of [X] years on this product, and this fault is in what that guarantee covers. Under Article 17 of Directive (EU) 2019/771 you are directly liable to me for a free repair or replacement for that whole period.
rules.source_quote: Under the conditions laid down in this Article and without prejudice to any other applicable provisions of Union or national law, where a producer offers to the consumer a commercial guarantee of durability for certain goods for a certain period of time, the producer shall be liable directly to the consumer, during the entire period of the commercial guarantee of durability for repair or replacement of the goods in accordance with Article 14.

rules.title: France: the seller's 2-year guarantee, plus 6 months after a repair
rules.window_note: Two years from the day the item was delivered, for new and second-hand items bought from a business. For a new item, a fault that shows up in the first 24 months is taken to have been there from the start, unless the seller proves otherwise. For second-hand and refurbished items that period is 12 months. After it, you have to prove the fault was there when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement from the seller, done within 30 days of your request. You choose which one, but if one clearly costs more, the seller can pick the cheaper one. If the item is repaired under this guarantee, the guarantee gets 6 more months. If you chose repair but the seller replaced the item instead, a new two-year guarantee starts on the day you get the replacement. An EU law says that for items bought from 31 July 2026, choosing repair must add 12 months, but the government says France has not finished putting this into French law yet.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the seller, not the maker. Say you are using the garantie legale de conformite and that you choose repair. Take the item back with your receipt, invoice or delivery note, or write to the seller, ideally by registered letter with acknowledgement of receipt. After the repair, ask for the new end date of your guarantee in writing. If the seller will not help, you can report the problem to the consumer fraud office on SignalConso.
rules.script_hint: Je fais jouer la garantie légale de conformité et je choisis la réparation. Merci de me confirmer par écrit la nouvelle date de fin de garantie, prolongée de six mois selon l'article L217-13 du Code de la consommation. (I am using the legal guarantee of conformity and I choose repair. Please confirm in writing the new end date of my guarantee, extended by six months under article L217-13 of the Consumer Code.)
rules.source_quote: Tout bien réparé dans le cadre de la garantie légale de conformité bénéficie d'une extension de cette garantie de six mois.

rules.title: France: money knocked straight off your repair bill
rules.window_note: No age limit, so an old item still qualifies. But the item must not be under a guarantee, legal or commercial, and must not be covered by an insurance policy. The law says the bonus is not paid on a repair done under the legal guarantee (2 years from delivery in France) or a shop or maker's guarantee. The schemes for electrical items, bikes, sports gear, garden tools and furniture go further: the item itself must be out of guarantee, including extended warranties. The government's bonus page also says the item must have been bought in France.
rules.what_you_get: Money taken off the bill when a labelled repairer fixes your item. It is paid from repair funds that the makers of these products finance. It covers electrical and electronic items, clothes, household linen and shoes, furniture, sports and leisure gear such as bikes, backpacks and tents, and DIY and garden tools. Clothes made of leather or real fur are not covered. The amount is set for each type of item and repair, for example 25 euros off a mobile phone repair. The repair has to cost more than the bonus, so a bill smaller than the bonus gets you nothing, and some items have a minimum bill: at least 12 euros for clothes and shoes, and 100 or 150 euros for computers, printers, scanners and monitors. Labelled repairers must also guarantee their repair for at least 3 months.
rules.how_to_claim: Find a labelled repairer on the official site of the scheme for your item. The government page links to each one, and QualiRepar is the label for electrical and electronic items. The discount comes off your bill when you pay. There is no form to fill in and nothing to claim back, because the fund pays the repairer.
rules.script_hint: Êtes-vous labellisé pour le bonus réparation ? Mon article n'est plus sous garantie et n'est pas couvert par une assurance, et je voudrais que le bonus réparation instauré par la loi AGEC soit déduit de ma facture. (Are you labelled for the repair bonus? My item is out of guarantee and is not covered by insurance, and I would like the repair bonus set up by the AGEC law taken off my bill.)
rules.source_quote: Le bonus réparation est un dispositif instauré par la loi AGEC permettant la déduction d’un montant directement sur la facture du consommateur qui se rend chez un réparateur labellisé pour faire réparer son produit.

rules.title: Ireland: six years to claim, and they cannot keep re-repairing the same fault
rules.window_note: Six years counted from the day you received the goods. In the first 30 days you can simply reject it for a full refund. In the first 12 months the business has to prove it was not faulty.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, a replacement, money off or your money back - for up to six years, well past any manufacturer warranty. And if the same fault keeps coming back, you can refuse another repair and demand a replacement or a refund instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the business that sold it to you - your contract is with them, not the manufacturer. Say how many times it has been fixed already if this is a repeat fault.
rules.script_hint: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2022 my contract is with you as the seller, and I can seek a remedy for up to six years. This fault has already been repaired once, so I am asking for a replacement or a refund instead.

rules.title: Quebec: the shop cannot tell you to go bother the manufacturer
rules.window_note: Applies the whole time the legal warranty applies. It is about who you are allowed to chase, not about how old the item is.
rules.what_you_get: You get to pick. You can deal with the store, the manufacturer, or both at the same time. The store is not allowed to send you to the manufacturer instead of dealing with you itself. This works when the item isn't fit for normal use, didn't last a reasonable time, has a hidden defect, or has no parts or repairs available.
rules.how_to_claim: If a store says 'that's a manufacturer issue, call them', say no and point to this rule. Then keep dealing with the store. You can also contact the manufacturer at the same time if you want.
rules.script_hint: Section 54 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act lets me claim directly from you, the merchant, and Quebec's consumer office says a merchant may not require me to deal with the manufacturer. I am claiming the legal warranty from you.
rules.source_quote: A merchant may not require that you deal with the manufacturer.

rules.title: Quebec: parts, repairs and repair info must stay available for a reasonable time
rules.window_note: In force since 5 October 2025. No fixed cut-off: parts, repair services and repair information must stay available for a reasonable time after you buy. It covers things bought or rented from a business, new or used, whose use may need a part replaced, cleaned or updated, such as a toaster, a cell phone, a bike or a car. The shop or maker can only get out of it by warning you in writing, before you buy, that it doesn't supply them. A car maker can never opt out of giving access to the car's repair data.
rules.what_you_get: Replacement parts, repair services and the information needed to maintain or repair it (instructions, software and so on), in French. Prices must be reasonable, meaning not so high that they put you off. Repair information must be free when it is available online, in software or in an app, but a car's data can cost a reasonable fee. Parts must go in with commonly available tools and without damaging the item for good. If they don't supply these, you can ask them to repair it at their cost. If that fails, they must replace it with a new or reconditioned one that does the same things, or refund the price.
rules.how_to_claim: This is for when you can't get what you need to fix the item. If the shop or maker won't give you the replacement part, the repair service or the repair information, start here. If those are available and you can get them, this rule is not the one you want. First check whether it warned you in writing, before you bought it, that it doesn't supply parts, repairs or repair information. If it did, it doesn't have to supply them. If it didn't, ask it in writing to repair the item at its cost. It then has 10 days to tell you in writing when it will do the repair. You can accept or refuse that date. If you refuse, you can have someone else fix it and it pays the reasonable cost. If it gives no proper answer within 10 days, or misses the date it gave, you can demand a replacement or a refund. It picks which one, and you give back the broken item. If it still refuses, send a formal notice and, as a last step, go to court.
rules.script_hint: I can't get the replacement part, the repair service or the repair information I need for this item, and you never warned me in writing before I bought it that you don't supply them. Section 39 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act says they have to stay available for a reasonable time, so under section 39.5 I'm asking you to repair it at your cost and to tell me in writing within 10 days when you will do it.
rules.source_quote: The availability warranty applies when the use of an item may require the replacement, cleaning or updating of one of its components.

rules.title: BC, Saskatchewan and New Brunswick: goods must be durable, by law
rules.window_note: No fixed number of years - the test is what is reasonable for that kind of product used that way. In New Brunswick you can claim even if you were not the person who bought it - a gift counts. Each province also has its own deadline for going to court, usually about two years from when you noticed the problem, so do not sit on it. In BC and Saskatchewan, a seller of clearly used goods can sometimes switch this off. Applies to items bought or leased from a business, not from a private seller.
rules.what_you_get: A built-in promise, attached to every sale, that the item and its parts will last a reasonable period of time. It cannot be signed away, and 'sold as is, no warranty' does not remove it in a normal consumer sale.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the retailer. Say what you paid, how long it lasted, and that the province's statutory durability warranty applies whatever the manufacturer's warranty says. If they refuse, your provincial consumer office can advise (Consumer Protection BC, Saskatchewan's Financial and Consumer Affairs Authority, or New Brunswick's FCNB), and small claims court is the backstop.
rules.script_hint: The law in this province gives an implied warranty that goods will be durable for a reasonable period of time. This item was not. That warranty applies whatever the manufacturer's warranty says, and it cannot be waived.
rules.source_quote: there is an implied condition that the goods will be durable for a reasonable period of time having regard to the use to which they would normally be put and to all the surrounding circumstances of the sale or lease

rules.title: Saskatchewan: spare parts and repair shops must actually be available
rules.window_note: Runs for a reasonable period after you bought it - no fixed number of years. It only applies to products that normally need servicing or repair.
rules.what_you_get: A promise, built into the sale, that spare parts and somewhere to get it repaired will exist for a reasonable time after you buy. If the maker discontinued the part a year in, that is a breach you can push on.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Saskatchewan's Consumer Protection Division for guidance, then put your complaint to the retailer or manufacturer in writing. These statutory warranties cannot be excluded, and trying to exclude them can itself be an offence.
rules.script_hint: Saskatchewan's statutory warranties say spare parts and repair facilities must be available for a reasonable period after purchase. They are not, so I am asking you to repair, replace or refund this.

rules.title: Visa Signature / Visa Infinite: one extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Kicks in the day the maker's warranty runs out. Only works if that warranty was 3 years or less, so the latest it can help you is about 4 years after you bought the thing. The clock that really matters is after it breaks: call within 60 days or they can say no. Once the item breaks you have only 60 days to phone, and 90 days to send the paperwork. Banks pick which Visa benefits to switch on, so check your own card's Guide to Benefits before you count on it.
rules.what_you_get: Your Visa card quietly adds a whole extra year onto the maker's warranty. So if your TV died 14 months in and the maker only covered 12 months, Visa can pay to fix it, or replace it, or pay you back what you spent - up to $10,000 for that one item and $50,000 total.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Visa Benefit Administrator at 1-888-221-3289 as soon as the item stops working. Have ready: the receipt, the card statement showing you paid with the Visa, and the maker's warranty paper. They send you a claim form and tell you which repair shop to use.
rules.script_hint: I have a Visa Signature card and I'm filing an Extended Warranty Protection claim. I bought this on my card, the manufacturer's warranty was under three years, it just failed, and I'm calling within sixty days of the failure.

rules.title: Standard Mastercard: doubles a one-year warranty
rules.window_note: Only helps if the maker's warranty was 12 months or less. It doubles that, so most people are covered until about two years after they bought it. After it breaks you get 60 days to report it and 180 days to send the paperwork. Your bank picks which Mastercard benefits your card gets, and many basic cards do not have this one, so check your Guide to Benefits first.
rules.what_you_get: If your bank switched it on, a basic Mastercard doubles the maker's warranty by up to 12 extra months. Most electronics come with one year, so this usually gets you a second year free. They pay the repair or replacement, capped at what you charged to the card or $10,000, whichever is smaller.
