rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-627-8372 (that's 1-800-Mastercard) or go to mycardbenefits.com and start a claim within 60 days of the day it broke. Then send in the receipt and the card statement showing the purchase within 180 days.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to open a Mastercard Extended Warranty claim. I paid for this entirely with my Mastercard, it came with a manufacturer's warranty of twelve months or less, and it failed on this date - within the last sixty days.
rules.source_quote: Extended Warranty doubles the original manufacturer warranty up to a maximum of twelve (12) months on most items you purchase.

rules.title: World Elite Mastercard: up to two extra years of warranty
rules.window_note: Works on maker's warranties of 24 months or less, and doubles them - so a 2-year warranty becomes 4 years. Report the failure within 60 days and get your paperwork in within 180 days of the failure.
rules.what_you_get: A World Elite Mastercard with this benefit doubles the maker's warranty by up to 24 extra months - twice as much as a plain Mastercard. They repair it, replace it, or pay you back what you charged, up to $10,000.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-800-627-8372 (1-800-Mastercard) within 60 days of the day it broke. Send the receipt, your statement, the warranty paper and a repair estimate within 180 days. Banks pick which benefits their World Elite cards get, so check your Guide to Benefits first.
rules.script_hint: I have a World Elite Mastercard and I'm opening an Extended Warranty claim. The manufacturer's warranty was twenty-four months or less, the item failed on this date, and I'm reporting inside sixty days.
rules.source_quote: Extended Warranty doubles the time period of your Covered Purchase's original Manufacturer's Warranty or Store Warranty up to a maximum of twenty-four (24) months following the day that the Manufacturer's Warranty or Store Warranty expires.

rules.title: Citi Prestige: two extra years of warranty
rules.window_note: Citi adds 24 months on top of the maker's warranty, with total cover capped at 7 years from the day you bought it. Send all requested documents within 180 days of the failure. These are the Citi Prestige terms - other Citi cards have different ones, so check your own guide.
rules.what_you_get: On the Citi Prestige card, Citi adds a full 24 months to the maker's warranty - double what most cards give. They repair, replace or pay you back up to $10,000 per item.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-506-5222 (8am to midnight ET, any day) or go to mybenefits.cardbenefitclaims.com as soon as the item fails. First, check your card actually has the benefit - look up your card's Guide to Protection Benefits at cardbenefits.citi.com.
rules.script_hint: I want to open an Extended Warranty claim on my Citi Prestige card. The item failed on this date and the manufacturer's warranty has run out.
rules.source_quote: We will extend the manufacturer's warranty for an additional 24 Months. ... Total coverage up to a maximum of 7 years from the purchase date.

rules.title: Citi extended warranty (US)
rules.window_note: How much extra time you get, and how fast you must report a breakdown, is set in your card's Guide to Protection Benefits - read it before you count on this. Not every Citi card has it.
rules.what_you_get: Some Citi cards, like Double Cash, come with extended warranty cover: after the maker's warranty ends, the insurer can pay to repair or replace the item. The time and money limits are in your card's guide.
rules.how_to_claim: Sign in at citi.com and open your card's Guide to Protection Benefits. Call the claims number in it as soon as the item stops working, and keep the receipt, the card statement and the maker's warranty.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to file a Citi Extended Warranty claim. My [item] failed after the manufacturer's warranty ran out, and I paid for it in full with this Citi card.
rules.source_quote: Extended warranty Benefits are subject to terms, conditions and limitations, including limitations on the amount of coverage. Please refer to your Guide to Protection Benefits to learn more.

rules.title: Citi Prestige: damaged or stolen in the first 90 days
rules.window_note: Covers the first 90 days from purchase or delivery, whichever comes first. Get your documents in within 180 days of the incident. This is a Citi Prestige benefit - most other Citi cards do not have it.
rules.what_you_get: On the Citi Prestige card, Damage and Theft Purchase Protection repairs or pays back an item damaged or stolen in its first 90 days - up to $10,000 per incident and $50,000 a year. It even covers the deductible on your home insurance.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-506-5222 or go to mybenefits.cardbenefitclaims.com as soon as it happens. Have the receipt, the statement, and a police report for theft.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Damage and Theft Purchase Protection claim on my Citi Prestige card. I bought this within the last ninety days and it was damaged/stolen on this date.
rules.source_quote: If an item is purchased with Your Citi® Card and/or ThankYou® Points and is damaged or stolen within 90 days of purchase or delivery of the item, whichever is first

rules.title: Citi Prestige: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Not tied to when you bought the phone - it's tied to paying your monthly phone bill with the Citi card. Report within 90 days of the break or theft, and send written proof within 120 days.
rules.what_you_get: If your monthly phone bill goes on your Citi Prestige card, a damaged or stolen phone gets repaired or replaced - up to $1,000 per claim minus a $50 deductible, and $1,500 a year. Covers the main line and up to four more lines on the same bill. Cracked screens that don't stop the phone working are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-833-763-6324 (Mon-Fri, 8am to 8pm ET) or go to phonebenefit.com within 90 days of the damage or theft. Bring the statement showing last month's phone bill paid with the card, and a police report if stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm opening a cell phone protection claim on my Citi Prestige card. I pay my wireless bill with this card and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date, within the last ninety days.
rules.source_quote: The maximum liability is $1,000 per claim, and $1,500 per 12-month period. Each claim is subject to a $50 deductible.

rules.title: Capital One: still has extended warranty in 2026
rules.window_note: How long the extension runs depends on your card. World Elite Mastercard versions double the maker's warranty, adding up to 24 months. Visa Signature and Discover versions double it too, but add 12 months at most; Visa Infinite adds a flat 12 months. Capital One says to file within 60 to 90 days of the thing breaking.
rules.what_you_get: Capital One kept this benefit while others dropped it. Venture, VentureOne, Savor, SavorOne, Quicksilver and QuicksilverOne all have extended warranty. Covers TVs, phones and appliances that aren't wired or plumbed in - so a toaster yes, a built-in dishwasher no.
rules.how_to_claim: Mastercard versions: call 800-627-8372 or go to mycardbenefits.com. Visa and Discover versions: call 844-288-2140 or go to cardbenefitservices.com. File within 60 days of the failure to be safe. Bring the itemised receipt, the maker's warranty, a repair estimate and the statement showing the purchase.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an extended warranty claim on my Capital One card. The item failed after the manufacturer's warranty ended and I bought it with this card.
rules.source_quote: Your warranty coverage can be doubled up to one (1) additional year on eligible warranties of two (2) years or less.

rules.title: Capital One Venture X adds a free extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Only works if the maker's warranty was 3 years or shorter. It adds 1 more year on top. Call within 60 days of the item breaking and send the signed form within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim and $50,000 per cardholder.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140 right after the item fails. Have the receipt, warranty paper, and card statement.
rules.script_hint: The maker's warranty just ended and my item stopped working. I bought it on my Capital One Venture X and want an extended warranty claim.
rules.source_quote: However, if the manufacturer's warranty is for three (3) years, it would only be extended one (1) additional year for a combined total of four (4) years of coverage.

rules.title: Capital One Visa Signature cards double your warranty, up to one extra year
rules.window_note: Covers Capital One Visa Signature cards, such as Venture, VentureOne, Savor or Quicksilver cards with the Visa logo. It doubles the maker's warranty but adds 1 year at most, so a 6-month warranty becomes 12 months and a 3-year one becomes 4 years. Only works on maker warranties of 3 years or less. Call within 60 days of the breakdown and send the form within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim and $50,000 per cardholder. These cards do not have cell phone or return protection.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Benefit Administrator at 1-844-288-2140. You can also register the warranty ahead of time by calling the same number.
rules.script_hint: My item's maker warranty just ran out and it failed. I bought it on my Capital One Visa Signature card and want an extended warranty claim.
rules.source_quote: Your warranty coverage can be doubled up to one (1) additional year on eligible warranties of three (3) years or less.

rules.title: Capital One World Elite Mastercard doubles your warranty, up to 2 extra years
rules.window_note: Works on maker or store warranties of 24 months or less and doubles them, so a 2-year warranty becomes 4 years. Report within 60 days of the breakdown and send written proof within 180 days.
rules.what_you_get: They pay to repair or replace the item, up to $10,000 per claim. Their damage and theft cover is separate and smaller: $1,000 per loss within 90 days of buying.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to mycardbenefits.com or call 1-800-627-8372. Have the receipt, warranty paper, and card statement.
rules.script_hint: My item's warranty just ran out and it stopped working. I bought it on my Capital One World Elite Mastercard and want an extended warranty claim.
rules.source_quote: Extended Warranty doubles the time period of your Covered Purchase's original Manufacturer's Warranty or Store Warranty up to a maximum of twenty-four (24) months following the day that the Manufacturer's Warranty or Store Warranty expires.

rules.title: Wells Fargo: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: Nothing to do with when you bought the phone. Cover starts on the first day of the month after your phone bill posts to the Wells Fargo card, and stops if you skip a month. Report within 60 days of the loss. Send documents within 120 days. Lost phones are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: Pay your monthly phone bill with a Wells Fargo card and a damaged, stolen or accidentally-lost-forever phone gets fixed or replaced - up to $600 a claim minus a $25 deductible, 2 paid claims and $1,200 max in 12 months. Every line on that bill is covered. Cracked screens that don't affect how it works are not.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-316-8051 or go to mycardbenefits.assurant.com within 60 days of the damage or theft. You'll need the wireless bill showing the whole monthly payment went on the Wells Fargo card.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a Cellular Telephone Protection claim on my Wells Fargo card. I paid my full wireless bill with this card last month and my phone was damaged/stolen on this date.

rules.title: Some Wells Fargo cards: one extra year of warranty
rules.window_note: Works on maker's warranties of 36 months or less and adds 12 months, so a 3-year warranty becomes 4 years. If the maker's warranty is longer than 36 months you get nothing extra. Report within 60 days of the failure. Not every Wells Fargo card has this - Active Cash, for one, does not - so check your card's Guide to Benefits.
rules.what_you_get: On the Wells Fargo cards that have it, Wells Fargo adds 12 months onto the maker's warranty when you paid for the whole thing with the card. They cover the repair or a like-for-like replacement, up to $10,000 an item and $50,000 in a year.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-800-316-8051 or go to mycardbenefits.assurant.com within 60 days of the item failing. You can also upload your receipt and warranty to that site right after you buy something so it's ready later.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing an Extended Warranty Protection claim on my Wells Fargo card. I paid for the item in full with this card, the manufacturer's warranty was thirty-six months or less, and it failed on this date.
rules.source_quote: This coverage extends the manufacturer's U.S. repair warranty by an additional twelve (12) months.

rules.title: U.S. Bank Visa Platinum: pays for a smashed or stolen phone
rules.window_note: You must have charged your monthly phone bill to the U.S. Bank Visa Platinum in the calendar month before the phone broke or was stolen. Report it quickly - these benefits usually allow 60 to 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $600 per claim, minus a $25 deductible, and $1,200 or 2 claims in a 12-month period. Covers damage, theft, and a phone that's accidentally gone for good. Does NOT cover a phone you simply lost, or one that just stopped working on its own.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to usbank.com/cellphoneprotection or call the number on the back of your card and ask for the cell phone protection benefit administrator. Bring the statement showing last month's phone bill on the card, and a police report if it was stolen.
rules.script_hint: I'm filing a cell phone protection claim on my U.S. Bank Visa Platinum. I charged my monthly cell phone bill to this card the month before my phone was damaged/stolen.

rules.title: The 60-day rule that kills most card claims
rules.window_note: This is the deadline nobody knows about. Visa, Mastercard and Wells Fargo give you 60 days from the day the item breaks. American Express gives you only 30. Chase gives 90. The warranty itself might have years left - but if you sit on it, the card benefit is gone.
rules.what_you_get: Knowing this is worth money. People assume a card's extended warranty lasts as long as the coverage does. It doesn't - the moment the thing breaks, a short clock starts, and once it runs out the claim is dead no matter how good your case is.
rules.how_to_claim: The day something you bought on a credit card breaks or gets stolen, phone the card's benefit administrator - the number is on the back of your card. Open the claim first, gather paperwork after. Opening the claim is what stops the clock.
rules.script_hint: I want to open a claim today to protect my deadline, even though I don't have all my paperwork yet. Please note the date I reported this.

rules.title: A written warranty means the company behind it can't erase your basic "it has to work" right
rules.window_note: A "Limited" warranty is allowed to cut this promise short to match its own length, but only if it says so in clear words on the warranty. If it doesn't, most states give you about 4 years from the day the item was handed to you, which is often much longer than the printed warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A second, quieter promise on top of the printed warranty: the thing has to actually work for what it's normally used for. If a company gives you a written warranty, or sells you a service plan within 90 days, that company is not allowed to cancel this promise in the fine print.
rules.how_to_claim: When the maker says "sorry, out of warranty" but the thing died far too soon, check the warranty paper for a line that shortens the implied warranty. If there isn't one, write to the company that gave the warranty (or sold you the service plan) and say the item was never fit for normal use. Ask for a repair, refund or replacement. Small claims court is the backstop and you don't need a lawyer there.
rules.script_hint: This came with a written warranty, so under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act the implied warranty can't be disclaimed. This product didn't work the way this kind of product normally should.
rules.source_quote: implied warranties may be limited in duration to the duration of a written warranty of reasonable duration, if such limitation is conscionable and is set forth in clear and unmistakable language

rules.title: Stuff has to actually work — for about 4 years you can hold the store to it
rules.window_note: Almost every state gives you 4 years from the day the item was delivered to you - the clock starts at delivery, not at the day it broke. A contract can legally shorten it to as little as 1 year, so read the receipt. In most states a shop can also switch this promise off by clearly selling the item "as is" - unless it gave you its own written warranty. It does not cover damage from misuse, accidents, or normal wear.
rules.what_you_get: A repair, replacement or refund from the store even when there is no warranty paper at all, because the law says goods sold by a business have to be fit for the job they're sold for. It also covers used items bought from a business, unless they were clearly sold "as is".
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the store, not the maker. Put it in writing: what you bought, when, what it failed to do, and what you want. If they say no, small claims court is cheap, fast and lawyer-free.
rules.script_hint: This wasn't fit for the ordinary purpose it's sold for, so the store has broken the implied warranty of merchantability. I'd like a refund or a replacement.
rules.source_quote: Unless excluded or modified (Section 2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

rules.title: Some states don't let anyone sell you a dud "as is"
rules.window_note: Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, West Virginia, Kansas, Vermont and Washington DC. Same rough 4-year clock from the day you got it. Works on clearance items and floor models, and on used things bought from a business - except in Vermont, where the ban covers new or unused goods only. In Kansas and DC a shop can still exclude a specific defect it clearly told you about when you bought.
rules.what_you_get: In these places, "sold as is" and "no warranty" fine print simply doesn't work on consumer goods - a court will ignore it. The basic promise that the thing works stays with you no matter what the receipt says. In Kansas a judge can also make them pay your lawyer.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the store, not the maker. Tell them your state does not allow them to disclaim the implied warranty, and name your state's law. Keep the receipt and any photo of the "as is" sign.
rules.script_hint: "As is" isn't enforceable here - my state bans it on consumer goods (MA c.106 s.2-316A, MD Com. Law 2-316.1, ME 11 s.2-316(5), WV 46A-6-107, KS 50-639, VT 9A s.2-316(5), DC 28:2-316.01). The implied warranty still applies, so I'd like a refund.
rules.source_quote: The provisions of subsections (2), (3) and (4) of this section shall not apply to sales of new or unused consumer goods or services.

rules.title: If your warranty says FULL, repeated failures mean refund or replacement
rules.window_note: Only while the full warranty runs. Look at the top of your warranty paper — it has to say "Full" (like "Full One-Year Warranty"). If it says "Limited", this one doesn't apply to you. Write to them, list the dates of every failed repair, and say you are choosing a refund (or a replacement) because it's your choice under the law.
rules.what_you_get: After the company has had a fair number of tries and still can't fix it, you choose: your money back, or a brand new one. Free. They also can't charge you for the repair itself, and the only thing they're allowed to ask of you is that you tell them it's broken.
rules.how_to_claim: Count your repair attempts and find the dates. Call the warranty line, say how many times it has been in, and ask for the refund-or-replace choice in writing.
rules.script_hint: This is a Full warranty, so under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act, after a reasonable number of failed repairs I get to choose a refund or a free replacement. I'm choosing a refund.

rules.title: A FULL warranty follows the product, not the first buyer
rules.window_note: Only while the original Full warranty is still running, counted from when it was first sold new — not from when you bought it secondhand.
rules.what_you_get: If you bought it used and there is time left on a Full warranty, the free repair is yours too. You don't need to be the person whose name is on the original receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the maker's warranty line, give the serial number, and ask them to check warranty status by serial number. Serial number lookups are how they date the product without your receipt.
rules.script_hint: This has a Full warranty, and under the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act a Full warranty covers whoever owns the product, not just the first buyer. Here's the serial number.

rules.title: Not mailing the registration card doesn't cost you a Full warranty
rules.window_note: Any time the warranty is still running. The FTC rule covers warranties marked "Full" - look at the top of your warranty paper.
rules.what_you_get: If your warranty says "Full", it still counts even though you binned the little card or never registered online. They can ask for the card as proof of when you bought it, but they can't make it a condition of fixing your stuff. A "Limited" warranty is allowed to require registration, so check what yours says.
rules.how_to_claim: Claim as normal. If they say "you never registered", offer your receipt, bank statement or order email as proof of the purchase date instead, and point at the FTC rule.
rules.script_hint: My warranty is a Full warranty. The FTC's rule at 16 CFR 700.7 says making me return a registration card as a condition of service under a full warranty is an unreasonable duty. Here's my receipt for the purchase date.
rules.source_quote: A requirement that the consumer return a warranty registration card or a similar notice as a condition of performance under a full warranty is an unreasonable duty.

rules.title: California: the lemon law covers regular stuff, not just cars
rules.window_note: California only. Works while the written warranty is still running. Most people have never heard this applies to a fridge or a laptop, but it does. Ask the maker or the shop in writing for a repair under the Song-Beverly Act. If it ends up in court, you generally have about 4 years from the purchase date. Once it's past 30 days, or after two or three failed fixes, ask in writing for a replacement or a refund and attach your log. Warranty repairs have to be finished within 30 days, unless you agree in writing to wait longer.
rules.what_you_get: If the maker can't fix it after a fair number of tries, California law makes them replace it or hand back what you paid, minus a small amount for the use you already got out of it. Warranty repairs have to be finished within 30 days, unless you agree in writing to wait longer.
rules.how_to_claim: Keep every repair ticket — dates matter more than anything else here. Then write to the maker, not the store, list the dates it went in for the same fault, and ask for a replacement or a refund.
rules.script_hint: Under California Civil Code 1793.2(d)(1), after a reasonable number of repair attempts you have to replace this or refund me. Here are the repair dates.

rules.title: California: warranty repairs are supposed to be finished in 30 days
rules.window_note: California only. Applies to any repair being done under a written warranty. The clock can stretch if something outside the maker's control holds it up, like a genuine parts shortage.
rules.what_you_get: A deadline you can actually hold them to. If your stuff has been sitting at the repair centre past 30 days, that's a broken legal promise and it's your best lever for asking for a replacement instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Count the days from when you handed it over. Email the maker and the repair centre with the drop-off date in writing and ask for a completion date.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1793.2(b) says warranty repairs must be finished within 30 days. It's been 45. When is it going back together, or are we talking about a replacement?

rules.title: California: your warranty clock pauses while the thing is in the shop
rules.window_note: California only, for things that cost $50 or more. The pause starts the day you hand it over for repair (or, if it can't reasonably be brought in, like something too big or built in, the day you tell them it's broken) and ends the day you get it back or they tell you it's ready.
rules.what_you_get: Free extra warranty days. Every day your product spends waiting for or getting a warranty repair does not count against your warranty — so a six-week repair pushes your expiry date six weeks later.
rules.how_to_claim: Keep the work order or receipt showing the drop-off date and the date you got it back. When the maker later says you're out of warranty, add those days back on and show them the paperwork.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1795.6 pauses the warranty while the product is being repaired. You had it from March 3rd to April 20th, so my warranty runs 48 days longer than your system says.
rules.source_quote: warranty period relating to an implied or express warranty accompanying a sale or consignment for sale of consumer goods selling for fifty dollars ($50) or more shall automatically be tolled

rules.title: California: a hidden safety net that can run a full year
rules.window_note: California only, on new goods. It lasts as long as the written warranty, but never less than 60 days and never more than 1 year from the day you bought it. So a 30-day warranty doesn't leave you bare on day 31: you're covered to at least day 60.
rules.what_you_get: A basic "it has to work" promise that runs alongside the printed warranty. It lasts as long as the printed warranty, but never less than 60 days and never more than a year, even when the maker only gave you 30 days.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to the store or the maker inside that year and say the item wasn't fit to use. Put it in writing. California small claims court is cheap and you're not allowed to bring a lawyer, so the company can't out-lawyer you.
rules.script_hint: California Civil Code 1791.1(c) gives me an implied warranty on new consumer goods that lasts as long as your written warranty and never less than 60 days, so I'm still covered. This wasn't fit for normal use.
rules.source_quote: shall be coextensive in duration with an express warranty which accompanies the consumer goods ... but in no event shall such implied warranty have a duration of less than 60 days nor more than one year

rules.title: Minnesota: parts, tools and manuals within 60 days of a product's launch
rules.window_note: Minnesota only, for gear sold on or after 1 July 2021. Cars, medical devices, farm and construction gear, power tools, lawn and garden gear, game consoles and home battery systems are left out. Minnesota's version covers appliances, which New York's does not. The tools you can get include software updates needed for the repair.
rules.what_you_get: You or an independent shop can buy the parts and tools and get the repair documents on fair terms — and the maker has to have them ready within 60 days of the product first going on sale in Minnesota.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the maker, or have your repair shop ask, for the specific part, tool or manual. Keep any refusal in writing — refusing breaks Minnesota's deceptive trade practices law, so report it to the Minnesota Attorney General.
rules.script_hint: Minnesota Statute 325E.72 requires you to make this documentation, part or tool available to me on fair and reasonable terms. Please confirm in writing if you're refusing.
rules.source_quote: Nothing in this section applies to manufacturers, distributors, importers, or dealers of any off-road or nonroad equipment, including without limitation ... turf, yard, and garden equipment; outdoor power equipment; portable generators; ... power tools

rules.title: Paid by credit card? The law lets you hand the fight to your card company
rules.window_note: Credit cards only — not debit, not cash. The law itself sets no hard deadline, but card companies get strict fast, so call within a couple of months of giving up on the seller. Normally the purchase has to be over $50 and made in your home state or within 100 miles of your address, though that limit drops away if the card company and the seller are connected.
rules.what_you_get: The right to stop paying your card company for something a seller sold you broken and won't put right. You raise the same complaint against the card company that you had against the shop. It only covers what you still owed on that purchase when you first complained to the shop or the card company, so complain before you pay it off.
rules.how_to_claim: First genuinely try the seller and keep proof that you tried — emails, chat logs, a call log. Then ring the number on the back of your card and use the exact wording below, because "claims and defenses" is routed differently inside the bank than a plain disputed charge.
rules.script_hint: I'm asserting my claims and defenses under section 170 of the Truth in Lending Act and Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(c). The merchant sold me a defective product and won't fix it, and I've made a good faith attempt to resolve it with them.
rules.source_quote: The cardholder may withhold payment up to the amount of credit outstanding for the property or services that gave rise to the dispute and any finance or other charges imposed on that amount.

rules.title: Whirlpool, Maytag, KitchenAid or IKEA bottom-freezer fridge that ices up and leaks onto the floor
rules.window_note: Only the Group B models on the settlement's list, with serial numbers from VS141 to VS827. The fridge has to be less than 5 years old when it ices up, and you need to report it within 90 days. The whole thing shuts on 31 December 2026.
rules.what_you_get: A free new drain tube part, and Whirlpool pays the repair bill: all of it in years 1 to 3, then all the parts plus 65% of the labour in year 4, and all the parts plus half the labour in year 5.
rules.how_to_claim: Ring Whirlpool's special service line on 1-888-900-7957 and report it. A Whirlpool engineer has to see it, so book the visit through that number rather than calling your own repair person.
rules.script_hint: I'd like to report a Future Freezing Event under the Corzine v. Whirlpool settlement. Ice built up in my freezer, the drain froze, and water ran out onto my floor. My model is on the Group B list.
rules.source_quote: 100% of parts and 65% of labor costs for Qualifying Repairs you paid for in year four (4) after purchase; and 100% of parts and 50% of labor costs for Qualifying Repairs you paid for in year five (5)

rules.title: Keurig K-Supreme coffee maker that died while you were descaling it
rules.window_note: You need to have bought a K-Supreme, K-Supreme Plus or K-Supreme SMART between 1 October 2020 and 20 June 2025. If it lost power for good while descaling after 20 June 2025, you have until 30 September 2027 to claim. If it died before then, that deadline passed on 14 November 2025.
rules.what_you_get: 12 more months of Keurig's warranty for one fault: the machine losing power for good while you descale it. That means Keurig has to repair or replace it for free instead of you buying a new one.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at ksupremesettlement.com. Say your machine permanently lost power during descaling and that you want the extended warranty.
rules.script_hint: I own a K-Supreme and it permanently lost power while I was descaling it, following Keurig's own instructions. I'm in the Coffee Maker Purchaser Class in the Cahill v. Keurig settlement and I'm claiming the 12-month extended warranty.
rules.source_quote: Keurig will provide an additional 12-month extended Limited Warranty for claims that a defect caused an operational issue that resulted in a permanent loss of power to the subject Coffee Maker(s) as a result of the descaling process.

rules.title: Toyota with the airbag control unit that could fail in a crash
rules.window_note: Covers 2011-2019 Corolla, 2011-2013 Corolla Matrix, 2012-2018 Avalon, 2013-2018 Avalon HV, 2012-2019 Tacoma, 2012-2017 Tundra and 2012-2017 Sequoia. You have until 11 December 2028, so this one is not urgent.
rules.what_you_get: Money back for what this cost you out of pocket, a cash payment, a free loaner car while the work is done, a free inspection, and a longer warranty on the new parts.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to airbagcontrolunitsettlement.com, put your VIN in the lookup tool, then submit the claim form online or by post.
rules.script_hint: I own a Toyota listed in the ZF-TRW airbag control unit settlement. I'd like to file a claim for my out-of-pocket costs and the extended parts warranty.

rules.title: Kia Optima or Sportage where a window won't roll up or down
rules.window_note: Covers certain 2016-2017 Kia Optima and all 2017 Kia Sportage cars. How much you get back depends on the mileage when the window broke, not on how long ago you bought it. Closes 23 November 2026.
rules.what_you_get: Up to $400 back for each window you paid to fix, up to four windows on one car. You get 100% back under 35,000 miles, sliding down to 40% over 125,000 miles. If you still own the car you can take a $40 dealer service card instead.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to kiawindowregulatorsettlement.com, check your VIN, then upload the repair invoice showing you paid for a window regulator replacement.
rules.script_hint: I paid out of pocket to replace a window regulator on my Kia, which is a class vehicle in the Le Beau v. Kia settlement. Here is my invoice and my mileage at the time.

rules.title: Honda or Acura whose engine won't restart after Auto Idle Stop
rules.window_note: Covers 2015-2020 Acura TLX, 2016-2020 Acura MDX, 2016-2021 Honda Pilot, 2019-2021 Honda Passport and 2020-2021 Honda Ridgeline. Free repairs run for 10 years from when the car was first sold new, with an extra 24 months for 2015 TLX and an extra 18 months for 2016 TLX, MDX and Pilot. Towing costs must be claimed within 60 days of paying them.
rules.what_you_get: A free starter replacement or valve adjustment at a Honda or Acura dealer. If your car has already had the Auto Idle Stop software update, the dealer can't make you prove the fault in front of them before replacing the starter for free. Towing costs get paid back too.
rules.how_to_claim: Book your car into an authorised Honda or Acura dealer and ask for the Auto Idle Stop repair under the service bulletin. Do not let them turn you away for not being able to reproduce the fault.
rules.script_hint: My car is covered by the Honda Idle Stop settlement and it's still inside the warranty extension. It has already had the software update, so under the settlement you can't require me to reproduce the no-restart symptom before doing the free starter replacement.
rules.source_quote: if your Class Vehicle has already received a software update, the dealership cannot require that they verify the AIS symptom is present in your vehicle for a free starter replacement

rules.title: Subaru where the EyeSight auto-braking or lane-keeping stopped working
rules.window_note: Covers certain 2013-2024 Subarus with EyeSight. The extra cover runs for 4 years or 48,000 miles from the day the car went into service, whichever comes first. It moves with the car, so it still counts if you bought it used. Claims for repairs you already paid for closed on 27 September 2025 — this is only for repairs you get done now.
rules.what_you_get: Subaru pays 75% of the repair bill when the EyeSight camera or the rear sonar sensor makes the pre-collision braking, rear auto braking or lane-keep assist stop working.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN on eyesightsettlement.com, then take the car to an authorised Subaru dealer and ask them to do the repair under the settlement's warranty extension.
rules.script_hint: My VIN is a class vehicle in the Subaru EyeSight settlement, and I'm still inside the 4-year, 48,000-mile warranty extension. Please book this repair under that extension so 75% is covered.

rules.title: VW Atlas or Atlas Cross Sport with a failed water pump
rules.window_note: Covers 2018-2022 Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport with the 3.6 litre engine. The extra cover runs 8.5 years or 85,000 miles from the day the car went into service. Claims for repairs you already paid for close on 5 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: 80% of what a water pump repair costs. If you used a non-VW garage, the payout is capped at $820 for the water pump or $3,325 for a head gasket.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your VIN on the settlement website, then send the signed claim form with your repair invoices to the administrator so it's postmarked by 5 October 2026.
rules.script_hint: My VW Atlas has the 3.6 litre engine and is covered by the main engine water pump settlement. I paid out of pocket for a water pump repair and I'm claiming the 80% reimbursement.
rules.source_quote: eight and a half years or 85,000 miles, whichever occurs first, from the car's in-service date

rules.title: Bestway, Power Steel, Steel Pro or Coleman above-ground pool (48 inches or taller)
rules.window_note: Covers pools sold from 2008 through 2024 that are 48 inches tall or more with the straps running on the outside of the legs. No time limit from when you bought it, but everything closes on 30 October 2026.
rules.what_you_get: $40 in cash with no receipt at all, or 10% of what you actually paid if you still have the receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at poolsettlementbw.com. You don't need a receipt for the $40 — you just sign to say you bought one.
rules.script_hint: I bought a Bestway above-ground pool that's 48 inches or taller with the compression straps on the outside of the legs. I'm filing a claim without proof of purchase.

rules.title: Sanyo solar panels on your house that are peeling apart
rules.window_note: Covers Sanyo HIP-xxxBA2, BA3 and BA5 panels sold for homes, roughly 2001 to 2010. You have until 20 years after they were bought, or 31 December 2029, whichever comes first. It counts even if the panels came with the house when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: A free new or refurbished panel to replace each bad one, or cash based on what the panel originally cost minus wear. A panel bought 10 years ago for $700 pays about $350.
rules.how_to_claim: Take clear photos of the peeling, then email the claim form, photos and proof you own the panels to sanyosolarclaims@4class.com. The form is on sanyosolarclaims.com.
rules.script_hint: I own Sanyo HIP-series solar panels that are delaminating. I'm filing a claim under the Ziccarello v. Sanyo settlement, with photos of the circular delamination.

rules.title: CertainTeed Horizon roof shingles that are failing
rules.window_note: Covers buildings in the US where CertainTeed Fiberglass Horizon shingles were put on between 1995 and 2010. You have until 2 March 2030, so there's no rush.
rules.what_you_get: A cash payment if your roof shingles show the kind of damage the settlement covers.
rules.how_to_claim: Start the claim at ctroof.com, or post the claim form to the Horizon Settlement Administrator, 805 W. 5th Street, Suite 7, Lansdale, PA 19446. You'll need to show the damage.
rules.script_hint: My building has CertainTeed Fiberglass Horizon shingles installed between 1995 and 2010, and they're showing qualifying damage. I'm filing a claim under the Segebarth v. CertainTeed settlement.

rules.title: Pixel Care+ pays $0 for a battery under 80%
rules.window_note: While your Pixel Care+ cover is running: 24 months on the 2-year plan, or up to 60 months if you pay monthly. It is only sold in the US, the UK and Japan, and only works in the country you bought it in.
rules.what_you_get: A new battery at zero cost if yours holds less than 80% of its original charge. Screens and back glass are $0 on the same plan.
rules.how_to_claim: Check Pixel battery health in Settings, then Battery. Google says a Pixel 8a or later should still hold 80% at around 1000 charges, and a Pixel 3 to 8 Pro at around 800 charges. If you are under 80% and you have Pixel Care+, start a repair through Google Store support and say it is a Pixel Care+ battery claim. Without Pixel Care+, the plain warranty only pays out for a battery that is actually defective, not one that has simply aged.
rules.script_hint: My Pixel battery holds less than 80% of its original capacity and I have Pixel Care+, so this should be a $0 battery replacement.
rules.source_quote: Pixel Care+ is Google's insurance protection program. It is available in Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

rules.title: Milwaukee tools get 5 years, the batteries only 2 or 3
rules.window_note: It depends on the pack: some, like 48-11-1850 or 48-11-2440, get 3 years from purchase, while others, like 48-11-1820 or 48-11-2420, get only 2. The tool itself is usually 5 years, and Milwaukee hand tools are lifetime. If you have no receipt they go by the manufacturing date. You do not have to register the tool first.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement battery pack if it fails inside the battery's own shorter window.
rules.how_to_claim: Find the pack's catalogue number printed on the battery (like 48-11-1850) and look it up on Milwaukee's warranty page to get its exact years. Then take the pack and your receipt to a Milwaukee authorised service centre. Do not assume the tool's 5 years covers it.
rules.script_hint: I know the battery pack has its own warranty length, separate from the tool. Can you check the coverage on catalogue number [number]?

rules.title: DeWalt 20V MAX battery packs carry 3 years
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase or delivery, whichever is later. There is also a 90 day money back window if you simply are not happy with it.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement of a battery pack that failed from faulty materials or workmanship.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the pack and proof of purchase to a DeWalt factory service centre or authorised service centre. Say it is a 3 year limited warranty claim. If you are still inside 90 days and just unhappy with the runtime, ask for the money back guarantee instead, which is easier to win.
rules.script_hint: This battery is under three years old and it has failed. I'm claiming under the 3 Year Limited Warranty.

rules.title: Ryobi gives batteries 3 years but accessories only 90 days
rules.window_note: 3 years from purchase for Ryobi power tools, 18V ONE+ outdoor tools and batteries. 40V outdoor tools used at home get 5 years, with 3 years on their batteries. Power tool accessories are only 90 days, so claim those fast.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or replacement for a tool or battery with a workmanship or materials fault.
rules.how_to_claim: Register or find your proof of purchase, then contact Ryobi support or take it to an authorised service centre. Ask them to confirm which bucket your item falls in, because a battery gets 3 years while a blade or attachment may only get 90 days.
rules.script_hint: This is a Ryobi battery, which carries the three year warranty, not the ninety day accessory warranty.
rules.source_quote: 5 Year Tool / 3 Year Battery / 3 Year Charger - Five years for the tool, three years for the battery and chanrger if the product is used for personal, family or household use

rules.title: Toyota hybrid batteries get 10 years, and it follows the car
rules.window_note: For 2020 model year and newer Toyota hybrid, plug-in hybrid and fuel cell vehicles: 10 years from the date the car was first used, or 150,000 miles, whichever lands first. Older ones are 8 years or 100,000 miles.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement hybrid battery pack, the single most expensive part on the car.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the car to any Toyota dealer service department with the VIN. Ask them to check the Hybrid Battery Warranty specifically, because that one runs longer than the Hybrid System Warranty that covers the other high voltage parts. If you bought the car second hand, say so anyway, because this coverage carries over to every later owner at no cost.
rules.script_hint: This is a 2020 or newer Toyota hybrid, so the hybrid battery is covered for 10 years or 150,000 miles, and that coverage transfers to me as a later owner.
rules.source_quote: Toyota announced it will extend its hybrid battery warranty from 8 years / 100,000 miles to 10 years from date of first use/150,000 miles, whichever comes first.

rules.title: A cracked screen is never a warranty claim, but it can be $29
rules.window_note: While your AppleCare+ plan is running. Monthly and yearly plans keep going until you cancel. The plain one year warranty never covers a drop, no matter how new the device is.
rules.what_you_get: A screen or back glass repair for a $29 fee, or other accidental damage for $99, with no cap on how many times.
rules.how_to_claim: Check whether you actually have AppleCare+ under Settings, General, About, Coverage. If you do, book the repair and expect to pay the $29 service fee for screen or back glass, or $99 for other accident damage. If you do not have AppleCare+, stop here: the standard warranty covers manufacturing faults only, so a drop or a crack will be quoted at full price.
rules.script_hint: I have AppleCare+, so this should be the $29 screen repair service fee, not a full price screen replacement.
rules.source_quote: Damaged displays, back glass, or Ceramic Shield can be repaired as often as you need for a low fee — often in the same day. $29 service fee

rules.title: EU: shop finance can make the lender your back-up
rules.window_note: Only for credit that paid for this one purchase and is tied to the shop: the shop gave you the credit itself, the lender used the shop to set it up, or the credit agreement names the item. Under the EU rule a normal credit card you can use for anything does not count, because it is not only for this purchase. The EU rule also leaves out credit under €200 or over €75,000, credit with no interest and no other charges, and credit you must pay back within three months with only tiny charges. You must try the seller first and fail before you can turn to the lender. Your own country's law sets the details, such as how long you have, and may give you more. For credit taken out from 20 November 2026, newer EU rules also cover amounts under €200 or up to €100,000, and interest-free plans from a separate lender.
rules.what_you_get: If a shop-linked loan paid for your item and it never arrived, only partly arrived, or is faulty, you can take your claim to the lender once the seller has failed to give you what the law or your contract says you are owed.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the shop first and keep proof they did not put it right. Then write to the finance company, explain that the credit was a linked credit agreement for that purchase, and ask them to put things right.
rules.script_hint: This was a linked credit agreement for these goods, and the seller has not given me the remedy I am entitled to. Under Article 15(2) of the Consumer Credit Directive (2008/48/EC), as it applies in our national law, I am now pursuing my claim against you as the lender.
rules.source_quote: Where the goods or services covered by a linked credit agreement are not supplied, or are supplied only in part, or are not in conformity with the contract for the supply thereof, the consumer shall have the right to pursue remedies against the creditor if the consumer has pursued his remedies against the supplier but has failed to obtain the satisfaction to which he is entitled according to the law or the contract for the supply of goods or services.

rules.title: EU: free legal help when the shop is in another country
rules.window_note: No deadline of its own, but they can only help while your underlying rights are still alive, so go early rather than late.
rules.what_you_get: The European Consumer Centres Network is a government-backed service with 29 centres, one in every EU country plus Norway and Iceland. About 150 legal experts take up your case with a shop in another of those countries, in your own language, completely free. Useful when a foreign online seller ignores you.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to eccnet.eu, choose the centre for the country you live in, and send them your case with the receipt and the messages the shop ignored.
rules.script_hint: I bought this from a trader in another EU country, they will not honour the legal guarantee, and I would like your centre to take up my case.
rules.source_quote: 29 centres, based in every EU member state, as well as in Norway and Iceland.

rules.title: Quebec: cancelled an online order for a reason the law allows and got no refund? Your card issuer must reverse the charge
rules.window_note: Each step has its own clock. First, cancel with the seller. If the item has not come 30 days after the delivery date in the contract, or 30 days after you bought it when no date was set, you can cancel any time before it arrives. If you agreed in writing to a later date, count the 30 days from that later date. If the seller tried to deliver on the agreed date and could not because of something you did or did not do, the law treats the delivery as done, so you cannot cancel for late delivery. If the seller left out required information before you bought, did not let you check and fix your order, or sent a contract copy that is missing things or hard to save and print, you have 7 days after you get the copy. If you only notice the missing information when the item or your card statement arrives, the 7 days start then. If no copy came within 15 days of buying, you have 30 days from the purchase. Next, the seller has 15 days to refund you. If they do not, you have 60 days after that to ask your card issuer.
rules.what_you_get: This covers things you bought at a distance, for example online or by phone, and paid for by credit card. If you cancelled for one of the reasons the law allows and the seller does not refund you within 15 days, your card issuer must take the charge back when you ask in writing. The issuer must confirm it got your request within 30 days. It must put the money back within 90 days or within two full statement periods, whichever comes first. Some purchases are left out, such as food or other goods that spoil quickly and things bought at an auction.
rules.how_to_claim: First check that your reason is one the law gives, then send the seller a cancellation notice, for example by email or registered mail, and keep proof you sent it. If you already have the item, send it back within 15 days of cancelling, or of getting it if it arrives after you cancel. The seller pays reasonable return costs. If no refund comes within 15 days, send your card issuer a written chargeback request naming section 54.14 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. Include your name, card number and expiry date, the seller's name, the purchase date, the amount, what you bought, why you cancelled, and the date and way you sent the cancellation. Quebec's consumer protection office has a sample letter you can copy. Send it in a way you can prove, and keep a copy.
rules.script_hint: I cancelled this distance purchase under Quebec's Consumer Protection Act and the seller did not refund me within 15 days. Under section 54.14, please charge back all amounts I paid under this contract and cancel all related charges on my account.
rules.source_quote: If the merchant defaults on the obligation to make a refund under section 54.13 and the consumer has paid by credit card, the consumer may, within 60 days following the default, request the card issuer to chargeback all amounts paid under the contract and any accessory contract, and to cancel all charges made to the consumer’s account in relation to those contracts.

rules.title: CIBC card: warranty doubled, nothing to sign up for
rules.window_note: The extra cover starts the day the maker's warranty ends and lasts as long again, up to one extra full year. Tell them within 45 days of the loss, theft or damage, then send the completed paperwork within 90 days.
rules.what_you_get: Many CIBC credit cards double the manufacturer's warranty for up to one extra full year at no cost and with no sign-up, on most items bought anywhere in the world, as long as at least part of the price went on the card and the maker's warranty is honoured in Canada or the US. They only pay back the part you charged, and you must live in Canada. Damage or theft in the first 90 days is covered too.
rules.how_to_claim: Call 1-866-363-3338 free from Canada and the US, or 905-403-3338 collect, as soon as the item fails, and ask for the claim forms. Keep the store receipt, the card statement and the original manufacturer's warranty.
rules.script_hint: I am claiming under CIBC's Purchase Security and Extended Protection insurance. The manufacturer's warranty has expired and the item has failed inside the doubled term.
rules.source_quote: Extended Protection automatically provides you, without registration, with double the term of the manufacturer’s warranty up to a maximum of one additional full year ... when at least a portion of the purchase price is charged to the card

rules.title: Lodge replaces cracked or warped cast iron free, with no end date
rules.window_note: No deadline. It lasts as long as you own the pan, and it counts if the pan was a gift to you. It stops if you buy the pan second-hand, and it does not cover restaurant use.
rules.what_you_get: A brand new pan, free, if your bare cast iron or carbon steel cracks or warps, or came out of the factory with a hole or bad casting. Enamelled pieces are covered for chips and cracks that happen while you are cooking normally. It will not cover rust, a sticky pan, or damage from dropping it, overheating it, or putting it in the dishwasher.
rules.how_to_claim: Go to Lodge's warranty page and fill in the form for your type of pan. They will usually ask for photos of the damage first. If they want the pan back, Lodge pays the postage.
rules.script_hint: My Lodge pan cracked during normal cooking and I would like it replaced under the Made Right warranty.

rules.title: All-Clad pans, knives and bakeware carry a limited lifetime warranty
rules.window_note: No end date, but you have to be the person who bought it, it must have come from All-Clad or a shop All-Clad has approved, and you need proof of purchase.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a replacement if the metal, the construction or the workmanship was faulty. It will not cover misuse, or damage from ignoring the care instructions.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact All-Clad's Consumer Service team by phone or through their website. They check the claim and give you a return number before you send anything. Keep the receipt — they can refuse a claim without one.
rules.script_hint: This pan is covered by All-Clad's limited lifetime warranty and it has failed. Here is my proof of purchase.
rules.source_quote: Should your All-Clad cookware require warranty service, please contact our Consumer Service Department by phone or website per below for a warranty evaluation and return authorization number.

rules.title: Zwilling knives are covered for as long as you own them
rules.window_note: It lasts for as long as you own the knife. But you must have proof you bought it — a receipt, an order email, a shop invoice, or a card or bank statement showing the purchase. No proof, no claim.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement knife or tool if yours was faulty in the metal or the making. Zwilling does not repair anything — they send you a new one, and you do not get the old one back. Normal wear from use, and blades you have blunted or damaged, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Submit a claim through Zwilling's online Support Center with your proof of purchase. Do not take it to a Zwilling shop — shops cannot process claims. Never send in a knife you are attached to, because it will not come back.
rules.script_hint: My Zwilling knife has a fault in the material. Here is my proof of purchase — I would like a replacement under the limited warranty.
rules.source_quote: This warranty applies only to products purchased in the United States from Zwilling or a Zwilling authorized seller located in the United States

rules.title: Cutco sharpens your knives free forever, and fixes or replaces anything that stops performing
rules.window_note: Forever, and it travels with the knife. If you were given the knives, inherited them, or they were handed down, they are still covered. Home use only.
rules.what_you_get: Free sharpening whenever your knives get dull, plus a free fix or a replacement if any Cutco product stops performing properly. Sharpening itself costs nothing — you only pay return postage, which is $15 for 1 to 5 items and goes up in steps for larger batches.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in a service request on Cutco's website, print the confirmation, and post your knives with it: to Cutco in Olean, New York if you live in the US, or to Cutco in London, Ontario if you live in Canada. Allow a few weeks once they have them.
rules.script_hint: These Cutco knives were passed down to me and need sharpening. The Forever Guarantee covers them even though I was not the original buyer.
rules.source_quote: Mailing Address Cutco Customer Service 7-2351 Huron St. London, ON N5V 0A8

rules.title: Craftsman swaps a broken hand tool for a new one, for any reason, with no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever, and no receipt is needed. Old Craftsman tools with model numbers starting with 9 get exactly the same deal as the new CMHT and CMMT ones, so tools from a parent's or grandparent's toolbox still count.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement tool. Craftsman's own wording is that if the tool fails to perform for any reason, they will replace it. This covers hammers and demolition tools, screwdrivers, pliers, hex keys, nut drivers, wrenches, ratchets and sockets, and whole mechanics tool sets.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the broken tool to a shop that stocks Craftsman and ask for a warranty swap over the counter, or ring Craftsman Customer Care and they will sort it out. Do not throw the broken tool away.
rules.script_hint: This Craftsman hand tool has the full lifetime warranty and it failed. No proof of purchase is required — I would like a replacement.
rules.source_quote: Note : Same warranty for all new CRAFTSMAN® models (Model # starting with CMHT) and older models (Model # starting with 9). No proof of purchase required.

rules.title: DeWalt replaces mechanics tools that ever fail, for any reason, no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever, and no proof of purchase is needed. This full lifetime warranty covers wrenches, sockets, ratchets and drive accessories. Other DeWalt hand tools only have a limited lifetime warranty, for the first owner. Most people forget this one entirely.
rules.what_you_get: A free replacement tool posted out to you. DeWalt's words are that if a DeWalt Mechanics Tool ever fails for any reason, they will replace it. Their hand tools other than mechanics tools have a narrower promise that only covers faults in the material or the making.
rules.how_to_claim: Do not take it back to the shop — DeWalt say not to. Ring DeWalt Customer Care instead and they will ship a replacement to you.
rules.script_hint: This is a DeWalt mechanics tool with the full lifetime warranty. It failed, and I understand no proof of purchase is required.
rules.source_quote: If any DEWALT Mechanics Tool ever fails for any reason, DEWALT will replace it. NO PROOF OF PURCHASE required. DO NOT RETURN PRODUCT TO STORE.

rules.title: Milwaukee hand tools carry a limited lifetime warranty
rules.window_note: Lasts the lifetime of the tool, for the first owner, as long as you bought it from a shop Milwaukee has approved. Keep your receipt if you can — Milwaukee says it helps them check the claim.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, of a hand tool that turns out to have a fault in the material or the way it was made. It will not cover a tool you wore out, misused, changed, did not look after, or damaged in an accident. Milwaukee power tools and batteries are different and have much shorter windows.
rules.how_to_claim: Find a Milwaukee service centre on their website and post or drop the tool off. You pay to get it there.
rules.script_hint: This Milwaukee hand tool has a limited lifetime warranty and it has a fault in the way it was made. I would like it repaired or replaced.
rules.source_quote: MILWAUKEE will repair or replace any hand tool which, after examination, is determined by MILWAUKEE to be defective in material or workmanship for the lifetime of the tool.

rules.title: Estwing will replace an all-steel hammer that fails in normal use — but it is not a lifetime warranty
rules.window_note: There is no fixed end date on the all-steel hammers, but Estwing say in plain print on their own site that this is NOT a lifetime warranty. Their titanium hammers are only covered for 1 year, and that one cannot be passed to a new owner.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement hammer if the steel failed while you were using it the way it was meant to be used. Estwing will refuse claims for a hammer that simply wore out, got dented in the handle neck from over-striking, or was used on hardened steel like chisels or cat's paws.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it back to the shop you bought it from first. If you cannot reach them, ring Estwing customer service. Estwing cannot repair or re-grip a used hammer, so a fair claim ends in a replacement.
rules.script_hint: My Estwing all-steel hammer failed in normal use and I would like to make a fair claim.
rules.source_quote: If you feel you have a fair claim, contact your Estwing retailer. If you cannot reach your Estwing retailer, please call Estwing customer service at 815-397-9558.

rules.title: JanSport backpacks have a lifetime warranty on zips, buckles and seams
rules.window_note: Runs for the lifetime of the bag, for the first owner. It covers packs, bags, pouches, totes and cases. It does not cover JanSport clothing, hats, pins or patches, and cooler bags only get 5 years.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, if a zip, buckle, fabric or seam failed because of how the bag was made. Normal wear, faded colour, spills and accidents are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty form on JanSport's site, or ring or email them. In Canada, start your claim on JanSport's Canadian site, jansport.ca, instead. Then post the bag in, washed, because they charge for cleaning or send it back dirty. You pay to send it; they pay to send it home. Allow 3 to 4 weeks.
rules.script_hint: The zip on my JanSport pack has failed. I would like to claim the lifetime warranty on manufacturing defects.
rules.source_quote: For Warranty Questions outside of the United States or Canada please see the International JanSport section specific to your region for further information on who to contact

rules.title: Eagle Creek's No Matter What warranty covers faults for the life of the bag
rules.window_note: It runs for the usable life of the bag — not for your lifetime. Eagle Creek are open about the difference: once wheels, handles or zips have simply worn out from years of use rather than failing from a fault, the bag has reached the end of its life and the cover stops. First owner only.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a credit toward a new bag, if a zip, wheel, handle or seam was faulty in the materials or the workmanship. Lost or stolen bags, and damage to what was inside, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty request form on Eagle Creek's site. You pay to ship it to one of their repair centres, and they cover the parts, the labour and the trip home. In Canada, claims go through Eagle Creek's Canadian distributor, In-Sport Fashions. Start from the Warranty page on insport.ca. Ask about a DIY repair kit first: wheels, buckles and small parts are often quicker to fix yourself.
rules.script_hint: The wheel on my Eagle Creek bag failed from a defect, not from wear. I would like to claim the No Matter What warranty.
rules.source_quote: The lifetime of the product is the period during which the item can reasonably be expected to remain in usable condition, with proper care, for its intended purpose. It is not based on the owner's lifetime.

rules.title: Tortuga covers build faults for the practical life of the bag
rules.window_note: Runs for the practical life of the bag, for the first owner. Tortuga say faults are rare and usually show up in the first few uses, so check a new bag early.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement bag or store credit if the materials, hardware or construction were faulty in a way that stops the bag working. Airline damage is not covered — claim that from the airline instead. Once the bag is genuinely worn out, Tortuga will point you to a repair partner to keep it going.
rules.how_to_claim: Email Tortuga with photos of the problem and your order number.
rules.script_hint: There is a defect in the hardware on my Tortuga bag. Photos and my order number are attached — I would like to claim the Worldwide Warranty.

rules.title: The North Face covers build faults for the working life of the item
rules.window_note: Runs for the practical, reasonably expected life of the item, not a set number of years, and only for the first owner. Footwear and items from The North Face Renewed only get a 1-year warranty.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement, if a seam, zip or fabric failed because of the way it was made. Accidents, poor care, normal wear and colours fading over time are not covered. Only original, unaltered items count.
rules.how_to_claim: Send the item in for warranty assessment through The North Face's warranty page. They may ask for proof of purchase, so dig out the receipt or order email if you can.
rules.script_hint: The seam on this jacket has failed from a manufacturing defect. I would like it assessed under the Limited Lifetime Warranty.
rules.source_quote: Footwear and products from our The North Face Renewed series are covered by a One-Year Warranty which covers manufacturing defects in materials and workmanship for the first year following purchase.

rules.title: Darn Tough replaces worn-through socks free, forever, with no receipt
rules.window_note: Forever. There is no time limit, no registration and no receipt needed — Darn Tough knit their name into every sock, so the sock itself is the proof. You can send several pairs in on one claim.
rules.what_you_get: A credit code by email for the full value of a new pair, which you spend on their site with free shipping. It covers socks that have worn through with holes, or been damaged by accident, as long as there is enough left to tell they are Darn Tough. Seconds and irregulars, and socks you have dyed or altered, are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the claim form at warranty.darntough.com, wash the socks, put the printed form in the parcel and post them back. Processing usually takes a week or two.
rules.script_hint: These Darn Tough socks have worn through. I am claiming the unconditional lifetime guarantee — no receipt is needed.

rules.title: Smartwool gives you two years to be unhappy with anything you bought
rules.window_note: Two years from the day you bought it. This one is NOT for life, so check the date on the receipt before you count on it. Items bought second-hand through thredUP, or from a seller Smartwool have not authorised, do not qualify.
rules.what_you_get: A digital gift card for the value, so you can pick something new yourself. In the US you usually do not even have to post the old item back any more.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the Smartwool Product Guarantee Form on their site and upload four photos: the whole item, a close-up of the problem, and your receipt or order confirmation. File a separate claim for each item.
rules.script_hint: I bought these within the last two years and I am not happy with how they have held up. I would like to use the Smartwool guarantee.

rules.title: Zippo fixes any windproof lighter free, however old it is
rules.window_note: For the life of the lighter, on Zippo windproof pocket lighters. Decades-old lighters still qualify and no receipt is needed. Their other products — butane lighters, hand warmers, multipurpose lighters — are handled under separate, shorter terms.
rules.what_you_get: Your lighter repaired free. Zippo's own promise is 'It works or we fix it free.' The finish and decoration are not covered — if they wear off in the first year, contact Zippo to ask what they can do.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the repair form for windproof lighters in Zippo's help centre and post the lighter to their repair clinic in Bradford, Pennsylvania.
rules.script_hint: My Zippo windproof lighter has stopped working. I am sending it in under the 'it works or we fix it free' lifetime warranty.
rules.source_quote: The finish and decoration on a Zippo Windproof Lighter are not covered by the lifetime guarantee.

rules.title: Leatherman multi-tools carry a 25-year warranty
rules.window_note: 25 years from the day you got it, for the first owner only. On the US site, Leatherman Insider members get 40 years. It is long, but it is not forever, so work out how old the tool is.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair. If they cannot fix it, you get a comparable refurbished tool instead, and old or limited models may be swapped for an equivalent one. Owners of MagnaCut blades also get free sharpening. Rust, finishes, most sheaths, and damage from misuse are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Fill in the warranty form on Leatherman's site (in Canada, use ca.leatherman.com), print the packing slip, and post the tool in using a tracked, insured service. They pay to send it back. Allow about two to three weeks. In Canada it can take up to three weeks longer, because Canadian claims are gathered up and sent on to Leatherman in Oregon.
rules.script_hint: This Leatherman is inside its 25-year warranty and a tool on it has failed. I would like it repaired or replaced.
rules.source_quote: If we can't repair it, we'll replace it with a comparable refurbished model, unless you've specified otherwise in your form.

rules.title: Victorinox covers Swiss Army knives and kitchen knives for their lifetime
rules.window_note: For the lifetime of the product. That covers knives, cutlery and tableware, personal care tools, sharpeners and kitchen utensils. Anything electronic (USB knives, LED lights), plus lanyards, pouches, straps, knife blocks and small leather goods, only gets 2 years.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or a replacement if there was a fault in the material or the making. If parts for your model no longer exist, they use comparable ones. Normal wear, cosmetic marks, and damage from rough handling or accidents are not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to a Victorinox shop or service centre, or post it in. They may ask you to show proof of purchase, and they cover the trip back, though a handling fee can apply.
rules.script_hint: There is a manufacturing fault in my Victorinox knife. I would like it repaired under the lifetime warranty.
rules.source_quote: Victorinox AG warrants to the end-user purchaser that the Victorinox product will be free from material or manufacturer defects that appear during the course of normal use of the product for the lifetime of the product

rules.title: Fisher Space Pen guarantees its pens for the life of the pen
rules.window_note: For the lifetime of the pen and its refill cartridges. Ink you have used up, and worn-out erasers and O-rings, are normal running costs and are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a new pen if they choose to replace it. Damage from dropping it, misuse, poor care, normal wear or cosmetic marks is not covered. They cannot post out loose parts like springs, so a pen needing parts has to go in.
rules.how_to_claim: Print the warranty directions from the Fisher site, put them in the parcel, and post the pen to their repairs address in Boulder City, Nevada. You pay the postage there. Allow at least three weeks, or six between November and January.
rules.script_hint: My Fisher Space Pen has a manufacturing fault. I am sending it in under the lifetime guarantee.

rules.title: Briggs & Riley repairs your bag for life, even when the airline broke it
rules.window_note: For life, and no proof of purchase is needed. This is one of the very few luggage promises that covers damage someone else caused, including baggage handlers.
rules.what_you_get: Free repair of anything that stops the bag working — wheels, handles, zips, frames — including damage done by an airline. Cosmetic scuffs, cleaning, stains and smells are not covered, and neither is a lost or stolen bag or what was inside it.
rules.how_to_claim: Submit a repair on the Briggs & Riley website, or take the bag to an authorised repair centre. You pay to send it in and they pay to send it home. Ask about a DIY repair kit first — many wheel and buckle fixes are easy at home. If an airline damaged it and you want to hold them responsible, file with the airline before you leave the airport; otherwise just send it to Briggs & Riley and they fix it free.
rules.script_hint: This bag is covered by the Simple As That lifetime guarantee. The wheel is broken and I would like it repaired free of charge.
rules.source_quote: Our 'Simple as that' guarantee will cover the repair of all functional aspects of your Briggs & Riley bag for life.

rules.title: Herman Miller chairs get 12 years of free parts and free labour
rules.window_note: 12 years from the date you bought it, for the first owner only, and it must have been bought new from Herman Miller or a shop they have approved — a second-hand chair is not covered. It assumes round-the-clock use, so heavy use does not shorten it. Because it is 12 years and not forever, check the date before you assume you have run out.
rules.what_you_get: Free parts and free labour to fix a chair that failed — gas cylinders, casters, tilts, arm pads, electrics and other moving parts included. In the US and Canada the cost of the service visit is covered too.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the dealer or shop you bought it from. Before you call, take a photo of the manufacturing label underneath the chair, which has the product number, the FO number and the date it was made, plus photos of what has gone wrong. If the label is gone, your receipt can stand in.
rules.script_hint: This chair is inside its 12-year warranty and the gas cylinder has failed. I would like it repaired under warranty, parts and labour included.
rules.source_quote: This warranty is non-transferable and extends only to the original end-user purchasers who acquire new product from MillerKnoll, its subsidiaries, or its authorized resellers.

rules.title: Steelcase covers a chair frame for life and its moving parts for 12 years
rules.window_note: The frame, base and structure have no end date — Steelcase say it runs for the normal expected life of the product, no matter how many shifts a day it is used. The moving parts stop at 12 years. It only counts for the first owner, so a second-hand chair is not covered. If you bought yours from a shop as an ordinary customer rather than through a dealer, Steelcase point you to a separate consumer version of the same promise.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair, or a replacement part, for the frame, seat shell, outer back, arm frame and base with no time limit. Tilt mechanisms, gas cylinders, arm caps, foam, casters and glides are covered for 12 years. Normal wear and tear is not covered.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact the Steelcase dealer you bought it from, or ring Steelcase directly. They may ask you to send the broken part back before they replace it.
rules.script_hint: My Steelcase chair's tilt mechanism has failed. It is under 12 years old, so I would like a replacement part under the limited lifetime warranty.

rules.title: Red Wing fixes faults free in the first year, and will resole welted boots at any age for a fee
rules.window_note: The free part lasts 12 months from purchase, only for the first owner, and you need the original receipt. After that, Red Wing's repair shop will still resole boots built with welt construction at any age, but you pay for it.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair or an exchange if a fault in the making or the materials shows up in the first 12 months of normal use. After that it is not free — but Red Wing's repair shop will resole welted boots for around $165, or do a full package for around $180, which is far cheaper than replacing them. Boots with cracked insoles, torn uppers or worn-through linings usually cannot be saved.
rules.how_to_claim: For a fault in the first 12 months, take the boots and your original receipt back to the shop you bought them from or to any Red Wing store. For a paid resole, print the repair form from Red Wing's repairs page and take it with the boots to a Red Wing store, or ring customer service for a free shipping label — they cover postage on any repair over $50.
rules.script_hint: These Red Wing boots are less than 12 months old and have a fault from the way they were made. Here is my original receipt — I would like them repaired or exchanged under the warranty.
rules.source_quote: If within 12 months of purchase, a defect occurs in a Red Wing branded footwear product as the result of normal use, Red Wing will repair the defect or exchange the product.

rules.title: Costco refunds electronics in full for 90 days
rules.window_note: 90 days from the day you got it. This covers TVs, projectors, computers, tablets, smart watches, phones, cameras, drones and big appliances like fridges, washers, dryers and dishwashers.
rules.what_you_get: All your money back. Not a repair, not a store credit - the price you actually paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to the returns counter at any Costco warehouse with your membership card. If you bought it online you can still bring it to a warehouse, or start the return on Costco.com.
rules.script_hint: I bought this here about two months ago and I'd like to return it under the 90-day electronics policy.

rules.title: Costco's satisfaction guarantee has no deadline on most things
rules.window_note: No time limit. A mattress, a vacuum or a jacket you bought years ago still counts. Only electronics and big appliances have the 90-day cutoff. Custom orders, gift cards, shop cards, tickets and precious metals cannot be returned, cigarettes and alcohol cannot come back where the law forbids it, and diamonds of 1 carat or more need their original certificates.
rules.what_you_get: All your money back, the full price you paid.
rules.how_to_claim: Bring it to the returns counter at any Costco warehouse with your membership card and say you're not satisfied with it.
rules.script_hint: I'm not satisfied with this. Costco guarantees satisfaction on everything it sells, so I'd like a refund.
rules.source_quote: Diamonds: 1.00ct or larger: Members returning a diamond over 1.00ct must also present all original paperwork (IGI and/or GIA certificates)
