rules.script_hint: I'm a later owner of this item, and section 54 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act lets a subsequent purchaser claim directly from the manufacturer, so please repair or replace it.
rules.source_quote: Rights of action against the manufacturer based on an obligation resulting from section 37, 38 or 39 may be exercised by any consumer who is a subsequent purchaser of the goods.

rules.title: Quebec: your warranty stops counting while the item is in for repair
rules.window_note: No cut-off of its own: it pushes back the end of your other warranties. Add up the days the store or maker had the item for warranty work or a recall, and move the end date back by that many days. Keep the slips that show drop-off and pick-up dates.
rules.what_you_get: Every day the store or the manufacturer has your item, or part of it, for warranty work or because of a recall is added to the end of your warranty. That goes for the maker's written warranty and for the warranties Quebec law gives you.
rules.how_to_claim: If you're told your warranty has just run out, show the dates the item was with them and ask them to add that time back under section 50 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. If they refuse, send a formal notice and call the OPC for advice.
rules.script_hint: Section 50 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act extends my warranty by the [number] days you had this item for warranty repairs, so it is still covered.
rules.source_quote: The duration of a warranty provided by this Act or of a conventional warranty shall be extended for a period equal to the time during which the merchant or the manufacturer has had the goods

rules.title: Quebec: what the ad or the salesperson promised is part of the deal
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. Keep the ad, web page, box or email, and write down what the salesperson said, when, and who said it. You can prove a spoken promise with your own testimony, even if the written contract says something different.
rules.what_you_get: The item has to match its description in your contract and what the store's or maker's ads and statements said about it. Anything a store's or maker's representative told you about it, in writing or out loud, binds that business. A warranty promised in an ad counts too, even if it isn't in your contract.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the store, and to the maker if it made the claim. Quote the ad or the statement and ask them to deliver what was promised, or to repair, replace or refund. If they refuse, send a formal notice, call the OPC, then use the Small Claims Division of the Court of Québec (up to $15,000, no lawyers).
rules.script_hint: Under sections 41 and 42 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act, what your ad and your salesperson said about this item binds you, and it doesn't do what was promised, so please make it right.
rules.source_quote: The goods or services provided must conform to the statements or advertisements regarding them made by the merchant or the manufacturer. The statements or advertisements are binding on that merchant or that manufacturer.

rules.title: Quebec: a seller the maker hasn't approved must warn you, or cover the warranty itself
rules.window_note: Lasts as long as the maker's warranty would have. It only applies when the maker's warranty really does depend on buying from a seller it has approved, and when you bought from a business, not a private person.
rules.what_you_get: Some makers only honour their warranty if you bought from a seller they approved. A store that isn't approved has to tell you in writing, before the sale, that the maker's warranty won't be valid. If it didn't, that store has to provide the maker's warranty itself, at its own cost.
rules.how_to_claim: If the maker turns down your claim because the seller wasn't authorised, go back to the seller. Say they never warned you in writing, so under section 47 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act they owe you the maker's warranty at their own expense. If they refuse, send a formal notice and call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: You didn't tell me in writing that the manufacturer's warranty wouldn't be valid, so under section 47 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act you must honour that warranty yourself.
rules.source_quote: notify the consumer in writing that the manufacturer’s warranty is not valid. Failing that notification, the merchant is bound to assume that warranty at his expense.

rules.title: Quebec: a warranty repair can't come with surprise fees or shipping costs
rules.window_note: Applies every time you use a store's or maker's written warranty, for as long as it runs. A fee only counts if the warranty document states the exact amount.
rules.what_you_get: The store or maker can't charge you anything to carry out its written warranty unless the warranty document says so and gives the exact amount. It also pays the real cost of shipping or transport for the warranty work, unless the warranty document says otherwise.
rules.how_to_claim: If you're asked for a service fee or to pay for shipping, ask them to show you where the warranty document states it. If it doesn't, say sections 48 and 49 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act mean you don't pay. If they insist, send a formal notice and call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: Sections 48 and 49 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act say you can't charge me for this warranty repair unless the warranty states the exact amount, and that you pay the shipping unless it says otherwise.
rules.source_quote: No charge may be exacted by the merchant or the manufacturer for the performance of a conventional warranty unless the writing evidencing the warranty stipulates it and precisely determines the amount.

rules.title: Quebec: a warranty can't depend on you buying the maker's own brand of supplies
rules.window_note: Applies for as long as the written warranty runs. There are only three exceptions: the branded product was given to you free, the item really won't work properly without it, or the warranty is a separate one you paid for.
rules.what_you_get: A store or maker can't make its warranty valid only if you use a particular brand-name product, such as a brand of ink, filter or oil, unless one of the three exceptions applies.
rules.how_to_claim: If a claim is refused because you used another brand, ask which exception they are relying on. If none applies, point to section 52 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act and ask them to carry out the warranty. If they refuse, send a formal notice and call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: Section 52 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act says you can't make this warranty depend on my using your brand of [product], so please carry out the warranty.
rules.source_quote: The merchant or the manufacturer shall not make the validity of a conventional warranty conditional upon the consumer using a product which is identified by brand name

rules.title: Quebec: not sending in the warranty card doesn't cancel your warranty
rules.window_note: Applies for as long as the warranty itself runs. Keep your receipt so you can show when you bought it.
rules.what_you_get: A store or maker can't refuse to honour its warranty because the warranty card or registration never reached it, or was never validated.
rules.how_to_claim: If you're told the product was never registered, say section 226 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act bans refusing a warranty for that reason, and send your proof of purchase. If they still refuse, send a formal notice and call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: Section 226 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act says you can't refuse this warranty because the registration card didn't reach you, so here is my receipt and I'm asking you to honour it.
rules.source_quote: No merchant or manufacturer may refuse to perform the warranty granted by him on the pretext that the document evidencing it has not reached him or was not validated.

rules.title: Quebec: cancel an extended warranty within 10 days and get all your money back
rules.window_note: 10 days from the day you took out the extended warranty, by written notice. From 5 October 2026, the 10 days become one year if the store skipped a required explanation, for example if it didn't tell you about Quebec's free legal warranty, out loud and in writing, before offering the plan. It doesn't apply to plans underwritten by an authorized insurer.
rules.what_you_get: You can cancel an extended warranty or protection plan with no fee or penalty, and the store has to give back what you paid for it as soon as possible. Before selling you one, the store must explain the free legal warranty Quebec law already gives you and tell you how long the maker's warranty lasts, and it must tell you about this 10-day right.
rules.how_to_claim: Send the store a written notice saying you are cancelling the extended warranty under section 228.3 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act, and keep a copy. The plan is cancelled the moment you send it. If the refund doesn't come, send a formal notice and call the OPC.
rules.script_hint: Under section 228.3 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act I'm cancelling this extended warranty within 10 days, without cost or penalty, so please refund what I paid for it.
rules.source_quote: resolve without cost or penalty a contract of additional warranty on goods or clauses of a contract regarding such a warranty within 10 days after the contract has been entered into

rules.title: Quebec: a recent car that keeps failing can be declared a lemon
rules.window_note: In force since 5 October 2023. Cars only, not motorcycles or mopeds. The defects must first show up within 3 years of the car's first sale or long-term lease and before 60,000 km; those limits count from the car's first sale, not from when you bought it used. You also need one of these: 3 failed repair attempts for the same defect under the maker's warranty; 1 or 2 failed attempts for the same defect while the dealer or maker had the car more than 30 days (days they had no parts but gave you a free replacement car don't count); or 12 repair attempts for unrelated defects. The defects must make the car unfit for normal use or greatly reduce its usefulness.
rules.what_you_get: A court can declare the car a 'seriously defective automobile'. The law then treats it as having a hidden defect, so you don't have to prove one. You can ask the dealer and the manufacturer to lower the price you paid, cancel your contract, or pay for losses you can prove, and in court you can also claim punitive damages. It covers owners and long-term lessees, whether you bought from a dealer or from a private person.
rules.how_to_claim: Keep every warranty work order. Tell the dealer and the manufacturer that the car has a hidden defect and meets the anti-lemon conditions, and say what you want. If that fails, send them a formal notice, then ask the court to declare the car seriously defective and make your claims. The OPC can explain the steps.
rules.script_hint: This car has had [three] failed warranty repairs for the same defect within three years and 60,000 km, so under section 53.1 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act it qualifies as a seriously defective automobile and is deemed to have a hidden defect.
rules.source_quote: It allows the owner or long-term lessee to petition the court to declare an automobile as seriously defective when certain conditions are met. Such an automobile is thus deemed to have a hidden defect.

rules.title: Quebec: when a store or maker breaks the consumer law, here's what you can ask for
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off in the Consumer Protection Act. Ask for something that fits the problem: Quebec's consumer office says that if you have a warranty you should generally accept a repair rather than demand your money back. Keep receipts for costs the problem caused you, like repair bills, towing or spoiled food, because damages have to be backed by proof.
rules.what_you_get: You can demand that the store or maker does what it owes you, for example delivers or fixes the item; that you're allowed to have it done by someone else at its expense; that you pay less; or that the contract is cancelled. You can claim damages on top of any of these. In court you can also ask for punitive damages, which judges often give for serious failings such as bad faith.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the store or maker exactly what you want. If they refuse, send a formal notice with a deadline. You can also file a complaint with the OPC. Then go to the Small Claims Division of the Court of Québec, which hears claims up to $15,000; you represent yourself there, without a lawyer.
rules.script_hint: Section 272 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act lets me have this repaired at your expense, or ask for a price reduction or cancellation plus damages, so I'm asking you to [repair it] by [date].
rules.source_quote: authorization to have the obligation performed at the merchant’s or manufacturer’s expense (e.g., demand that the item be repaired at the merchant’s expense);

rules.title: Quebec: fine print can't force you into arbitration or out of a class action
rules.window_note: Applies whatever the contract or terms of service say. Once a dispute has started you can still choose arbitration if you want to.
rules.what_you_get: Any clause that forces you to take a dispute to private arbitration, limits your right to go to court, or stops you from bringing or joining a class action is banned. You keep your right to go to Small Claims or any other court.
rules.how_to_claim: If a business points to an arbitration clause, tell them in writing that section 11.1 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act bans it, and carry on: formal notice, then the Small Claims Division of the Court of Québec. The OPC can confirm this for you.
rules.script_hint: Section 11.1 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act bans clauses that force me into arbitration, so I'll be taking this to court if we can't settle it.
rules.source_quote: Any stipulation that obliges the consumer to refer a dispute to arbitration, that restricts the consumer’s right to go before a court, in particular by prohibiting the consumer from bringing a class action

rules.title: Quebec: stores and makers can't make repairs harder on purpose
rules.window_note: In force since 5 October 2025. No fixed cut-off. The law lets the government set limits on this rule by regulation.
rules.what_you_get: No store or manufacturer may use a technique that makes it harder for you, or someone you hire, to maintain or repair what you bought. For cars, that includes making it harder to get at the car's data for diagnosis, maintenance or repair.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the store or maker in writing to remove whatever is blocking the repair, naming section 227.0.3 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. If they refuse, report it to the OPC and send a formal notice; you can ask a court to order them to comply, plus damages.
rules.script_hint: Section 227.0.3 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act bars you from using techniques that make it harder for me or my repairer to fix this, so please remove the block.
rules.source_quote: Subject to any applicable regulations, no merchant or manufacturer may use a technique that has the effect of making it more difficult for the consumer or his mandatary to maintain or repair goods.

rules.title: Quebec: carmakers must give you and your mechanic the car's repair data
rules.window_note: In force since 5 October 2025. No fixed cut-off. Cars only, not motorcycles or mopeds.
rules.what_you_get: The manufacturer has to give the owner or long-term lessee, or someone acting for them such as an independent garage, access to the car's data for diagnosis, maintenance and repair, in a readable format. Unlike some parts and repair duties, the maker can't get out of this one by warning you in writing before the sale.
rules.how_to_claim: Ask the manufacturer in writing, through the dealer or its customer line, to give you or your garage access to the car's diagnostic and repair data under section 39.4 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act. If they refuse, report it to the OPC and send a formal notice.
rules.script_hint: Section 39.4 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act requires you to give me, or my garage, access to this car's diagnostic and repair data in a readable format, so please send me how to get it.
rules.source_quote: The manufacturer of an automobile must provide the automobile owner or long-term lessee, their mandatary or any other person determined by regulation, with access, in a legible format, to the automobile’s data for purposes of diagnostic, maintenance or repair.

rules.title: Yukon: what a business sells you has to work, whatever the fine print says
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off. The law sets no number of months, so each case is judged on its facts. It covers things you buy from a business for a cash price of up to $8,500. It also covers renting from a business with an option or a promise to own the item, unless you can end that deal at any time on two months' notice or less without a penalty. It does not cover private sales, goods bought to resell, or purchases made by a company. There is still a time limit for going to court, so don't wait.
rules.what_you_get: Promises built into every sale that no sales terms can take away: the item is of sellable quality (the law says "merchantable") apart from faults pointed out to you in writing, and it matches how it was described. If you made clear what you needed it for and relied on the seller's advice, and they sell that kind of thing, it also has to be reasonably fit for that job. That last promise does not apply if you asked for a specific product by its brand name.
rules.how_to_claim: Go back to the business that sold it, with your receipt, and explain what is wrong. If they say no, write to them: name section 58 of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act and ask for a refund, repair or replacement by a set date. If that fails, call Yukon Consumer Services at 867-667-5111 (toll-free 1-800-661-0408, extension 5111) for guidance. Your last step is Yukon's small claims court.
rules.script_hint: Section 58 of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act says what you sell me has to be of merchantable quality whatever the sales terms say, and this isn't, so I'd like you to repair, replace or refund it.
rules.source_quote: Despite any agreement to the contrary, the following conditions or warranties on the part of the seller are implied in every retail sale of goods ... a condition that the goods are of merchantable quality

rules.title: Yukon: it has to be new, unless you were told in writing that it isn't
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off; each case is judged on its facts. It covers things you buy from a business for a cash price of up to $8,500, not private sales or purchases made by a company. For a vehicle, a description showing it is more than one year old is enough to count as saying it is used.
rules.what_you_get: Unless you were told otherwise, the law treats what you bought as new and unused. A statement that it is used, how old a vehicle is, what faults it has, or what condition it is in only counts if it was in writing: a notice you could easily see at or before the sale that clearly pointed to that item, or a paper handed to you before you accepted it. If you bought on credit, it has to be in the credit agreement. Things properly sold as used still have to be of sellable quality, judged for their age and the fact they are used.
rules.how_to_claim: If you were sold something used, refurbished or with faults and nothing in writing told you, go back to the seller and ask for a refund or a new one. Put it in writing and name section 58 of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act. If they refuse, call Yukon Consumer Services at 867-667-5111 for guidance. Your last step is Yukon's small claims court.
rules.script_hint: Under section 58 of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act this had to be new and unused unless I was told otherwise in writing, and I wasn't, so I'm asking for a refund or a new one.
rules.source_quote: a condition that the goods are new and unused unless otherwise described ... a statement of a kind referred to in subsection (3) has no effect unless it is made in writing

rules.title: Yukon: purchases over $8,500 still carry an 'it must work' promise, unless your contract drops it
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off; each case is judged on its facts. This is the fallback for sales the Consumers Protection Act does not reach, like anything over $8,500. Unlike that Act, these promises can be taken away by a clear term in your contract. There is still a time limit for going to court, so don't wait.
rules.what_you_get: When you buy from a seller who deals in that kind of product, it must be of sellable quality (the law says "merchantable"). If you examined it before buying, that promise does not cover faults your check should have shown. It must match its description, and be reasonably fit for a job you told the seller about if you relied on their skill and they sell that kind of thing. A written warranty does not cancel these promises unless it contradicts them.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your contract for a term that cuts out these promises. If there isn't one, write to the seller, name section 15 of Yukon's Sale of Goods Act, and ask for a repair, a refund or money for your loss by a set date. If they refuse, call Yukon Consumer Services at 867-667-5111 for guidance. Your last step is court.
rules.script_hint: Section 15 of Yukon's Sale of Goods Act says goods from a seller who deals in them must be of merchantable quality, and this isn't, so I'm asking you to repair it, refund me or cover my loss.
rules.source_quote: when goods are bought by description from a seller who deals in goods of that description, whether the seller is the manufacturer or not, there is an implied condition that the goods shall be of merchantable quality

rules.title: Yukon: a repair or other service you pay a business for has to be done with skill
rules.window_note: No fixed cut-off; each case is judged on its facts. It covers services, such as a repair, bought from a business for up to $8,500, but not services bought by a company. The only way out for the business is a written agreement, signed by you, that says otherwise.
rules.what_you_get: A promise built into the deal that the work will be done in a skillful manner. A repair or service done badly can break that promise.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the business what went wrong with the work and ask them to redo it properly or refund you. If they refuse, put it in writing and name section 58(6) of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act. Then call Yukon Consumer Services at 867-667-5111 for guidance. Your last step is Yukon's small claims court.
rules.script_hint: Section 58(6) of Yukon's Consumers Protection Act says the service I paid for had to be done in a skillful manner, and this wasn't, so I'd like you to redo it properly or refund me.
rules.source_quote: Unless otherwise expressly agreed in writing signed by the buyer, there shall be implied in every retail sale of services a condition on the part of the seller that the services sold shall be performed in a skillful manner.

rules.title: Louisiana: if it has a hidden defect, the seller must fix it or give your money back
rules.window_note: You have to sue within 2 years of the day it was delivered to you, or within 1 year of the day you found the defect, whichever comes first (Civil Code art. 2534). If the seller takes it in for repair, the clock starts over from the day they hand it back or tell you they can't or won't fix it. The defect must have been there when you got it; if it shows up within 3 days of delivery, the law assumes it was. Defects you knew about, or that a careful buyer would have spotted, aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: If the defect makes the item useless, or so hard to use that you wouldn't have bought it had you known, you can undo the sale. If it only makes the item less useful or worth less, you get part of the price back. A seller who didn't know about the defect gets the first chance to repair it. If they can't or don't, they must give back the price with interest from the day you paid, plus the reasonable costs of the sale and of looking after the item, minus a fair amount for the use you got out of it.
rules.how_to_claim: Tell the seller about the defect in writing as soon as you find it, and give them the chance to repair it. The law requires this notice, and waiting too long can cut what you get back. Keep a copy. If they can't or won't fix it, ask in writing for your money back with interest. If they still refuse, file suit against the seller before the deadline; for a smaller amount, ask your local city court or justice of the peace court about filing. You can also complain to the Louisiana Attorney General's Consumer Protection Section.
rules.script_hint: Under Louisiana Civil Code articles 2520 and 2531 this has a redhibitory defect, so I'm asking you to repair it, or if you can't, to return my price with interest.
rules.source_quote: A seller who did not know that the thing he sold had a defect is only bound to repair, remedy, or correct the defect.

rules.title: Louisiana: a seller who knew about the defect, or who made the item, also owes damages and lawyer's fees
rules.window_note: Against a seller who knew about the defect, or is treated as knowing, you have 1 year from the day you discover the defect, but never more than 10 years from the sale, whichever comes first (Civil Code art. 2534). If the seller takes it in for repair, the clock starts over from the day they hand it back or tell you they can't or won't fix it.
rules.what_you_get: A seller who knew about a defect and didn't tell you, or who said the item had a quality they knew it didn't have, must give back the price with interest from the day you paid, repay the reasonable costs of the sale and of looking after the item, and also pay damages and reasonable attorney fees. They can take a credit for the use you got out of it. The law treats the maker of an item as knowing about its defects, so if you bought straight from the brand, this stronger rule applies.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the seller describing the defect. If they made the item, point out that Civil Code article 2545 treats a manufacturer as knowing about it. Ask for your price back with interest, plus your costs. The law doesn't require notice when the seller actually knew of the defect, but a letter gives you a record. If they refuse, file suit before the deadline; for a smaller amount, ask your local city court or justice of the peace court about filing. You can also complain to the Louisiana Attorney General's Consumer Protection Section.
rules.script_hint: Louisiana Civil Code article 2545 treats the manufacturer as knowing about this defect, so I'm asking for my price back with interest, plus my costs and damages.
rules.source_quote: A seller is deemed to know that the thing he sells has a redhibitory defect when he is a manufacturer of that thing.

rules.title: Louisiana: what you buy has to be reasonably fit for its normal use
rules.window_note: Same deadline as a hidden-defect claim: you have to sue within 2 years of the day it was delivered, or 1 year from the day you found the problem, whichever comes first (Civil Code art. 2534).
rules.what_you_get: The item must be reasonably fit for what it's normally used for. If the seller knew what you needed it for, and you relied on their skill or advice to pick it, it must also be fit for that purpose. If it isn't, your claim against the seller runs under Louisiana's general contract rules.
rules.how_to_claim: Write to the seller: say what you bought, what normal use it fails at (or what purpose you told them about), and ask them to make it right. Keep a copy. If they refuse, file suit before the deadline; for a smaller amount, ask your local city court or justice of the peace court about filing. You can also complain to the Louisiana Attorney General's Consumer Protection Section.
rules.script_hint: Louisiana Civil Code article 2524 says a thing sold must be reasonably fit for its ordinary use, and this isn't, so please make it right.
rules.source_quote: The thing sold must be reasonably fit for its ordinary use.

rules.title: Louisiana: an "as is" sale only counts if it was clear and pointed out to you
rules.window_note: This comes up inside a hidden-defect claim, so that deadline applies: 2 years from delivery or 1 year from finding the defect, whichever comes first. If the seller knew about the defect, it's 1 year from finding it, up to 10 years from the sale (Civil Code art. 2534).
rules.what_you_get: A seller can cut out or limit the hidden-defect warranty only with terms that are clear, not open to two readings, and brought to your attention. A waiver doesn't protect a seller who said the item had a quality they knew it didn't have. And even when the warranty was validly cut out, you take over the seller's own warranty rights against others, such as the maker.
rules.how_to_claim: If the seller points to "as is" or "no warranty" small print, ask them to show where it was made clear and pointed out to you when you bought. If it wasn't, make your repair-or-refund claim as normal. If the waiver does hold, you can still go after the maker using the seller's own warranty rights. If they refuse, file suit before the deadline in your local court.
rules.script_hint: Under Louisiana Civil Code article 2548 a warranty waiver only binds me if it was clear and brought to my attention, and it wasn't, so the redhibition warranty still applies.
rules.source_quote: The terms of the exclusion or limitation must be clear and unambiguous and must be brought to the attention of the buyer.

rules.title: Timberland boots, shoes and gear get 1 year against defects
rules.window_note: 12 months from the day you first bought it. It only covers the first buyer, and only if you bought from Timberland or a Timberland authorized seller in the country where you claim. Normal wear and tear, misuse, neglect, accidents, changes to the product and outside repairs aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: If Timberland finds a defect, it replaces the item or gives you credit. Once a claim is accepted, you usually don't have to send the item back: Timberland gives you an eGift card for the amount on your receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Bought from Timberland.com or a Timberland store less than 30 days ago? Return it and pick 'Item was defective' as the reason. Bought from another authorized store and still inside its return window? Take it back there with the receipt. Otherwise, fill in the online warranty claim on Timberland's warranty page with your proof of purchase. They answer in about 5 to 7 business days. Clean the item first.
rules.script_hint: My Timberland [item] has a defect in material or workmanship and I bought it less than 12 months ago, so it's covered by the Timberland warranty; here is my receipt.
rules.source_quote: Timberland products (the “Product(s)”) are warranted to be free of defects in material and workmanship for 12 months from the original date of purchase.

rules.title: Samsonite luggage: factory faults fixed free for up to 10 years
rules.window_note: The length depends on the bag: Samsonite's US warranties run 10, 5 or 3 years from the day it was bought, and some are for the lifetime of the first owner. Check your bag's warranty card or product page. It covers the first buyer or the person it was given to. In California, for buys from July 1, 2023, the clock starts on the day it was delivered. Airline or other transport damage, misuse, neglect, accidents, abrasion, extreme heat or cold, water, and normal wear and tear aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: If it's a covered fault and can be repaired, Samsonite fixes it and sends it back at its own cost. If it can't be repaired, you're offered a comparable replacement at no cost. You pay to get it to the repair center.
rules.how_to_claim: Create a repair request from the Submit Request button on Samsonite's Service & Repairs page. Then ship it with tracking, or take it yourself, to an authorized repair center. Or drop it at a Samsonite company store, which sends it on for $15 (22 inches or under) or $20 (23 inches or larger). Warranty repairs must be done by an approved Samsonite service center; a repair done elsewhere can void the warranty. For an eBags bag, email warranty@ebags.com.
rules.script_hint: My Samsonite [item] has a manufacturing defect and it's still inside the Samsonite limited warranty period, so please repair or replace it.
rules.source_quote: The warranty provided for herein applies only to the first purchaser or gift recipient of the Product for a period of ten years starting from the date this Product was purchased.

rules.title: Columbia jackets, snow gear, backpacks and sleeping bags are covered for their useful life
rules.window_note: No set number of years. Outerwear (insulated jackets, snow gear, shells) and equipment (sleeping bags, backpacks) are covered for the practical lifetime of the product, meaning until Columbia judges it worn out beyond reasonable repair. Normal wear and tear, poor care, misuse, accidents, neglect, materials breaking down with age, and items you repaired or altered aren't covered. Keep your receipt; Columbia may ask for it. Tents, watches, sunglasses and goggles, and belts and wallets are handled by the companies that make them for Columbia.
rules.what_you_get: If Columbia finds a defect in materials or workmanship, it repairs the item or gives you a Virtual Merchandise Credit worth its full retail price (MSRP). If it can't be repaired, you choose the credit or getting the item back unrepaired.
rules.how_to_claim: Start on Columbia's warranty page, pick your product type and fill in the claim form, one item per form (you need an email address). Print the form, or copy its details onto paper, and pack it with the whole item and your proof of purchase: the hood with the jacket, both parts of an interchange jacket. Ship it with a tracked carrier. Stores can't file claims for you, though the shop you bought it from may help. Call the warranty team 7 to 10 business days after it arrives to check on it.
rules.script_hint: My Columbia [item] has a defect in materials or workmanship, so under Columbia's limited lifetime warranty I'd like it repaired or credited.
rules.source_quote: These items are covered for the practical lifetime of the product. Proof of purchase may be required.

rules.title: Columbia shoes, boots and everyday clothes get 1 year
rules.window_note: 1 year from the day you bought it. This covers footwear (boots, hiking shoes, sandals) and sportswear (T-shirts, button-ups, shorts, pants, fleece). Proof of purchase is usually needed, but without it Columbia may still take the claim if the item was made within the last year. Normal wear and tear, poor care, misuse, accidents and neglect aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: If Columbia finds a defect in materials or workmanship, it repairs the item or gives you a Virtual Merchandise Credit for its retail value. If it can't be repaired, you choose the credit or getting the item back unrepaired.
rules.how_to_claim: Start on Columbia's warranty page, pick your product type and fill in the claim form, one item per form (you need an email address). Print the form, or copy its details onto paper, and pack it with the whole item and your receipt; send both boots even if only one is faulty. Ship it with a tracked carrier. Stores can't file claims for you, though the shop you bought it from may help. Call the warranty team 7 to 10 business days after it arrives to check on it.
rules.script_hint: My Columbia [item] has a defect in materials or workmanship and is less than a year old, so it's covered by Columbia's one-year limited warranty.
rules.source_quote: These items are covered for 1 year from the date of purchase. Proof of purchase is typically required.

rules.title: Arc'teryx jackets, clothing and packs are covered for their useful life
rules.window_note: No set number of years. Apparel, packs (not the Voltair airbag) and accessories are covered for their 'practical product lifespan': how long that kind of item normally lasts, judged by Arc'teryx from the product, how it was used, the problem and its age. It is not your lifetime. You must be the first buyer, with a receipt from an authorized Arc'teryx dealer. Rips, cuts, tears, burns, abrasion, down leaking through, fading, normal wear, misuse, accidents and outside repairs aren't covered. Separately, Arc'teryx will repair its gear for as long as it can be repaired, whatever the age or cause, sometimes for a fee.
rules.what_you_get: If it's covered, Arc'teryx chooses: a free repair (parts and labor), the same model, a comparable product if yours is discontinued, or a voucher for arcteryx.com. It's one repair or replacement per item you bought. You pay the shipping to send it in.
rules.how_to_claim: Don't take it back to the store you bought it from. Fill in the online Product Service Request on Arc'teryx's site with photos of the item and your receipt, or take it to an Arc'teryx store and they'll send it off to be checked. Wait for a case number and shipping instructions before you mail it. The warranty sends disputes to private arbitration, but you can still use small claims court, and you can opt out by writing to Arc'teryx within 60 days of buying.
rules.script_hint: My Arc'teryx [item] has a material or workmanship defect and is still within its practical product lifespan, so it's covered by the Arc'teryx Limited Warranty.
rules.source_quote: Practical Product Lifespan means the usual and customary wearable life of the product. The Practical Product Lifespan does not mean for your lifetime or mean a time period that is indefinite.

rules.title: Arc'teryx shoes and ski boots get 1 year
rules.window_note: 1 year from the day you bought them, for footwear and for ski boots. You must be the first buyer, with a receipt from an authorized Arc'teryx dealer. Normal wear, cosmetic scuffs, misuse, accidents and outside repairs aren't covered.
rules.what_you_get: If they're covered, Arc'teryx chooses: a free repair (parts and labor), the same model, a comparable product if yours is discontinued, or a voucher for arcteryx.com. It's one repair or replacement per pair you bought. You pay the shipping to send them in.
rules.how_to_claim: Don't take them back to the store you bought them from. Fill in the online Product Service Request on Arc'teryx's site with photos of the shoes and your receipt, or take them to an Arc'teryx store and they'll send them off to be checked. Wait for a case number and shipping instructions before you mail them. The warranty sends disputes to private arbitration, but you can still use small claims court.
rules.script_hint: My Arc'teryx shoes have a material or workmanship defect and I bought them less than a year ago, so they're covered by the Arc'teryx Limited Warranty.
rules.source_quote: Footwear (other than ski boots) 1 year from date of purchase

rules.title: Arc'teryx climbing gear gets 2 years
rules.window_note: 2 years from the day you bought it. You must be the first buyer, with a receipt from an authorized Arc'teryx dealer. Normal wear, cuts, abrasion, misuse, accidents and outside repairs aren't covered. The Voltair avalanche airbag has its own terms: 3 years or 50 inflations, whichever comes first, and 1 year on its battery.
rules.what_you_get: If it's covered, Arc'teryx chooses: a free repair (parts and labor), the same model, a comparable product if yours is discontinued, or a voucher for arcteryx.com. It's one repair or replacement per item you bought. You pay the shipping to send it in.
rules.how_to_claim: Don't take it back to the store you bought it from. Fill in the online Product Service Request on Arc'teryx's site with photos of the item and your receipt, or take it to an Arc'teryx store and they'll send it off to be checked. Wait for a case number and shipping instructions before you mail it. The warranty sends disputes to private arbitration, but you can still use small claims court.
rules.script_hint: My Arc'teryx climbing gear has a material or workmanship defect and I bought it less than two years ago, so it's covered by the Arc'teryx Limited Warranty.
rules.source_quote: Climbing Gear 2 years from date of purchase

rules.title: Carhartt will repair, replace or credit workwear that fails you
rules.window_note: Carhartt doesn't set a time limit, but it says all clothing has an expected service life, so this isn't a promise that it lasts forever. It doesn't cover normal wear and tear, misuse, neglect or obvious abuse, or clothes that were altered. For normal wear and tear, Carhartt may charge a fair fee to repair it. The repair service works only in the US, and it can't fix gloves, footwear, belts, bags, wallets, flame-resistant clothing, base layers, socks or back-pocket blowouts on pants.
rules.what_you_get: If a Carhartt product fails to hold up, Carhartt works to make it right with a repair, a replacement or credit.
rules.how_to_claim: Wash the item, then fill in the online repair form on Carhartt's Commitment & Repair page, or call customer service to be walked through it. In Chicago (Wicker Park) or Murray, Utah, you can drop it at the Carhartt store to be checked on the spot. Repairs take about 4 to 5 weeks from when they receive it.
rules.script_hint: My Carhartt [item] failed without misuse, so under Carhartt's commitment to make it right I'd like it repaired, replaced or credited.
rules.source_quote: If one of our products should fail to meet your expectations, we’ll work to make it right through repair, replacement, or credit.

rules.title: adidas shoes and clothes are covered for 6 months against factory defects
rules.window_note: 6 months from the day you bought it, with proof of purchase from adidas.com, the adidas app, an adidas store or an authorized adidas retailer. Items from unauthorized sellers, including some online marketplaces, aren't covered. Insoles, buttons, laces, emblems and drawstrings aren't covered, and neither are normal wear, poor care, misuse or accidents. A replacement you got from a claim can't be claimed again.
rules.what_you_get: adidas doesn't repair. If it agrees the item is defective, you get an online credit voucher toward a suitable replacement; the exact same model isn't promised. If adidas needs to inspect it, it sends a prepaid label, and the item isn't returned to you.
rules.how_to_claim: Bought in a shop, including an adidas store? Take it back there first. Bought on adidas.com or the app, or the shop won't help? Email customerservice@us.adidas.com with your name, mailing address, 'AD' order number, the article number and a short description of the fault. Attach your receipt and clear photos of the whole item, the defect, the label with its 6-digit code and manufacture date, and the soles for shoes. You get a claim number by email; most claims are settled in 1 to 3 weeks.
rules.script_hint: My adidas [item] has a manufacturing defect and I bought it less than 6 months ago, so it's covered by the adidas warranty policy.
rules.source_quote: The adidas (“adidas” or “we”) warranty policy covers consumers against certain manufacturing defects that exist within six (6) months from the date of purchase by Customer, with valid Proof of Purchase.

rules.title: adidas backpacks and duffels with a Lifetime Warranty tag get 5 years
rules.window_note: Most adidas duffels and backpacks carry a Lifetime Warranty, shown by a tag on the bag when you buy it. adidas defines 'lifetime' as the expected life of the bag, 5 years. Bags without that tag get the normal 6-month adidas warranty. Normal wear and tear isn't covered.
rules.what_you_get: A replacement bag if it has a defect in materials or workmanship. You get one replacement per bag you bought; the replacement can't be claimed again.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Agron, the company that handles these bags for adidas, at 800-966-7697 and choose option 3. Have your receipt and the bag ready.
rules.script_hint: My adidas bag has the Lifetime Warranty tag and a defect in materials or workmanship within 5 years, so I'd like a replacement under the adidas Lifetime Warranty.
rules.source_quote: The adidas Lifetime Warranty guarantees our product will be free from defects in materials and workmanship for the expected life of the product, outlined as five (5) years.

rules.title: New Balance tennis shoes: a new pair if the sole wears through in 6 months
rules.window_note: Only for the 996, 1007, CT-RALLY and WCHCOC tennis shoes bought from January 1 to December 31, 2026, in the 50 states or DC (or delivered there). The NDurance rubber sole must be worn right through to the midsole from playing tennis within 6 months, and you must start the claim within 6 months of the date on your receipt. The uppers aren't covered. New Balance has no general written warranty on its other shoes; for anything flawed or defective, contact its Customer Care team.
rules.what_you_get: After checking the shoes, New Balance gives you a promo code for a new pair of the same model on newbalance.com (it can't be used in stores). New Balance pays the shipping to send them in. If they don't qualify, it sends your pair back.
rules.how_to_claim: Contact Customer Care from newbalance.com/customerservice within 6 months of buying, with your receipt. They email you return instructions; put a copy of that email in the box with the shoes, or they're sent back without being checked.
rules.script_hint: The NDurance sole on my New Balance [model] wore through to the midsole from playing tennis within 6 months, so I'm claiming under the 6-Month NDurance Rubber Outsole Limited Warranty Guarantee.
rules.source_quote: The outsole must be completely worn through exposing the midsole of the shoe within 6 months of purchase.

rules.title: Dr. Martens boots and shoes get 1 year against defects
rules.window_note: 1 year from the day you bought them, for the first buyer only. They must be bought in the US from a Dr. Martens store, drmartens.com/us or an authorized reseller. A repair or replacement doesn't restart the year. Laces, insoles and tags aren't replaced, and normal wear, not following the care instructions, accidents, changes, outside repairs and extreme wet, heat or sun aren't covered. The old 'For Life' range has its own terms.
rules.what_you_get: If Dr. Martens agrees there's a defect, it chooses: you get them repaired and it pays you back the reasonable repair cost, it sends a replacement of equal value, or it gives you a coupon code for the price you paid. If it needs the pair back, it sends a return label, and it ships a replacement free within the US.
rules.how_to_claim: Bought from another shop? Ask them first; it's usually fastest. Otherwise, contact Dr. Martens within the year with photos of the defect, a description, and a receipt that shows the seller and the date. Have the product code, style, color and size ready.
rules.script_hint: My Dr. Martens [item] have a defect in materials or workmanship and I bought them less than a year ago, so they're covered by the Dr. Martens Limited Product Warranty.
rules.source_quote: warrants to the original purchaser that their Dr. Martens-branded footwear (“Product(s)”) will be free from defects in materials and workmanship for one (1) year from the date of purchase

rules.title: Blundstone boots with a factory fault are replaced for 2 years
rules.window_note: Boots bought more than 2 years ago are excluded. You must have bought them from Blundstone USA or an approved US reseller. Normal wear (scuffs, scratches, stains, marks from lack of leather care), damage you caused, and air bubbles in the soles aren't covered. Insoles, elastic sides and pull tabs are sent as parts on request, if in stock, rather than as a whole new pair.
rules.what_you_get: If Blundstone finds a manufacturing fault, it replaces the boots.
rules.how_to_claim: Bought straight from Blundstone USA less than 30 days ago? Use its returns portal instead. Otherwise, fill in the warranty claim form on Blundstone's US site, with photos of the boots from every side and your receipt or other proof of purchase. The team reviews claims within about 5 business days.
rules.script_hint: My Blundstones have a manufacturing fault and I bought them less than 2 years ago from an approved US reseller, so I'm asking for a replacement under the Blundstone warranty.
rules.source_quote: Exclusions from our warranty include but are not limited to: Products purchased more than 2 years ago.

rules.title: Razer gaming chairs get 3 years, and 5 if you bought on Razer.com and share a photo
rules.window_note: 3 years from the day you bought it for the Iskur, Iskur V2 and Enki chairs. The Fujin gets 5 years on the frame, mechanisms and armrests but 1 year on the mesh back and seat pan; the Soma gets 3 years on mechanisms and 2 on electronics; chair accessories get 1 year. Bought on Razer.com? Post a public photo of the chair with #RazerChair and submit the link within 3 months of buying to add 2 more years for free (Soma Chroma, Iskur V2, Iskur V2 X, their NewGen versions, and Enki, Enki Pro, Enki X). Scratches, dents, fading and tears in the cushions, leather or stitching count as wear and aren't covered. Card statements don't count as proof of purchase.
rules.what_you_get: A free repair with new or refurbished parts, or a swap for a product that works at least as well. You pay to ship it to Razer; Razer pays to send it back. A repaired or swapped chair is covered for 90 days or the rest of the original warranty, whichever is longer.
rules.how_to_claim: Bought from a shop in the US or Canada less than 30 days ago? Go to that shop. Otherwise, get a Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) number through mysupport.razer.com, write it on the outside of the box, put a dated receipt or your Razer.com order number inside, and ship it by a tracked carrier to the address Razer gives you.
rules.script_hint: My Razer [chair] has a defect and is inside its 3-year Razer limited warranty, so I'd like an RMA number for a repair or replacement.
rules.source_quote: While every Razer gaming chair already comes with a 3-year limited warranty, get an additional two years of coverage for free simply by showing us how good your chair looks.

rules.title: Anker power strips: Anker may pay for gear damaged while plugged into one
rules.window_note: No end date is stated, but you must claim within 15 days of the damage. It covers all Anker power strips and outlet extenders, for the first buyer. The terms say the strip must be 'purchased originally from Anker', so if you bought it from another store, ask Anker whether it counts. The strip must be plugged straight into a properly wired, grounded wall outlet (no extension cords or adapters), with no competing brand plugged into the same circuit, and the damaged gear must be UL listed, AC powered and used indoors in a dry place. Not covered: surges that came in through unprotected lines, direct lightning, brownouts, lost data, missing grounding, gear used with a generator, heater, sump pump, medical device or vehicle battery charger, and gear still covered by its own warranty.
rules.what_you_get: Up to USD 200,000 per incident: Anker may pay you the fair market value of the damaged equipment, or approve a repair at a service center authorized by that equipment's maker.
rules.how_to_claim: Within 15 days of the damage, call Anker or email support@anker.com with your order number, the strip's serial number, the receipt, and photos of the strip and the damaged gear. Anker sends a prepaid label and an RMA number; write the number on the strip and mail it back with a copy of the receipt within 20 days. Anker's terms say you pay the cost of getting the strip and the damaged gear to them for inspection.
rules.script_hint: My [device] was damaged while plugged into my Anker power strip, and I'm claiming within 15 days under Anker's Connected Equipment Warranty.
rules.source_quote: ANKER INNOVATION TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD (“Anker”) offers a limited Connected Equipment Warranty (“CEW”) for all Anker Power Strips and Outlet Extenders. The product shall be purchased originally from Anker

rules.title: iPhone and iPad get 1 year of free repairs from Apple in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year from the day you first bought it, on iPhone, iPad, iPod, Apple TV and HomePod, plus the Apple accessories that came in the box. Apple says this year already includes the legal warranty period. A repaired or replacement part is covered for 90 days or the rest of the year, whichever is longer. Not covered: accidents, liquid, scratches and dents, battery wear that isn't a defect, or changes made by people Apple didn't authorize. Apple can limit iPhone, iPad, Apple TV and HomePod service to the country where they were sold.
rules.what_you_get: Apple repairs it with new or tested genuine parts, replaces it with the same model, or refunds what you paid. In Mexico, parts, labour and shipping inside Apple's service network cost you nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Start at support.apple.com/es-mx or call Apple Support at 001-866-676-5682. Take it to an Apple Store or an Apple Authorized Service Provider, or Apple can send you prepaid shipping to mail it in. In Mexico you can also ask the store where you bought it to handle the warranty. Bring the product and the póliza stamped by the store (or your receipt), and back up your data first. If Apple or the store refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency (gob.mx/profeco), for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My [iPhone] stopped working on its own within a year of buying it, so it's covered by Apple's one-year limited warranty in Mexico; here is my receipt.
rules.source_quote: Apple, tal y como se define posteriormente, garantiza este producto de marca Apple frente a defectos en materiales y mano de obra durante un período de un (1) año desde la fecha de compra por el usuario final

rules.title: Samsung phones, TVs and appliances get 12 months in Mexico
rules.window_note: 12 months from the day it was delivered to you, on phones, tablets, watches, Bluetooth headsets, TVs and home appliances. Accessories that came in the box get 6 months, and ones bought separately get 3 months. Monitors get 36 months and home theaters 6 months. Washers, fridges and vacuums get 10 years on the Digital Inverter motor or compressor, but on washers and fridges labour is only free in the first year. It only covers products Samsung Electronics México sold through its authorized sellers in Mexico. Grey imports, second-hand units, cracked screens, moisture or corrosion, and repairs by unauthorized people are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: Samsung repairs or replaces the faulty parts for free, parts and labour included, using new or repaired parts that work as well or better. Samsung pays to move the product inside its service network. A repaired part is covered for the rest of the original period.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the product and the póliza (stamped by the store with the delivery date) to any Samsung authorized service center; if you lost the póliza, bring your original invoice or receipt. Call 800 726 7864 to find the nearest one, request a repair online at samsung.com/mx/support, or use Samsung's WhatsApp or live chat (every day, 8:00 to 21:00). If Samsung refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Samsung [item] has a factory fault and is less than 12 months old, so it's covered by Samsung Electronics México's warranty; here is my stamped póliza and receipt.
rules.source_quote: Samsung Electronics México, S.A. de C.V., garantizará este producto en todos sus componentes y mano de obra por el tiempo indicado en el listado anterior, contando a partir de la fecha de entrega al consumidor final

rules.title: LG TVs, audio and appliances get 1 year in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year from the day it was delivered to you, on TVs, sound bars, speakers, wireless earbuds, home appliances, monitors and projectors. Remotes get 3 months. Some key parts get 10 years: direct-drive washer, dryer and dishwasher motors, linear fridge compressors, inverter compressors and inverter microwave magnetrons. On most of those, labour is only free in the first year. It only covers LG products sold by LG Electronics México and its authorized sellers in Mexico. Installation and maintenance are not covered.
rules.what_you_get: LG repairs it, or swaps it for the same or a similar product, with parts and labour free. LG pays to move it once it is in LG's service network. The repair can't take longer than 30 business days from when the service centre receives it.
rules.how_to_claim: Call LG at 800 347 1919 (55 5321 1919 in Mexico City), or message LG on WhatsApp at the same 800 number, to be sent to an LG authorized service centre. Bring the product plus the póliza stamped with the delivery date, or your receipt or invoice. If LG refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My LG [item] has a manufacturing fault within its first year, so it's covered by LG Electronics México's warranty, parts and labour included.
rules.source_quote: LG Electronics México, S.A. de C.V. garantiza el funcionamiento de sus equipos, además de la mano de obra empleada en la reparación de los mismos, por el periodo comprendido de acuerdo a tabla anexa, contra cualquier defecto de fabricación

rules.title: HP laptops, PCs and printers get 1 year in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year on hardware, counted from the day you received it from an authorized HP seller. Ink and toner cartridges get 3 months, and software 3 months. Your model may come with more: HP's warranty check page shows the exact end date for your serial number. Not covered: use in abnormal conditions, not following the manual, or repairs by people HP didn't authorize.
rules.what_you_get: HP México repairs or replaces it so it works to its specifications, and pays shipping inside HP's service network in Mexico.
rules.how_to_claim: Check your end date at support.hp.com/mx-es/check-warranty with your serial number. Then call HP support at 800-063-0234 or 555091-24-55. Take the product and the póliza stamped by the store where you bought it to an HP authorized service centre. If HP refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My HP [item] has a hardware fault and is under a year old, so it's covered by HP México's limited warranty; here is my receipt.
rules.source_quote: Duración de la Garantía Limitada Hardware: 1 año Cartucho destinado al consumidor final: 3 meses

rules.title: Whirlpool large appliances get 1 year of free repairs in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year from the day you first bought it, for home use only, under Whirlpool's one-year warranty certificate for large appliances, with Whirlpool México as the guarantor. The certificate is part of your user manual, so check yours. Not covered: bad installation, wrong voltage or power surges, misuse, foreign objects like coins, harsh cleaners, cosmetic wear, glass, porcelain, plastic and rubber parts, light bulbs, or repairs by people Whirlpool didn't authorize.
rules.what_you_get: Free labour and the parts needed to repair it. Whirlpool should fix it within 30 business days of your request, unless parts have to come from abroad.
rules.how_to_claim: Call the Whirlpool contact centre at 81 8329 2100 (Monday to Friday 8:00 to 19:00, Saturday 8:00 to 17:00, Sunday 10:00 to 17:00), email servicio@whirlpool.com, or WhatsApp 81 2516 1867. Show the warranty certificate together with your original invoice or receipt. If Whirlpool refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Whirlpool [appliance] broke down on its own within a year of buying it, so it's covered by Whirlpool México's one-year warranty; here is my invoice.
rules.source_quote: El término de vigencia de esta Garantía es de un (1) año a partir de la fecha de compra original por el consumidor final del producto garantizado

rules.title: Mabe appliances get 1 year of free repairs in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year from the day you bought it. Any fault caused by how it was made is fixed for free in that year. The full terms are in the warranty policy in your user manual.
rules.what_you_get: A Servicio Mabe technician comes to your home to find the fault. If it comes from manufacturing, the repair costs you nothing.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Servicio Mabe at (55) 9088 6223 (Monday to Friday 8:00 to 20:00, Saturday 9:00 to 14:00), message WhatsApp 56 6214 1659, or book a visit at servicio.mabeglobal.com. Keep your receipt handy to show the purchase date. If Mabe refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Mabe [appliance] has a manufacturing fault and I bought it less than a year ago, so the repair should be free under Mabe's one-year warranty.
rules.source_quote: La garantía de nuestros productos tiene un año a partir de la fecha de compra, durante el periodo de garantía, cualquier daño originado por la fabricación del producto es sin costo

rules.title: Hisense 4K and 8K TVs get 2 years in Mexico
rules.window_note: Two years on 4K and 8K TVs and Laser TVs. Other smart TVs and HD TVs get only 1 year, and accessories that came in the box get 3 months. It counts from the purchase date on your receipt or stamped póliza, for TVs sold or distributed in Mexico. Not covered: drops and accidents, liquid, power surges, pests, cosmetic damage, business use, or a cracked or broken panel.
rules.what_you_get: Hisense repairs it with new or remanufactured parts and pays the labour, or swaps it for the same or a similar product. It has to be fixed within 30 days, and the days it spends in the shop are added back onto your warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Hisense for free at 800-008-8880 (Monday to Friday 9:00 to 21:00, Saturday 9:00 to 15:00) to get a service order. TVs under 40 inches go to an authorized service centre; other products are repaired at your home. Have your invoice or ticket, the model and the serial number ready; they may ask you to email documents to documentos.garantia@hisense.com. If Hisense refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Hisense 4K TV has a fault and is less than two years old, so it's covered by Hisense México's 2-year TV warranty.
rules.source_quote: TV y Laser TV con resolución 4K y 8K 2 Años

rules.title: Hisense appliances and phones get 1 year in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year on fridges, freezers, mini fridges, wine coolers, washers, washer-dryers, cooktops, gas ovens, hoods, dishwashers, air conditioners, dehumidifiers and phones. Some parts get longer, parts only and not labour: 10 years on inverter fridge compressors and washer-dryer motors, 8 years on air conditioner compressors, 3 years on twin-tub washer transmissions. Accessories that came in the box get 3 months. Not covered: accidents, liquid, power surges, pests, cosmetic damage, business use, or installing it against the manual.
rules.what_you_get: Hisense repairs it with new or remanufactured parts and pays the labour, or swaps it for the same or a similar product. It has to be fixed within 30 days, and the days it spends in the shop are added back onto your warranty.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Hisense for free at 800-008-8880 (Monday to Friday 9:00 to 21:00, Saturday 9:00 to 15:00) to get a service order. Fridges, washers, cooktops, ovens, hoods and other appliances are repaired at your home. Have your invoice or ticket, the model and the serial number ready; they may ask you to email documents to documentos.garantia@hisense.com. If Hisense refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Hisense [item] failed on its own within a year, so it's covered by Hisense México's warranty, parts and labour included.
rules.source_quote: HISENSE México S. de R. L. de C.V., garantiza los productos vendidos o distribuidos en la República Mexicana, en todos sus componentes y mano de obra por el tiempo indicado en el apartado anterior

rules.title: Xiaomi phones, TVs and gadgets get 1 year in Mexico
rules.window_note: Twelve months from the day it was delivered to you, for phones, tablets, watches and bands, earbuds, TVs, vacuums, scooters, kitchen gadgets and most other Xiaomi products. Chargers and cables in the box, and TV remotes, get 6 months. Straps, bags, USB sticks, scooter accessories and a few other small items get no warranty period (Xiaomi lists them as 'DAP' only). Not covered: abnormal use, not following the manual, or repairs by people Xiaomi didn't authorize.
rules.what_you_get: Xiaomi chooses: a free repair with new or tested genuine parts, a replacement of the same model (or a similar one if you agree), or a refund of what you paid. Parts, labour and shipping for the warranty are free.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Xiaomi's service line at 800-269-2630 or find an authorized service centre at mi.com/mx/support/service-centre. Bring the product with your invoice or other proof of purchase, and back up your data first. For some smart-home products, the authorized seller handles the warranty instead. Pick up the repaired product within 15 days of being told it's ready. If Xiaomi refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Xiaomi [item] has a factory defect and was delivered less than 12 months ago, so it's covered by Xiaomi's one-year limited warranty in Mexico.
rules.source_quote: XIAOMI garantiza nuestros productos contra defectos en los materiales y mano de obra por un periodo de UN AÑO (doce meses) a partir de la fecha de entrega al consumidor.

rules.title: Motorola phones get 12 months of free repairs in Mexico
rules.window_note: Twelve months under Motorola's standard manufacturer's limited warranty. Cracked or broken screens, other physical damage and liquid damage are not covered by it; Motorola will repair those only for a fee.
rules.what_you_get: Most repairs cost you nothing inside the standard warranty. Motorola's repair centre sends the phone back within 7 business days after it receives and checks it, though it can take longer depending on where you live.
rules.how_to_claim: Start at Motorola's Latin America repair page and use its warranty lookup. Then take the phone to a Motorola service centre (the page has a locator) or, in Mexico, ask for courier pickup and return. Back up and erase your phone first, and take out the SIM and memory cards. If Motorola refuses a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Motorola phone is less than 12 months old and failed on its own, so it's covered by Motorola's standard 12-month warranty.
rules.source_quote: La cobertura ESP de Moto Care Protection comienza el día en que finaliza el período de garantía limitada estándar del fabricante de 12 meses

rules.title: Nintendo consoles, controllers and games get 1 year in Mexico
rules.window_note: One year from the day it was delivered to you, for Switch 2, Switch, Switch Lite and Switch OLED consoles, accessories sold with them or separately, and physical games. Not covered: abnormal use, not following the instructions, or repairs by people not authorized by Latamel, Nintendo's importer in Mexico.
rules.what_you_get: Latamel Distribuidora repairs it and replaces faulty parts for free, and pays shipping inside its service network. The repair can't take more than 30 days from when the service centre gets it. A faulty physical game is swapped for a new one.
rules.how_to_claim: Call Latamel at 800 9107070 or 55 9178-4350, or email callcentermx@latamel.com. Show the product with the póliza stamped by the store, or any receipt that names the product. You can claim at the store where you bought it or at Latamel's service centre in Mexico City. If they refuse a valid claim, ask Profeco (gob.mx/profeco) for a conciliation.
rules.script_hint: My Nintendo [product] has a factory defect and I got it less than a year ago, so it's covered by the Mexican warranty póliza from Latamel Distribuidora.
rules.source_quote: garantiza este producto o accesorio en todas sus partes y la mano de obra contra cualquier defecto de fabricación y funcionamiento a partir de la fecha de entrega al consumidor, de acuerdo a los siguientes periodos

rules.title: Liverpool has no time limit on exchanges and returns
rules.window_note: Liverpool says there is no time limit to exchange or return something, as long as it's in good condition, with all its parts and its original box. Some things never come back: headphones, mattresses and bedding, towels, underwear, swimwear, socks, cosmetics and perfume, vitamins, baby-care products, downloads like software and video games, sealed collectibles, and anything made or set up just for you.
rules.what_you_get: A swap for another item, or your money back. With a receipt (paper, or the order confirmation email) the refund goes back to how you paid, or onto a Liverpool Monedero Electrónico. Without a receipt it goes onto a Monedero Electrónico.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the item and your receipt or confirmation email to any Liverpool store and ask for an exchange or a return. For something big, call Liverpool on 55 5262 9999 (or *7171 from a mobile) to book a pickup. If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: Liverpool's policy says there's no time limit on exchanges or returns, and this [item] has stopped working, so I'd like to swap it or get my money back.
rules.source_quote: No hay tiempo límite para realizar tu cambio o devolución, sin embargo te pedimos considerar lo siguiente

rules.title: Liverpool online order faulty or wrong? 90 days to swap or refund, plus a 20% bonus
rules.window_note: 90 days from the day you bought it or the day it arrived. This is for orders from liverpool.com.mx or the Liverpool app that arrive faulty or different from what the site showed. Liverpool's terms say the item must not have been used, altered or personalised. Items sold by outside sellers on Liverpool's site get a refund rather than a swap. The usual no-return list still applies (mattresses, bedding, underwear, cosmetics, downloads and similar).
rules.what_you_get: A similar item or your money back, and on top of that a 20% bonus (bonificación), paid into a Liverpool Monedero Electrónico, or onto your Liverpool or Suburbia card if you paid with one.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the item and your order confirmation email to any Liverpool store, or call or WhatsApp Liverpool on 55 5262 9999, or email atencion@liverpool.com.mx. Ask for the swap or refund and the 20% bonificación. Liverpool's terms say it answers in writing within 72 business hours. If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office. Liverpool's own terms name Profeco as the place to settle disputes.
rules.script_hint: My Liverpool online order arrived faulty, so under your terms I'd like a refund or a similar item, plus the 20% bonificación they promise.
rules.source_quote: el plazo para hacer efectiva la garantía es de 90 días naturales contados a partir de la fecha de compra o de la entrega del producto

rules.title: If the maker won't honour its warranty, Liverpool will
rules.window_note: As long as the maker's warranty lasts. The length is printed on the warranty that came with the item. This promise is in Liverpool's terms for things bought on liverpool.com.mx and the Liverpool app, including from outside sellers there.
rules.what_you_get: Liverpool takes over the warranty claim when the maker, importer or seller doesn't honour it or can't. The maker or seller may send a technician to check the item first.
rules.how_to_claim: Start with the maker, using the details on the warranty card. If they don't respond or refuse, contact Liverpool on 55 5262 9999 (phone or WhatsApp) or atencion@liverpool.com.mx, and send your receipt plus photos or other proof of the fault. If Liverpool doesn't sort it out either, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: The maker hasn't honoured the warranty on this [item] I bought from Liverpool, and your terms say Liverpool takes over the warranty when that happens, so here is my receipt and proof of the fault.
rules.source_quote: “Liverpool” se hará cargo de las garantías frente a “Los Clientes”

rules.title: Paid for Liverpool's +Garantía? A new one if the repair takes over 30 days
rules.window_note: Only if you bought +Garantía with the item. It adds 1, 2 or 3 years after the maker's warranty ends, so check the end date on your policy. Items costing $3,000 pesos or less get the replacement plan (1 extra year); items from $3,001 get unlimited repairs for 2 or 3 extra years. Power surges are covered from the first day. Not covered: theft, drops, water, accidents, misuse, cosmetic damage, or repairs done at unauthorised shops.
rules.what_you_get: Unlimited repairs with new parts and no deductible. If a repair takes more than 30 days from the diagnosis, you get a new one, and after the third repair of the same part it's replaced. On the replacement plan you get the same or a similar item, delivered to your home.
rules.how_to_claim: While the maker's own warranty is still running, claim with the maker first; +Garantía takes over when it ends. Then call +Garantía on 55 5322 1955. They book a home visit or collect the item, diagnose it and repair it. For questions, ask at the insurance desk (oficina de seguros) in any Liverpool store. If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: My [item] is covered by a Liverpool +Garantía policy and has stopped working, so I'd like to book a repair, and a new one if it takes more than 30 days as the plan promises.
rules.source_quote: Si la reparación tarda más de 30 días, a partir del diagnóstico técnico del producto. ¡Te entregamos un equipo nuevo!

rules.title: Walmart México online orders: 30 days to send back a faulty item for free
rules.window_note: 30 calendar days from the day you receive it, for orders from walmart.com.mx or the Walmart app. The reasons Walmart lists are a factory defect, it won't turn on, the hardware doesn't work, or you got a different model. Keep the receipt (paper or digital) and the original box. Never returnable: Apple products, headphones and gaming headsets, clothes and shoes, mattresses, motorcycles, SIM and gift cards, and downloads. Misuse, bad installation and personalised items aren't covered. Marketplace items are handled by the seller.
rules.what_you_get: Your money back to how you paid. Walmart says credit cards and PayPal take about 72 business hours and debit cards 3 to 30 business days; cash payments are refunded at any store with photo ID and the receipt.
rules.how_to_claim: Sign in, open the order, choose to return the item and pick the reason, then take it to a store or book a courier pickup. If it arrived broken or incomplete, email photos to devoluciones_mg@wal-mart.com, or the return can be refused. For anything else use the help chat in the app or WhatsApp 55 5134 0054. If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: I received this [item] from walmart.com.mx less than 30 days ago and it has a factory defect, so I'd like to return it free of charge under your 30-day return policy.
rules.source_quote: tienes hasta 30 días naturales posteriores a que recibas el producto para realizar su devolución sin costo alguno

rules.title: Coppel gives up to 2 years of free warranty, handled by Coppel itself
rules.window_note: 24 months, dealt with directly by Coppel, for these Coppel categories: TVs, línea blanca (big appliances), electrodomésticos (small appliances), tools, home and bedroom, mattresses, bicycles, sports, luggage, terrace and garden, office, heating and ventilation, car audio, automotive, and health and wellness. Other things get less: electronics, baby, watches and optical 12 months; air conditioners, heaters, computers, tablets, printers, consoles, e-bikes, Apple and carrier phones 12 months with the maker only; e-scooters 6 months; décor, bedding and toys 3 months, as do used, damaged or 'Rebaja' items. Marketplace sellers set their own.
rules.what_you_get: Coppel handles the fault itself, so you don't have to chase the maker. For an item it collects, Coppel ships you a replacement in good condition if it has one in stock.
rules.how_to_claim: Take the item and your receipt or order confirmation email to any Coppel store. If it was an online-only item, message Coppel on WhatsApp or call +52 559 500 0001, or email atencion@coppel.com, and send clear photos of the damage with a short description. They'll email a prepaid label to print twice: one for the box, one for the courier. If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: This [item] from Coppel broke within 24 months, and your Garantía Coppel covers it for 24 months directly with Coppel, so I'd like it sorted out.
rules.source_quote: Terraza y Jardín, Línea Blanca, Oficina y Papelería, Ventilación y Calefacción, Salud y Bienestar, y Televisiones cuentan con una garantía de 24 meses directamente con Coppel.

rules.title: Coppel electronics, watches and baby gear get 12 months of warranty
rules.window_note: 12 months for Coppel's electronics, baby, jewellery, watch and optical categories, handled by Coppel or by the maker. Watches from Bebé, Folio, Refill, Sahara and York get only 6 months. Zuum and Dreamtech phones also get 12 months, claimed only at Coppel. Computers, tablets, printers, consoles, video games, MP3 players, air conditioners, heaters, e-bikes, motorcycles, Apple products and phones from Telcel, Movistar, Unefon, Iusacell and AT&T get 12 months with the maker only. Coppel's help centre lists phone makers' service numbers.
rules.what_you_get: A repair or replacement for a factory fault, through Coppel or the maker.
rules.how_to_claim: Take it to any Coppel store with your receipt or order email and ask them to process the warranty, or to tell you exactly where to send it. You can also reach Coppel on +52 559 500 0001 (phone or WhatsApp). If they still say no, complain to Profeco, Mexico's consumer agency, on 55 5568 8722 or 800 468 8722, or at a Profeco office.
rules.script_hint: This [item] I bought at Coppel has a factory fault within 12 months, so it's covered by Coppel's 12-month warranty; could you take the claim or tell me exactly where to send it?
rules.source_quote: Para los artículos de las categorías de Bebés, Electrónica, Joyería, Relojería y Óptica tienen una garantía de 12 meses directamente con Coppel o con el proveedor.

rules.title: Coppel swaps furniture, appliances and electronics for free within 30 days
rules.window_note: 30 days from the day you bought it, for what Coppel calls 'Muebles', its non-clothing side, from sofas to TVs. From day 31 Coppel charges a usage fee to swap. Never exchanged: mobile phones, anything Apple, computer accessories, car batteries, air conditioners, amplifiers, car stereos, speakers, heaters, jewellery, watches, motorcycles, SIM chips, airtime and content cards.
